title: Corroborate AGV Active Errors Using AGV Active Error Database Model + Error Code Dictionary + Sort GUID
summary: Use WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to corroborate which AGVs currently have active errors by cross-checking the active-error model (robot code/name, error code, description, SortGuid) against the AGV error dictionary model (error code → description and critical vs non-critical classification). Use SortGuid to identify which sort occurrence the active error is associated with.
when_to_use: When you need to confirm which AGVs currently have active errors and map each active error code to its description/classification, including which sort occurrence (SortGuid) the error is tied to.

steps.title: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the OptiSweep database containing the Robotics / AGV error models
steps.instruction: Using WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), connect to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics / AGV error models.
steps.purpose: Establish access to the OptiSweep database where the AGV error models are stored.
steps.expected_result: SSMS is connected to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics/AGV error model tables.
steps.healthy_condition: You can browse/select the Robotics/AGV model tables needed for the active-error model and the error-code dictionary model.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the Robotics/AGV model tables (connection/database not available or tables not present).

actions.label: Connect to OptiSweep DB in SSMS
actions.exact_action: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics / AGV error models.

steps.title: Open the AGV Active Error Database model table (AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel)
steps.instruction: In SSMS, open the “AGV Active Error Database model table” (AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel).
steps.purpose: Retrieve the currently active AGV errors and their associated fields (robot code/name, error code, description, SortGuid).
steps.expected_result: The AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table view/query results show active error rows with fields including robot code (Name), error code, description, and SortGuid.
steps.healthy_condition: Active error rows are visible and include: Name (robot code), Error code, Description, and SortGuid.
steps.failure_condition: No active error rows are returned, or required fields (Name/Error code/Description/SortGuid) are not present in the results.

actions.label: Open active error model table
actions.exact_action: Open the “AGV Active Error Database model table” (AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel).

steps.title: Verify active error rows include Name, Error code, Description, and SortGuid; record error code and SortGuid for one or more rows
steps.instruction: Verify the table shows active error rows that include robot code (Name), error code (Error code), description (Description), and SortGuid (Sort id). For one or more active error rows, note the error code and SortGuid values.
steps.purpose: Capture the specific active error instances and their sort occurrence identifiers for later corroboration against the error dictionary model.
steps.expected_result: You have at least one active error instance recorded with its Error code and SortGuid (and can see the corresponding Description and robot Name in the same row).
steps.healthy_condition: For each recorded row, the Error code and SortGuid values are populated and the row also shows the Description and robot code (Name).
steps.failure_condition: Rows are missing SortGuid or Error code, or Description does not correspond to the error code shown in the same row.

actions.label: Record active error row fields
actions.exact_action: Verify the table shows active error rows that include: robot code (Name), error code (Error code), description (Description), and SortGuid (Sort id). For one or more active error rows, note the error code and SortGuid values.

steps.title: Open the AGV error model table (error code dictionary) and locate matching error code
steps.instruction: Open the “AGV error model table” (AgvErrorModel / error dictionary) and locate the matching error code to confirm the error description and critical vs non-critical classification.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the active error’s error code maps to the correct description and critical vs non-critical classification in the error dictionary model.
steps.expected_result: The matching error code is found in the AgvErrorModel dictionary and provides the description and critical vs non-critical classification for that error code.
steps.healthy_condition: The dictionary entry for the active error’s Error code shows a description consistent with the active-error row’s Description, and includes critical vs non-critical classification.
steps.failure_condition: The active error’s Error code cannot be found in the AgvErrorModel dictionary, or the dictionary description/classification does not align with the active-error row.
stop_or_escalate_if: If an active error row’s error code cannot be found in the AGV error dictionary table, escalate for data integrity/mapping issues.

actions.label: Lookup error code in dictionary
actions.exact_action: Open the “AGV error model table” (AgvErrorModel / error dictionary) and locate the matching error code to confirm the error description and critical vs non-critical classification.

steps.title: Use SortGuid to identify which sort the error occurred during
steps.instruction: Use the SortGuid value from the active-error row to identify which sort the error occurred during (SortGuid is the identifier for the sort occurrence).
steps.purpose: Tie each active error instance to the specific sort occurrence using SortGuid.
steps.expected_result: For each recorded active error row, you can associate the error instance with the corresponding sort occurrence using its SortGuid value.
steps.healthy_condition: SortGuid values are present in the active-error rows and are used as the sort-occurrence identifier for those errors.
steps.failure_condition: SortGuid is missing/blank in active-error rows, preventing association to a sort occurrence.

actions.label: Associate error to sort occurrence via SortGuid
actions.exact_action: Use the SortGuid value to identify which sort the error occurred during (SortGuid is the identifier for the sort occurrence).

title: Check OptiSweep System State API in Apidog
summary: Use the Apidog / WCS API client on an OptiSweep primary server to perform a read-only check of the GET System State request and determine whether it returns live OptiSweep system data. The source does not define response fields, HTTP status criteria, or response interpretation.
when_to_use: Use Apidog / WCS API client on an OptiSweep primary server when support needs to verify whether the read-only GET System State request can return live OptiSweep system data.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to execute POST System Startup, POST System Shutdown, POST CloseOut, POST Purge, POST ResetMetrics, or other mutating API requests.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for interpreting response fields, because the source does not define those fields or their meanings.
Do not use this procedure for API configuration or endpoint setup; the source does not provide configuration or access details.

steps.title: Open Apidog on the OptiSweep primary server
steps.instruction: On an OptiSweep primary server, open the Apidog / WCS API client and display the OptiSweep API overview.
steps.purpose: Reach the live Apidog / WCS API client used to access OptiSweep API requests.
steps.expected_result: The live Apidog / WCS API client is open and the OptiSweep API overview is visible.
steps.healthy_condition: Apidog is available on the primary server and displays the OptiSweep API catalog.
steps.failure_condition: Apidog cannot be opened, the OptiSweep API catalog is not available, or the primary server cannot be reached.
stop_or_escalate_if: Apidog cannot be opened or the OptiSweep API catalog cannot be reached; escalate to L3 support or the appropriate API/system owner.

actions.label: Open Apidog
actions.exact_action: Open Apidog / WCS API client on the OptiSweep primary server.

steps.title: Select GET System State
steps.instruction: In the live Apidog / WCS API client, open the System API group and select the GET System State request.
steps.purpose: Choose the named read-only System API request for the diagnostic check.
steps.expected_result: The GET System State request is selected in Apidog and ready to send.
steps.healthy_condition: The System group is visible and contains the listed GET System State request.
steps.failure_condition: The System group or GET System State request is not available in Apidog.
stop_or_escalate_if: GET System State is not listed or cannot be selected; escalate to L3 support or the appropriate API/system owner.

actions.label: Select the system-state request
actions.exact_action: Open the System API group and select GET System State.

steps.title: Send the read-only GET System State request
steps.instruction: In Apidog / WCS API client, send only the selected GET System State request. Observe whether the response contains live OptiSweep system data rather than an empty or failed request result. Do not send any POST request.
steps.purpose: Verify whether the live OptiSweep / WCS API returns system data through Apidog.
steps.expected_result: The GET System State request returns content representing live OptiSweep system data. The source does not specify the response fields or their meanings.
steps.healthy_condition: Apidog displays returned system data for the GET System State request.
steps.failure_condition: The request fails, cannot be reached, or returns no data. A specific HTTP status or field-level interpretation is not defined by the source.
stop_or_escalate_if: The GET System State request fails, returns no data, or cannot be reached from Apidog; escalate to L3 support or the appropriate API/system owner.
A POST request is selected or would be executed; stop and return to the read-only GET System State request.

actions.label: Send GET System State
actions.exact_action: Send the read-only GET System State request in Apidog.

actions.label: Inspect the response
actions.exact_action: Observe whether Apidog returns live OptiSweep system data rather than an empty or failed request result.

title: Cancel active exchanges after a manual bag out (purge/close recovery)
summary: After a manual bag out/back out was used because recovery took too long, and the system is back up and running, cancel the active exchanges that were marked by the bag out so operators don’t have to complete the remaining bag out exchange/tote processing.
when_to_use: Use when a manual bag out/back out occurred as a fallback because recovery took too long, and the system is now back up and running; then cancel active exchanges that were marked to exchange by the bag out.
not_for: Do not use if the system is not actually back up and running yet (cancel may not have the intended effect).
Do not use as a generic response to unrelated exchange activity without evidence of a manual bag out/back out event.

steps.title: Confirm manual bag out/back out occurred and the system is back up and running
steps.instruction: Confirm the situation matches a manual bag out/back out fallback (recovery took too long) and that the system is now back up and running before attempting to cancel active exchanges.
steps.purpose: Ensure cancel is only attempted after the system is restored and the exchange activity is specifically tied to a manual bag out/back out event.
steps.expected_result: You have confirmation that (1) the event was a manual bag out/back out due to slow recovery and (2) the system is back up and running.
steps.healthy_condition: System is back up and running (cancel is appropriate once restored).
steps.failure_condition: System is not actually back up and running yet.
stop_or_escalate_if: System is not actually back up and running yet.

actions.label: Confirm bag out/back out fallback and system restored
actions.exact_action: Confirm the situation is a manual bag out/back out that occurred because recovery took too long, and that the system is now back up and running.

steps.title: Locate the cancel function for active exchanges after bag out and identify required request parameters
steps.instruction: On the live API surface (Apidog / API Dog on a primary server), locate the cancel function described for canceling active exchanges after bag out and identify the request parameters needed for the cancel action.
steps.purpose: Prepare the exact API call and parameters needed to cancel the bag-out-marked active exchanges.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the specific cancel endpoint/function in Apidog and the request parameters required to execute it.
steps.healthy_condition: Cancel function and its request parameters are available in Apidog for execution.
steps.failure_condition: Cancel function/parameters cannot be identified (missing endpoint/fields).
stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot identify the cancel request parameters needed for the cancel action.

actions.label: Find cancel endpoint and parameters in Apidog
actions.exact_action: On the live API surface (API Dog on a primary server), locate the cancel function described for canceling active exchanges after bag out, and identify the request parameters needed for the cancel action.

steps.title: Execute the cancel request for bag-out-marked active exchanges
steps.instruction: Using Apidog on the primary server, execute the cancel request for the active exchanges created by the bag out event using the request parameters identified in the previous step.
steps.purpose: Perform the API action that cancels the active exchanges created/marked by the bag out event.
steps.expected_result: The cancel request returns a successful response in Apidog.
steps.healthy_condition: Apidog shows a successful response for the cancel request.
steps.failure_condition: Cancel request does not return a successful response.
stop_or_escalate_if: Cancel request does not return a successful response.

actions.label: Run cancel request in Apidog
actions.exact_action: Execute the cancel request for the active exchanges created by the bag out event, using the request parameters shown in the API Dog documentation/guide.

steps.title: Verify bag-out-marked exchanges are canceled (not remaining active)
steps.instruction: Verify on the live exchange/exchange-request status view that active exchanges marked by the bag out are canceled after the cancel request.
steps.purpose: Confirm the cancel action had the intended effect: bag-out-marked exchange requests no longer require processing.
steps.expected_result: Active exchanges that were marked by the bag out are canceled (i.e., they are no longer active).
steps.healthy_condition: Exchange/exchange-request status shows canceled vs active for the bag-out-marked exchanges.
steps.failure_condition: Exchange requests remain active after the cancel attempt.
stop_or_escalate_if: Exchange requests remain active after the cancel attempt.

actions.label: Check exchange/exchange-request status
actions.exact_action: Verify the observable result: active exchanges that were marked by the bag out are canceled (so the remaining bag out exchange requests do not need to be processed).

steps.title: Stop and escalate if cancel fails or exchanges remain active
steps.instruction: If the cancel request fails or if exchange requests remain active after the cancel attempt, stop and escalate.
steps.purpose: Ensure timely escalation when the cancel action does not succeed or does not produce the expected cancellation outcome.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is triggered when cancel response is not successful or when exchanges remain active.
steps.healthy_condition: Cancel succeeds and exchanges are no longer active.
steps.failure_condition: Cancel request fails or exchanges remain active after cancel.
stop_or_escalate_if: Cancel request does not return a successful response.
Exchange requests remain active after the cancel attempt.
System is not actually back up and running yet.

actions.label: Escalate on failure
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the cancel request does not return a successful response or if exchange requests remain active after the cancel attempt.

title: Check Charging Area Configuration in SSMS / Helix DB
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect charging-area records and confirm that each area has entrance IDs, exit IDs, and an explicit disabled status. This is a read-only diagnostic.
when_to_use: Use when investigating charging-area configuration in the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), including a suspected missing, inconsistent, or disabled charging area.
not_for: Changing charging-area configuration.
Determining charging-threshold behavior; the source identifies charging thresholds as a separate database model.
Replacing a live operational check of AGV or charger behavior.

steps.title: Open the charging database model in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the Robotics database model inventory and locate the charging database model table for charging areas. The source identifies this model as ChargingDatabaseModel; use the available live SSMS navigation rather than modifying the database.
steps.purpose: Locate the live database model that stores separate charging areas.
steps.expected_result: The charging database model is available for inspection and the charging-area records can be viewed.
steps.healthy_condition: The charging database model and its charging-area records are present in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
steps.failure_condition: The charging database model or the relevant charging-area records cannot be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: The charging database model or relevant charging-area records are missing.

actions.label: Locate charging model
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and locate the charging database model table for charging areas.

steps.title: Inspect charging-area fields
steps.instruction: In the charging-area records in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the entrance ID, exit ID, and disabled fields for the relevant charging area.
steps.purpose: Verify that the charging-area record exposes the configuration fields needed for diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: The relevant charging-area row contains values or explicit status entries for entrance ID, exit ID, and disabled status.
steps.healthy_condition: Entrance ID and exit ID are identifiable for the area, and the disabled field explicitly represents the area's status.
steps.failure_condition: Entrance ID or exit ID is empty or inconsistent, or the disabled field is absent or not explicitly represented.
stop_or_escalate_if: Required entrance or exit identifiers are empty or inconsistent.
The disabled status is not explicitly represented.

actions.label: Inspect charging-area fields
actions.exact_action: Inspect the charging-area records for entrance ID, exit ID, and disabled fields.

steps.title: Compare the record with the investigated charging area
steps.instruction: Compare the charging-area row in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) with the charging area being investigated. Confirm that the entrance and exit identifiers are usable for that area and determine whether the disabled status is expected.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the live database configuration corresponds to the charging area under investigation.
steps.expected_result: The relevant row is matched to the investigated charging area, its entrance and exit locations are identifiable, and its disabled status is explicitly understood as expected or unexpected.
steps.healthy_condition: The row matches the charging area under investigation, has usable entrance and exit identifiers, and is not unexpectedly marked disabled.
steps.failure_condition: The row cannot be matched to the investigated area, an identifier is inconsistent with the area, or the area is unexpectedly marked disabled.
stop_or_escalate_if: The charging-area row cannot be matched to the area being investigated.
The area is unexpectedly marked disabled.
The configuration is missing or inconsistent.

actions.label: Compare live configuration
actions.exact_action: Compare the configured charging-area record with the charging area being investigated.

title: Check Charger and Tote-Stand Mapping in SSMS / Helix DB
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect a charging-location record and verify that the individual charger is mapped to the expected station, tote stand, and charging area, with the disabled status appropriate for operation.
when_to_use: Use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when investigating whether a charger is correctly configured for its station, tote stand, and charging area, or whether its disabled status explains an observed charging or mapping issue.
not_for: Do not use this read-only diagnostic to edit charger mappings or change the disabled status.
Do not use this procedure to reassign a charger or perform charger recovery actions.

steps.title: Open the charging-location model in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and locate the charging location database model table. Use the charging-location model rather than the separate charging-area or charging-threshold model when inspecting an individual charger.
steps.purpose: Locate the live database model that contains charger-to-station, tote-stand, charging-area, and disabled-status information.
steps.expected_result: The charging-location database model is available for inspection and provides the record set used to identify individual chargers and their associated station, tote stand, charging area, and disabled status.
steps.healthy_condition: The charging-location model can be opened and its records can be inspected without making changes.
steps.failure_condition: The charging-location model cannot be located or opened, or the available model does not expose the charger mapping information needed for the investigation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the charging-location database model cannot be located or accessed.

actions.label: Open charging-location model
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB in SSMS and locate the charging location database model table.

steps.title: Inspect the charger mapping record in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) charging-location model, find the record for the charger being investigated. Inspect the charger or station identifier, associated tote stand, charging-area association, and disabled field.
steps.purpose: Compare the live charger record with the expected station, tote-stand, and charging-area associations.
steps.expected_result: The investigated charger has a present record with an identifiable charger or station value, an associated tote stand, a charging-area association, and a visible disabled status.
steps.healthy_condition: The charger record contains the expected station identifier, tote-stand association, charging-area association, and disabled status needed to interpret the live mapping.
steps.failure_condition: The charger row is missing, or the station, tote stand, charging-area association, or disabled field is absent, incorrect, or inconsistent with the charger being investigated.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the charger row is missing.
Escalate if a station, tote stand, or charging-area association is absent or incorrect.
Escalate if the disabled field is unexpectedly set.

actions.label: Find charger record
actions.exact_action: Find the record for the charger being investigated.

actions.label: Inspect mapping fields
actions.exact_action: Inspect its charger or station identifier, associated tote stand, charging-area association, and disabled field.

steps.title: Confirm the charger mapping is complete and enabled in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) record, confirm that the charger has a station and tote-stand mapping, belongs to a charging area, and is not unexpectedly disabled.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the live charger configuration is consistent with the expected charging layout.
steps.expected_result: The relevant charging-location row is present with an individual charger, station, tote-stand association, charging-area association, and disabled status. The charger expected to serve the area is mapped completely and is enabled.
steps.healthy_condition: The charger has a station mapping, tote-stand mapping, charging-area association, and an enabled disabled-status value appropriate for the investigated charger.
steps.failure_condition: The charger lacks one of the required mappings or is unexpectedly disabled in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the diagnostic and escalate to engineering if the mapping is incomplete or incorrect.
Stop the diagnostic and escalate if the charger is unexpectedly disabled.
Do not edit the mapping or disabled status from this procedure.

actions.label: Validate complete mapping
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the charger has a station and tote-stand mapping, belongs to a charging area, and is not unexpectedly disabled.

title: Inspect Charging Threshold Values in SSMS / Helix DB
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect the charging threshold database model and relate its configured values to the AGV charging state under investigation. The model stores values used by OptiSweep to determine whether an AGV needs charge, can be released from a charger, or needs emergency charge.
when_to_use: Use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when investigating an AGV charging state and determining whether the configured charging threshold records support the observed charge-required, charger-release, or emergency-charge behavior.
not_for: Do not use this read-only diagnostic to modify charging threshold values.
Do not use this procedure to validate numeric healthy ranges; the source does not provide exact column names or numeric ranges.

steps.title: Open the charging threshold model in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: Open the WCS / Helix DB in SSMS and locate the charging threshold database model table. Distinguish it from the separate charging database model tables for charging areas and individual charging locations.
steps.purpose: Locate the database model that contains the values used by OptiSweep for charging decisions.
steps.expected_result: The charging threshold database model table is located in the WCS / Helix DB and is identifiable as the model containing charging decision variables.
steps.healthy_condition: The charging threshold model is present and can be opened for read-only inspection in SSMS.
steps.failure_condition: The charging threshold model cannot be located or opened, or the available tables cannot be distinguished from the charging-area and charging-location models.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the charging threshold model is missing or inaccessible in the WCS / Helix DB.

actions.label: Locate charging threshold model
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB in SSMS and locate the charging threshold database model table.

steps.title: Inspect the charging decision records
steps.instruction: Inspect the threshold records in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and record the configured values associated with charge required, charger release, and emergency charge decisions. Do not edit the records.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the threshold records contain interpretable values for the three charging decisions described by the source.
steps.expected_result: The charging threshold records are present, readable, and contain values associated with charge-required, charger-release, and emergency-charge decisions.
steps.healthy_condition: Each documented charging decision has a present and interpretable record value.
steps.failure_condition: A documented charging decision has a missing, null, unreadable, or otherwise uninterpretable value.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not modify the threshold records.
Escalate to L3 support or engineering if threshold records are missing, null, or unreadable.

actions.label: Review threshold values
actions.exact_action: Inspect the threshold records and record the configured values associated with charge required, charger release, and emergency charge decisions.

steps.title: Compare threshold records with the AGV charging state
steps.instruction: Compare the relevant values in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) with the AGV charging state under investigation. Verify that the records are present and interpretable for the observed charge-required, charger-release, or emergency-charge behavior.
steps.purpose: Assess whether the available charging threshold records provide a concrete basis for interpreting the AGV behavior under investigation.
steps.expected_result: The threshold records can be related to the observed AGV charging state, or a specific missing, null, unreadable, or inconsistent record is identified for escalation.
steps.healthy_condition: The records are present and interpretable, and they provide a concrete basis for understanding why the application may keep an AGV charging, release it, or request emergency charging.

title: Check Ignition Gateway OPC Connection Status
summary: Use the Ignition gateway web UI to inspect live OPC connection states for tipper tags and compare each displayed status with the associated tipper equipment state.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to verify live OPC connection states serving tipper tags in the Ignition Gateway web UI, especially when a tipper state or tag connection is suspected to be unavailable.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to restart, repair, or recover an OPC connection; the source provides inspection only.
Do not treat a Faulted status as unexpected when the associated tipper is confirmed powered off.

steps.title: Open the Ignition Gateway OPC Connections page
steps.instruction: In the Ignition Gateway web view, navigate to Config > OPC > OPC Connections.
steps.purpose: Navigate to the live Ignition Gateway page that exposes the current OPC connection states.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition Gateway OPC Connections page displays the current OPC connection list and status values.
steps.healthy_condition: The OPC Connections page loads and displays the current connection entries with their statuses.
steps.failure_condition: The OPC Connections page cannot be opened or does not display the current connection list and status values.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Ignition Gateway OPC Connections page cannot be accessed or does not show current connection states.

actions.label: Navigate to OPC Connections
actions.exact_action: Open the Ignition Gateway web view and select Config > OPC > OPC Connections.

steps.title: Inspect the relevant tipper connection statuses
steps.instruction: On the Ignition Gateway Config > OPC > OPC Connections page, locate the relevant tipper OPC connection entries and observe the displayed status for each entry, such as Connected or Faulted.
steps.purpose: Identify the OPC connection entries associated with the relevant tipper tags and record their live displayed states.
steps.expected_result: The relevant tipper connection entries are visible and each has a displayed current status.
steps.healthy_condition: A relevant tipper OPC connection displays Connected.
steps.failure_condition: A relevant tipper OPC connection displays Faulted.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when a relevant tipper connection remains Faulted while the associated tipper should be powered and available.

actions.label: Inspect tipper connection status
actions.exact_action: Locate the relevant tipper OPC connection entries and observe whether each displays Connected or Faulted.

steps.title: Compare the OPC status with the tipper equipment state
steps.instruction: Compare each live status shown in Ignition Gateway Config > OPC > OPC Connections with the associated tipper equipment state. Treat a Faulted status as consistent with the documented example when the corresponding tipper is confirmed powered off.
steps.purpose: Distinguish an expected Faulted display caused by a powered-off tipper from a Faulted display affecting a tipper that should be available.
steps.expected_result: The displayed OPC status is interpreted together with the associated tipper state: Connected is shown for an available connection, while Faulted may be expected when the associated tipper is powered off.
steps.healthy_condition: The displayed status is consistent with the observed equipment state; for example, Tipper 7 and Tipper 8 are powered off and display Faulted.
steps.failure_condition: A relevant tipper connection displays Faulted while the associated tipper is confirmed powered and should be available.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not escalate solely because a tipper connection is Faulted when the corresponding tipper is confirmed powered off.
Escalate when a relevant tipper connection remains Faulted while the associated tipper should be powered and available.

actions.label: Correlate connection and equipment state
actions.exact_action: Compare the Ignition Gateway tipper connection status with the associated tipper equipment state.

The logs can provide timestamps, messages, exception details, trace information, host and instance information, and source code location fields.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to inspect recent WCS / Helix DB log records for Error or Fatal severity during investigation of a system issue.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database records.
Do not use this procedure to run unsupported mutating scripts.
Do not use this procedure as a resolution procedure for an identified error or fatal; escalate when diagnosis or remediation is not covered.

steps.failure_condition: No log records are returned, or the log retrieval action cannot be performed in SSMS.
stop_or_escalate_if: The database log records cannot be queried or retrieved in SSMS.
The available action would modify records or requires unsupported SQL syntax.

title: Check OptiSweep API Status and Fault Responses in Apidog
summary: Use Apidog on a primary server to call documented read-oriented OptiSweep / WCS API requests and verify that the API returns an observable response. Use the returned system-state or AGV fault-summary fields to support troubleshooting. Apidog calls the same API functionality that feeds Ignition and AVEVA.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to verify that the locally hosted OptiSweep / WCS API on a primary server returns system-state or AGV fault data, or when an API response needs to be compared with the live operating condition.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to infer detailed module-to-module request flow, downstream request stacking, or internal request tracing; the source states that this level of tracing is not available.
Do not create new request parameters or build a separate local API project.

steps.instruction: On a primary server, open Apidog / WCS API client and open the shared OptiSweep / WCS API project. Use the project and request parameters already installed on the primary server.
steps.purpose: Access the locally hosted OptiSweep / WCS API requests used for live status and fault diagnostics.
steps.expected_result: The shared project opens and displays documented OptiSweep / WCS API request categories and requests.
steps.healthy_condition: The Apidog project is available and the API list includes read-oriented requests such as Statuses, FaultStats, or System State.
steps.failure_condition: The project is unavailable, the API list cannot be opened, or the locally installed request configuration is missing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Apidog project or configured API requests are not available on the primary server.

actions.label: Open Apidog project

title: Check Windows Service State and Logs When the OptiSweep Gateway Is Unavailable
summary: Use Windows Event Viewer / services to inspect the relevant OptiSweep-related service, determine whether it is running or stopped, review available service or Event Viewer logs for crash or inactive-period evidence, and correlate the service state with gateway availability.
when_to_use: Use this Windows Event Viewer / services diagnostic when the OptiSweep gateway is unavailable, does not open, or does not appear to be running, and a stopped service or service crash is suspected.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to restart a service or change service configuration; the supplied evidence supports inspection only.
Do not use this procedure as a complete recovery procedure when the service state or logs do not explain the gateway outage.

steps.title: Inspect the OptiSweep-related service in Windows Services
steps.instruction: In the Windows Event Viewer / services surface, open Windows Services MMC and inspect the relevant OptiSweep-related service. The source identifies OptiSweep as a service involved in coordinating system operation; it also identifies Ignition and Stunnel as primary services used by the system.
steps.purpose: Identify the relevant OptiSweep-related service and observe its current live service state during the gateway outage.
steps.expected_result: The relevant service entry is visible with an observable status such as Running or a stopped/inactive state.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant OptiSweep-related service is visible and its status is Running.
steps.failure_condition: The relevant service is stopped or inactive, or the service entry cannot be identified from the available Windows Services view.
stop_or_escalate_if: The relevant service is stopped or inactive.
The relevant service cannot be identified from the available Windows Services view.

actions.exact_action: Open Windows Services MMC and inspect the relevant OptiSweep-related service.

steps.title: Record the observed service state
steps.instruction: In Windows Services MMC, record whether the relevant OptiSweep-related service is Running, stopped, or otherwise inactive. Do not restart or reconfigure the service as part of this diagnostic.
steps.purpose: Capture the live service state that can explain whether the gateway outage is associated with an inactive service.
steps.expected_result: The current service state is explicitly identified and can be compared with the reported gateway condition.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service is Running and the gateway is not showing the service-unavailable symptom.
steps.failure_condition: The relevant service is stopped or inactive while the gateway does not open or run.
stop_or_escalate_if: The service is stopped or inactive.
The gateway does not open or run while the service is stopped or inactive.

actions.label: Inspect service status
actions.exact_action: Record whether the relevant service is running or stopped/inactive.

steps.title: Review service and Event Viewer logs
steps.instruction: Use Windows Event Viewer / services to review the available Windows service logs or Event Viewer entries for the relevant service and the reported outage period. Look for observable evidence of a crash, restart, or period in which service activity was absent.
steps.purpose: Determine whether available Windows log evidence shows a service crash, restart, or inactive interval associated with the gateway outage.
steps.expected_result: Available log entries either correlate the outage with a service crash, restart, or inactive interval, or show that the available logs do not explain the outage.
steps.healthy_condition: The logs show continuous or otherwise explainable service activity without a crash or unexplained inactive interval during the gateway-availability check.
steps.failure_condition: The logs show a service crash, restart, or inactive interval corresponding to the gateway outage, or contain no explanatory evidence for the observed outage.
stop_or_escalate_if: A crash, restart, or inactive interval is identified.
The logs do not explain the observed gateway outage.

actions.label: Review Windows logs
actions.exact_action: Review the associated Windows service logs or available Windows Event Viewer entries for evidence of a crash, restart, or inactive interval.

steps.title: Correlate service state with gateway operation
steps.instruction: Confirm the current gateway condition while the relevant service state is known. Compare whether the gateway opens or runs when the service is Running with the reported condition when the service is stopped or inactive. Do not perform a service restart as part of this step.
steps.purpose: Confirm whether the observed service state corresponds to the live gateway-availability symptom.
steps.expected_result: The service state and gateway condition are correlated as either consistent or unexplained.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service is Running and the gateway is operating or opening normally.
steps.failure_condition: The gateway does not open or run while the relevant service is stopped or inactive, or the gateway remains unavailable even though the service is Running.
stop_or_escalate_if: The gateway does not open or run while the service is stopped or inactive.
The gateway remains unavailable while the relevant service is Running.
The service state and available logs do not explain the outage.

actions.label: Check gateway availability
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether the gateway is operating while the service is running.

title: Perform OptiSweep CloseOut Through the WCS API

actions.label: Report RMS availability
actions.exact_action: Communicate that the RMS screen is available so the site or UPS can coordinate the physical master E-stop removal.

title: Diagnose Active AGV Errors in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robotics database to inspect current AGV active-error records and identify the affected robot code, error code, description, and SortGuid. When an error is resolved or an AGV is removed, verify that the record is archived to AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel with available timing fields.
when_to_use: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robotics database when an AGV error must be correlated to the affected robot code, error code, error description, and sort during which the error occurred.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify or delete database records.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or production-stop procedure.

steps.title: Open the Robotics active-error table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the Robotics database and locate the AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table.
steps.purpose: Access the live Robotics database table that stores AGV errors currently present in the system.
steps.expected_result: The AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table is available for read-only inspection and exposes the active-error fields used for correlation.
steps.healthy_condition: The table can be opened and shows active-error records or an empty result set without requiring record changes.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database or AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table cannot be accessed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if L2_support cannot access the Robotics database or the AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table.

actions.label: Open active AGV error table
actions.exact_action: Open the Robotics database and locate the AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table in SSMS.

steps.title: Check for the affected AGV active-error row
steps.instruction: In the AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), check whether a row is present for the affected AGV. Use the Name field as the robot code and inspect ErrorCode, the error description, and SortGuid.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the affected AGV currently has an active error record.
steps.expected_result: The result shows either no active-error row for the affected AGV or a row containing the robot code, error code, error description, and SortGuid.
steps.healthy_condition: The active-error row, when present, has a Name value identifying the affected robot and populated ErrorCode, description, and SortGuid values.
steps.failure_condition: The active record lacks the expected robot code, error code, error description, or SortGuid, or the row cannot be correlated to the affected AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the active record lacks the expected robot code, error code, description, or SortGuid fields.
Escalate when an active-error row cannot be correlated to the reported AGV condition.

actions.label: Inspect active AGV error fields
actions.exact_action: Check whether a row is present for the affected AGV and inspect Name, ErrorCode, the error description, and SortGuid.

steps.title: Capture the active error and sort correlation
steps.instruction: From the active-error row in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), capture the Name robot code, ErrorCode, error description, and SortGuid. For example, the source shows error code 21057 with the description "Front bumper trigger." Use SortGuid as the identifier for the sort during which the error occurred.
steps.purpose: Preserve the live database evidence needed to identify the reported AGV error and the associated sort.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic record contains the affected robot code, active error code, description, and SortGuid, including the sort association when the active row provides it.
steps.healthy_condition: The captured values form a consistent active-error record that can be correlated to the affected AGV and reported condition.
steps.failure_condition: The error description cannot be correlated to the reported condition, or the active row does not provide enough identifying information.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the database diagnostic and escalate when the error description cannot be correlated to the reported condition.
Escalate when the active record is missing the robot code, error code, description, or SortGuid.

actions.label: Capture error evidence
actions.exact_action: Capture Name, ErrorCode, the error description, and SortGuid from the active-error row.

steps.title: Verify resolution in AGV error activity
steps.instruction: After the error is resolved or the AGV is removed, recheck AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and verify that the record is no longer an active-error row. Then inspect AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel for the archived record and available Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time fields.
steps.purpose: Confirm that a resolved or removed AGV error is no longer active and has been archived with available duration information.
steps.expected_result: The resolved or removed error is absent from the active-error table and is present in AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel with Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time when those fields are available.
steps.healthy_condition: The active row is no longer present and the corresponding archived record contains timing fields that show the error interval.
steps.failure_condition: The error remains in AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel after resolution or removal, or no corresponding archived record or expected timing fields are available.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when an active-error row remains for the AGV after the error is reported resolved or the AGV has been removed.
Escalate when the corresponding archived record or expected timing fields cannot be found.

actions.label: Verify active row removal
actions.exact_action: Recheck AgvActiveErrorDatabaseModel and verify that the resolved or removed error is no longer an active-error row.

actions.label: Inspect archived error activity
actions.exact_action: Inspect AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel for Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time when those fields are available.

title: Diagnose Missing Package Dimensions in the Ignition Lane Activity Model
summary: Use the live Ignition gateway's Lane Activity Model in the Sorter Sweeper Database view to determine whether incomplete package dimensions are associated with Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records and whether the condition is concentrated on an auto-induct source. Inspect package identifiers, tracking numbers, dimensional fields, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData.
when_to_use: Use this live Ignition gateway diagnostic when sorter totes are overfilling or package data appears incomplete and support needs to determine whether default dimensions were used, which dimensional attribute is missing, and whether the condition is associated with a particular auto-induct source.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change default dimensions, package classification, or database values.
Do not use this procedure to direct or perform dimensioner reboot or other physical equipment remediation.
Do not treat the observed MissingDimensionData rate as a universal pass/fail threshold; the source provides examples but no universal threshold.

steps.title: Open the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway, open the Sorter Sweeper Database view and select the Ignition Lane Activity Model.
steps.purpose: Open the live sorter data view that records package messages and dimensional information.
steps.expected_result: The live Lane Activity Model displays recent sorter records with package, message, dimensional, cube, and missing-data fields.
steps.healthy_condition: The view loads and exposes recent records with identifiable package or tracking fields and a Message value.
steps.failure_condition: The Lane Activity Model does not load, contains no usable recent records, or does not expose the fields needed for package and dimension inspection.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Ignition gateway view cannot be loaded or the required Lane Activity Model fields are unavailable.

actions.label: Open Lane Activity Model
actions.exact_action: Open the Sorter Sweeper Database view and select the Ignition Lane Activity Model.

steps.title: Review recent Message records in the Ignition gateway
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model, review recent rows and inspect the Message field. Distinguish Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf records.
steps.purpose: Determine which sorter message types are represented in the affected recent records.
steps.expected_result: Recent rows can be categorized by Message value, showing whether the affected package data appears on Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected records have a readable Message value and can be related to a package or tracking identifier.
steps.failure_condition: The Message field is absent, unreadable, or cannot be associated with the affected records.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if affected records cannot be associated with a package ID, tracking number, or message type.

actions.label: Inspect message type
actions.exact_action: Review recent rows and use the Message field to distinguish Scan Data 2, Induct, and SortConf records.

steps.title: Inspect package and dimensional fields in the Ignition gateway
steps.instruction: For the affected records in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model, inspect PackageLid or package ID, PackageUID where displayed, TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData.
steps.purpose: Identify the package record and determine which dimensional values are present or missing.
steps.expected_result: The records show observable package identifiers and dimensional values, including any NULL or missing Length, Width, Height, or Weight values and the associated Cube value.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected record has sufficient package identification and dimensional values to compare the recorded dimensions with MissingDimensionData.
steps.failure_condition: The record cannot be identified, or required dimensional fields are unavailable for comparison.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the table cannot associate affected records with a package ID or tracking number.
Escalate when the displayed dimensional data does not explain the reported sorter behavior.

actions.label: Inspect package attributes
actions.exact_action: Check PackageLid or package ID, TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData.

steps.title: Interpret MissingDimensionData against the live dimensions
steps.instruction: Compare MissingDimensionData with Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube for each affected record in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model. Treat MissingDimensionData=true as an indication that default dimensional values were used, then identify which dimensional field is NULL or otherwise missing.
steps.purpose: Determine whether default dimensions were applied and identify the missing dimensional attribute.
steps.expected_result: The comparison identifies whether defaults were used and shows the missing attribute, such as Weight, Width, or Height, while retaining the observed Cube value.
steps.healthy_condition: MissingDimensionData is not true for the reviewed records, or any true value is explainable by the specific missing attribute shown in the dimensional fields.
steps.failure_condition: MissingDimensionData=true is present across affected records and the associated dimensional fields show missing values that can account for incomplete package data or overfilling.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, especially when the records coincide with tote overfilling.
Do not assign a universal percentage threshold; the source does not define one.

actions.label: Compare missing-data flag
actions.exact_action: Compare the MissingDimensionData value with the dimensional fields and identify NULL or missing dimensional values.

steps.title: Correlate missing dimensions with the auto-induct source
steps.instruction: Use the package ID or related induct identifier in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model to compare affected records from the same source, such as Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2. Review the associated Message and dimensional fields for the grouped records.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the missing-dimension condition is concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.expected_result: The records show whether MissingDimensionData and the missing dimensional attribute are concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected records can be associated with an auto-induct source and do not show a source-specific pattern of missing dimensions.
steps.failure_condition: Records from one auto-induct source consistently show MissingDimensionData=true or repeated missing dimensional fields, such as missing width, height, or weight.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if affected records cluster on one auto-induct source.
Escalate if the table cannot associate affected records with an induct source.

actions.label: Compare auto-induct sources
actions.exact_action: Use the package ID or related induct identifier to compare records from the same auto-induct source, such as Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2.

steps.title: Summarize the observed missing-dimension pattern
steps.instruction: Count or estimate the observed proportion of recent records with MissingDimensionData=true, identify the dominant missing field, record the relevant Message values and auto-induct source, and relate the findings to the reported sorter behavior. Do not apply a threshold that is not defined by the source.
steps.purpose: Produce an evidence-based diagnostic summary for support escalation or site follow-up.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic summary states the observed MissingDimensionData condition, missing dimensional attribute, affected message type, package or tracking examples, associated auto-induct source, and any relationship to tote overfilling.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed records provide a coherent explanation of the package-dimension condition and do not show a broad unexplained pattern.
steps.failure_condition: A substantial or source-specific group of records has MissingDimensionData=true, repeated missing dimensions, or an unexplained relationship to the reported sorter behavior.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2 support or the site support contact if MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, especially when records cluster on one auto-induct source or coincide with tote overfilling.
Escalate when the displayed dimensional data does not explain the reported sorter behavior.

actions.label: Summarize observed pattern
actions.exact_action: Check the observed count or percentage of records with MissingDimensionData and note whether affected records are primarily missing weight, width, or height rather than length.

title: Diagnose AGV Location Dwell in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database to inspect active and completed AGV dwell records. Identify the AGV, station, SortGuid, and elapsed-time evidence associated with a tracked location dwell.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when investigating AGV waiting, idle time, or possible bottlenecks at a tracked hospital, tipper, or other station. Inspect the WCS / Helix Robotics Database in SSMS to determine whether the dwell is currently active or has been archived.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify DwellTracking settings or database records.
Do not use dwell records to identify a specific worker or tipper operator; the available evidence does not provide personnel cycling information.
Do not use this procedure as a complete throughput investigation or to optimize one location without considering system-level throughput.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the Robotics Database and locate the LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity tables.
steps.purpose: Access the WCS / Helix Robotics Database tables used to identify active and completed location dwell.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics Database is selected and the two named dwell tables are available for read-only inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS provides access to the Robotics Database and the dwell tables can be inspected without changing data.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics Database or either named dwell table is unavailable, or the access level would require modification of database records.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3_support if the Robotics Database or named dwell tables cannot be accessed.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

actions.label: Locate dwell tables
actions.exact_action: Locate LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity.

steps.title: Inspect active dwell records
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for active rows at locations marked for DwellTracking. Review the AgvName, Station, and SortGuid fields.
steps.purpose: Determine whether an AGV is currently dwelling at a station configured for DwellTracking.
steps.expected_result: An active dwell row, when present, identifies the AGV in AgvName, the tracked location in Station, and the associated sort in SortGuid.
steps.healthy_condition: The active row contains the displayed identifying fields: AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.
steps.failure_condition: A station expected to use DwellTracking has no active row, or the active row lacks AgvName, Station, or SortGuid needed for interpretation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering if a station expected to use DwellTracking has no corresponding active dwell evidence.
Escalate if the active record lacks the displayed identifying fields needed for interpretation.

actions.label: Inspect active dwell model
actions.exact_action: Inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for locations marked for DwellTracking.

actions.label: Review active identifiers
actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, and SortGuid for the active dwell record.

steps.title: Correlate the active row with the reported AGV station
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the LocationActiveDwellModel Station and AgvName values with the AGV's current location or reported station when that evidence is available through the live support investigation.
steps.purpose: Check whether the active database association agrees with available live AGV location evidence.
steps.expected_result: The active database row associates the AGV named in AgvName with the station named in Station for the current dwell.
steps.healthy_condition: The available AGV location evidence is consistent with the active row's AgvName and Station.
steps.failure_condition: The available AGV location evidence conflicts with the active row, or no current-location evidence is available to perform the comparison.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate for further review if available live AGV location evidence conflicts with the active database row.

actions.label: Compare AGV and station
actions.exact_action: Compare the active row's AgvName and Station with the AGV's current location or reported station when available.

steps.title: Inspect the archived dwell activity
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationDwellActivity for the AGV and station of interest. Review AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.
steps.purpose: Recover the completed dwell interval after the AGV has left the tracked location.
steps.expected_result: A completed activity row contains the AGV, station, and sort identifiers together with Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time. A displayed interval may appear in a format such as 00:00:04.9803282.
steps.healthy_condition: The completed row contains the identifying and timing fields needed to establish the archived dwell interval.
steps.failure_condition: No completed activity is present after the AGV leaves the tracked location, or the row lacks AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, or Total Time.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering if expected completed dwell evidence is missing.
Escalate if the archived record lacks the displayed identifying or timing fields needed for interpretation.

actions.label: Open dwell activity archive
actions.exact_action: Inspect LocationDwellActivity after the AGV leaves the tracked location.

actions.label: Review completed fields
actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

steps.title: Interpret the dwell interval and station
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), use the LocationDwellActivity Station and Total Time values to record the observed dwell interval and determine whether the live record names a hospital, tipper, or another tracked location.
steps.purpose: Use the archived timing and station values to characterize the observed dwell as operational evidence.
steps.expected_result: The recorded result identifies the station named in Station and the elapsed interval shown in Total Time, such as 00:00:04.9803282.
steps.healthy_condition: The station and Total Time are visible and can be associated with the AGV and SortGuid in the same completed record.
steps.failure_condition: The station or Total Time is absent, or the record cannot be associated with an AGV and SortGuid.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not attribute a tipper dwell interval to a specific worker because personnel cycling information is not available in this evidence.

actions.label: Record station and duration
actions.exact_action: Use the displayed Total Time and station values to record the observed dwell interval.

actions.label: Classify the tracked location
actions.exact_action: Identify whether the live Station value names a hospital, tipper, or other tracked location.

title: Diagnose Sorter Location and Queue Mapping in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics database to verify sorted-location rows, associated queue locations, sorter-side associations, and sorter-entry sequence when investigating sorter mapping behavior.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic on the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) when support needs to verify sorter-side, sorted-location, queue-location, or sorter-entry sequence configuration associated with an observed sorter mapping issue.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify Robotics database configuration.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for confirming the physical sorter layout when the database-to-floor relationship is unknown.
Do not use this procedure to diagnose unrelated AGV errors, robot commands, charging, or dwell behavior.

steps.title: Open the Robotics database model in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the Robotics database and locate the SortLocationsDatabaseModel table/model. Do not edit rows or database configuration.
steps.purpose: Establish the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view needed to inspect sorter-location configuration.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics database exposes the sort-location model for read-only inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: The SortLocationsDatabaseModel table/model is available and its rows can be inspected without making changes.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database or SortLocationsDatabaseModel cannot be located or read.
stop_or_escalate_if: The Robotics database or sort locations model is unavailable to the assigned support role.
The investigation would require modifying database configuration.

actions.label: Open Robotics database
actions.exact_action: Open the Robotics database in SSMS and locate the sort locations database model/table.

steps.title: Inspect sorted-location and queue-location rows
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), review the relevant SortLocationsDatabaseModel rows. Inspect the sorted-location identifier and its associated queue-location identifier; where present, use the model fields SorterId, StagingId, and QueueId to distinguish the sorter location, staging location, and queue location.
steps.purpose: Confirm that each relevant sorted location has the expected queue location behind it.
steps.expected_result: The affected sorted locations and their associated queue locations are visible as rows that can be compared with the observed sorter configuration.
steps.healthy_condition: Each required sorted location has a corresponding queue-location association, and the association represents the location behind the sorted location where an empty-tote AGV stages for an exchange.
steps.failure_condition: A required sorted-location row is missing, the QueueId association is absent, or the row does not identify the expected queue location.
stop_or_escalate_if: The required location row is missing.
The queue-location association is absent.
The database row cannot be related to the affected sorter location.

actions.label: Review location associations
actions.exact_action: Review rows for the sorted locations and the associated queue locations behind those sorted locations.

steps.title: Check sorter-side and entrance-queue sequence
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the sorter-side association and Sequence for each relevant row. Compare the recorded sequence with the observed sorter entrance queue order. Sequence values are used to order the locations from the sorter entrance queue; the supplied model reference describes sequence values 1–4 as starting at that entrance queue.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the database maps each location to the intended sorter side and preserves the expected order from the sorter entrance queue.
steps.expected_result: Each relevant location has a sorter-side association and a sequence that can be compared to its expected position from the sorter entrance queue.
steps.healthy_condition: The sorter-side value identifies the intended side, and the sequence progresses consistently with the observed entrance-queue order.
steps.failure_condition: A sorter-side value is missing or unexpected, sequence values do not correspond to the entrance-queue order, or the mapping points to a different location than the observed configuration.
stop_or_escalate_if: Sorter-side and sequence values do not correspond to the observed configuration.
The sequence cannot be reconciled with the sorter entrance queue order.
The observed configuration is insufficient to determine whether the database mapping is correct.

actions.label: Compare sorter-side mapping
actions.exact_action: Check the sorter-side association for each location.

actions.label: Compare sequence order
actions.exact_action: Compare the recorded sequence with the sorter entrance queue order.

steps.title: Confirm complete mapping for the affected sorter side
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), verify that all locations and queue associations needed for the affected sorter side are present and that their sorter-side and Sequence values remain consistent with the observed sorter entrance queue order. Keep the inspection read-only.
steps.purpose: Conclude whether the required sorted locations, queue locations, sorter-side associations, and sequence values form a consistent mapping.
steps.expected_result: The affected sorter side has a complete, internally consistent set of sorted-location and queue-location mappings.
steps.healthy_condition: All required rows are present; each sorted location has its expected queue location; sorter-side associations match the affected side; and sequence values identify the expected entrance-queue order.
steps.failure_condition: Any required row or queue association is missing, or the sorter-side and sequence values conflict with the observed configuration.
stop_or_escalate_if: The required location row is missing.
The queue-location association is absent.
Sorter-side or sequence values do not correspond to the observed configuration.
A database change would be needed to make the mapping consistent.

actions.label: Validate mapping completeness
actions.exact_action: Verify that the locations and queue associations needed for the affected sorter side are present and have a consistent sequence.

title: Exchange a Specific Tote Through the OptiSweep / WCS API (Apidog)
summary: Use the Apidog / WCS API client to open the Totes API, submit POST Exchange Tote with the required ToteName, and review the displayed request outcome.
when_to_use: Use the Apidog / WCS API client when support needs to submit an exchange request for one specific tote identified by its ToteName.
not_for: Do not use POST Exchange Lane when the intent is to exchange one specific tote; Exchange Lane uses a LaneName and exchanges a specific destination.
Do not use this procedure when the required ToteName is unavailable.

steps.title: Open the Totes API in Apidog
steps.instruction: On the primary server, open Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client and open the Totes API area.
steps.purpose: Reach the live OptiSweep / WCS API surface containing the tote exchange request.
steps.expected_result: The Totes API area is displayed and includes the POST Exchange Tote request.
steps.healthy_condition: The POST Exchange Tote request is available in the Totes API area.
steps.failure_condition: The Totes API area or POST Exchange Tote request is unavailable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the OptiSweep / WCS API client or Totes API area is unavailable.
Escalate if the POST Exchange Tote request is not available after confirming access to the primary server.

actions.label: Open Totes API
actions.exact_action: Open the Totes API area in Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client.

steps.title: Enter the required ToteName
steps.instruction: Open POST Exchange Tote in the Apidog / WCS API client and enter the required ToteName.
steps.purpose: Identify the individual tote that the exchange request will target.
steps.expected_result: The POST Exchange Tote request contains the intended ToteName.
steps.healthy_condition: The ToteName field is populated with the confirmed name of the specific tote to exchange.
steps.failure_condition: The ToteName is unavailable, blank, or does not identify the intended tote.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the required ToteName is unavailable.
Stop and confirm the target before submitting if the ToteName does not identify the intended specific tote.

actions.label: Open exchange request
actions.exact_action: Open POST Exchange Tote.

actions.label: Enter ToteName
actions.exact_action: Enter the required ToteName.

steps.title: Submit the exchange request and review the API outcome
steps.instruction: Submit POST Exchange Tote in the Apidog / WCS API client and review the resulting request outcome displayed by the OptiSweep / WCS API.
steps.purpose: Send the specific-tote exchange request and capture the observable result presented by the live API client.
steps.expected_result: The API displays an outcome for the submitted POST Exchange Tote request.
steps.healthy_condition: The request is accepted by the API and the displayed outcome indicates that the named tote exchange request was processed. The source packet does not define a specific success response or HTTP response code.
steps.failure_condition: The API rejects the request or does not provide a request outcome.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the API rejects the request.
Escalate to L3_support if the request is rejected after a valid ToteName is supplied.
Escalate if the API does not display a resulting request outcome.

actions.label: Submit request
actions.exact_action: Submit POST Exchange Tote.

actions.label: Review request outcome
actions.exact_action: Verify that the API displays the resulting request outcome.

title: Retrieve Current AGV Fault Statistics From the WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent approved API client to retrieve current AGV fault statistics. Treat sort goods information as historical rather than as the current fault result.
when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog when a live diagnostic result for current AGV fault statistics is required.
not_for: Do not use historical sort information as a substitute for the current AGV fault statistics.
Do not use this procedure to assign fault severity or prescribe corrective actions; the source does not define fault meanings or corrective actions.

steps.title: Locate GetAgvFaultStats in the OptiSweep / WCS API client
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent approved API client, open the OptiSweep / WCS API and locate GET GetAgvFaultStats in the System API list.
steps.purpose: Select the API operation that retrieves current AGV fault statistics.
steps.expected_result: GET GetAgvFaultStats is visible and selected as the request to inspect current AGV fault statistics.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep / WCS API client displays GET GetAgvFaultStats in the System API list.
steps.failure_condition: GET GetAgvFaultStats is not available or the OptiSweep / WCS API cannot be opened in the approved API client.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the OptiSweep / WCS API cannot be opened.
Escalate if GET GetAgvFaultStats is not present in the System API list.

actions.label: Open the API client
actions.exact_action: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or an equivalent approved API client.

actions.label: Locate the request
actions.exact_action: Locate GET GetAgvFaultStats in the System API list.

steps.title: Execute GET GetAgvFaultStats
steps.instruction: With GET GetAgvFaultStats selected in Apidog or the approved WCS API client, execute the GET request.
steps.purpose: Request the current AGV fault statistics from the OptiSweep / WCS API.
steps.expected_result: The OptiSweep / WCS API returns a response containing the current AGV fault statistics.
steps.healthy_condition: The GET request completes and returns current AGV fault statistics.
steps.failure_condition: The request fails or returns no current AGV fault statistics.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the GET request fails.
Escalate if the response does not contain current AGV fault statistics.

actions.label: Execute the API request
actions.exact_action: Execute GET GetAgvFaultStats.

steps.title: Verify that the response is current AGV fault information
steps.instruction: Review the returned result in the OptiSweep / WCS API client and identify it as the current AGV fault statistics. Do not substitute sort goods or other historical sort information for this result.
steps.purpose: Ensure the diagnostic result is the current AGV fault result rather than historical sort information.
