title: Look Up an AGV Error Code and Severity Classification
summary: Use read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) access to compare an observed AGV ErrorCode with the Robotics database AGV error reference and active AGV error record. Read the stored description and critical or non-critical classification when available.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when an AGV error code needs to be interpreted in the Robotics database through WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), including comparison with an active AGV error record.
not_for: Do not use the Robotics database lookup to infer RMS error-code mappings; the source indicates that the RMS/API relationship is uncertain.
Do not modify the AGV error lookup table.

steps.title: Open the Robotics database in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the Robotics database and locate the AGV Error model table. Use read-only access.
steps.purpose: Access the Robotics database and locate the AGV error reference used for code and description lookup.
steps.expected_result: The AGV Error model table is available for inspection in the Robotics database.
steps.healthy_condition: The Robotics database and AGV Error model table can be opened without modifying data.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database or AGV Error model table is unavailable, or the available access would permit or require modifying the lookup table.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Robotics database or AGV Error model table cannot be located.
Stop if the procedure would require modifying the lookup table.

actions.label: Locate AGV error reference
actions.exact_action: Open the Robotics database and locate the AGV Error model table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

steps.title: Find the observed ErrorCode and read its description
steps.instruction: In the AGV Error model table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), find the row matching the observed ErrorCode and read the stored error description. The source example shows ErrorCode 21057 with the description "Front bumper trigger."
steps.purpose: Match the observed AGV error code to the stored reference description.
steps.expected_result: A matching row returns the observed ErrorCode and its stored description.
steps.healthy_condition: The ErrorCode matches a row whose description is readable and corresponds to the observed AGV error.
steps.failure_condition: No row matches the observed ErrorCode, or the returned description does not correspond to the active AGV error record.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the observed ErrorCode has no matching AGV Error model row.
Escalate when the returned description conflicts with the active AGV error record.

actions.label: Inspect error-code row
actions.exact_action: Find the row for the observed ErrorCode and read its error description in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

steps.title: Read the critical or non-critical classification
steps.instruction: In the AGV Error model table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the row or field that classifies the observed error as critical or non-critical.
steps.purpose: Determine the documented severity classification associated with the error reference row.
steps.expected_result: The matching AGV error reference provides an observable critical or non-critical classification.
steps.healthy_condition: A critical or non-critical classification is present for the matching ErrorCode.
steps.failure_condition: The matching row does not expose a critical or non-critical classification, or the classification cannot be associated with the observed ErrorCode.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the matching error row has no observable critical or non-critical classification.

actions.label: Inspect severity classification
actions.exact_action: Check the AGV error table's critical or non-critical classification in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

steps.title: Compare the reference row with the active AGV error record
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the reference ErrorCode and description with the active AGV error record. The active record includes the robot code in Name, ErrorCode, Description, and SortGuid, which identifies the sort during which the error occurred.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the reference description and code agree with the currently active AGV error.
steps.expected_result: The active AGV error record contains an ErrorCode and Description consistent with the reference lookup; the active record's Name and SortGuid identify the robot and associated sort when present.
steps.healthy_condition: The active record's ErrorCode and Description agree with the AGV Error model lookup, and the active record can be associated with the relevant robot through Name.
steps.failure_condition: The active record's ErrorCode or Description conflicts with the reference row, or no active record is available for comparison when one is expected.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the reference description conflicts with the active-error record.
Do not infer an RMS/API mapping from a discrepancy; the source indicates that this relationship is uncertain.

actions.label: Compare active error fields
actions.exact_action: Compare the reference ErrorCode and description with the active AGV error record in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

title: Check OPC COM tag subscription updates flowing to Sorter Sweeper (Ignition tag provider → OPC server → Sorter Sweeper processing)
summary: Verify that OPC COM is actively subscribing to tags and that tag updates are being written to the OPC server and forwarded to the Sorter Sweeper module for processing by checking live WCS/Helix DB (SSMS) tables/models for OPC COM activity and correlating it to Sorter Sweeper processing records; also confirm Ignition gateway health when needed.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm the live tag flow: OPC COM subscribes to tags, tag updates are written via the OPC server/ignition tag provider, and Sorter Sweeper receives/acts on those updates.

steps.title: Open WCS/Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the live OptiSweep/WCS database catalog
steps.instruction: Using SSMS / Helix DB (wcs_sql), connect to the live OptiSweep/WCS database catalog that includes the OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper modules.
steps.purpose: Establish a live view of the OptiSweep/WCS databases that include OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper data needed for correlation.
steps.expected_result: SSMS connection is established and you can browse the live database objects for the OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper modules.
steps.healthy_condition: You can access the live database objects needed to query OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper-related models/tables.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect to the live database or cannot access the relevant module databases/objects.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot connect to the live WCS/Helix DB, stop and escalate (database access/connectivity issue).

actions.label: Connect to live WCS/Helix DB
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS / Helix DB (wcs_sql) and connect to the live OptiSweep/WCS database catalog that includes the OPCComms and SorterSweeper modules.

steps.title: Locate live OPC COM communications and Sorter Sweeper processing models/tables
steps.instruction: In SSMS / Helix DB (wcs_sql), locate the live tables/models for OPC COM communications and for Sorter Sweeper processing.
steps.purpose: Identify the specific live objects that represent OPC COM tag subscription/update activity and Sorter Sweeper processing so you can correlate them by timeframe/tag identity.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the live OPC COM communications objects and the live Sorter Sweeper processing objects that will be used for correlation.
steps.healthy_condition: The identified objects correspond to OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper databases/models used for tag subscription/update and processing.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot identify the correct live objects for OPC COM communications and Sorter Sweeper processing (no clear mapping to the live schema).
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot locate the correct live OPC Comms and Sorter Sweeper objects, stop and escalate (schema mapping gap).

actions.label: Locate module objects
actions.exact_action: Locate the live tables/models for OPC COM communications (opc_comms) and Sorter Sweeper processing (sorter_sweeper).

steps.title: Check for recent OPC COM tag update activity in OPC COM communications objects
steps.instruction: Using the OPC COM communications objects you identified in SSMS / Helix DB (wcs_sql), check for recent tag update activity (e.g., recently updated records/timestamps) for the relevant subscribed tags.
steps.purpose: Confirm that OPC COM is actively receiving/subscribing to tag updates and that updates are being written to the OPC server (observable as recent update activity in OPC COM-related records).
steps.expected_result: There are recent records showing tag update activity (updated timestamps/entries) in the OPC COM communications objects.
steps.healthy_condition: OPC COM shows continuous/recent tag update activity (recent rows/records with updated timestamps for relevant tags).
steps.failure_condition: No recent tag update activity is present in OPC COM communications objects.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if OPC COM shows no recent tag updates (possible OPC server connectivity/subscription issue).

actions.label: Verify recent tag updates
actions.exact_action: Check for recent tag update activity in the OPC COM tables/models (evidence of tag updates being written to the OPC server).

steps.title: Correlate OPC COM tag updates to Sorter Sweeper processing records
steps.instruction: In SSMS / Helix DB (wcs_sql), correlate the timeframe of the recent OPC COM tag update activity to Sorter Sweeper processing records; if available, match tag identifiers between the two.
steps.purpose: Confirm that tag updates observed in OPC COM are actually being forwarded/processed by Sorter Sweeper (not just received by OPC COM).
steps.expected_result: Sorter Sweeper has corresponding processing entries for the same tag update timeframe (and, if available, matching tag identifiers).
steps.healthy_condition: For recent OPC COM updates, Sorter Sweeper shows corresponding processing entries in the same timeframe.
steps.failure_condition: OPC COM updates exist, but there are no corresponding Sorter Sweeper processing records for that timeframe.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if OPC COM updates exist but there are no corresponding Sorter Sweeper processing records.

actions.label: Timeframe correlation
actions.exact_action: Correlate those tag updates to Sorter Sweeper processing records.

steps.title: If applicable, verify Ignition gateway health for tag provider connectivity
steps.instruction: Using Ignition gateway (ignition_gateway), perform a basic health check to confirm the gateway is not in a failed/unreachable state.
steps.purpose: Ensure the Ignition gateway is not in a failed/unreachable state that would prevent tag updates from being provided to the OPC COM/OPC server path.
steps.expected_result: Ignition gateway status indicates it is reachable/healthy enough to provide tag updates.
steps.healthy_condition: Ignition gateway is not in a failed/unreachable state; performance indicators do not show obvious crash behavior (e.g., memory spiked then dropped to 0).
steps.failure_condition: Ignition gateway appears failed/unreachable or shows obvious crash/performance failure behavior.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if Ignition gateway health indicates it is failed/unreachable (tag provider connectivity issue).

actions.label: Check gateway performance/health
actions.exact_action: Use the Ignition gateway performance page as a support view for memory/performance behavior.

steps.title: Stop and escalate based on correlation results
steps.instruction: Based on your findings from Steps 3–4, stop and escalate using the failure mode that matches the observed evidence.
steps.purpose: Ensure fast routing when the tag flow is broken at either the OPC COM subscription/update stage or the Sorter Sweeper processing stage.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is triggered only when the evidence indicates missing tag updates or missing Sorter Sweeper processing correlation.
steps.healthy_condition: OPC COM shows recent tag updates and Sorter Sweeper shows corresponding processing entries for the same timeframe.
steps.failure_condition: Either OPC COM has no recent tag updates, or OPC COM updates exist but Sorter Sweeper has no corresponding processing records.
stop_or_escalate_if: OPC COM shows no recent tag updates (possible OPC server connectivity/subscription issue).
OPC COM updates exist but there are no corresponding Sorter Sweeper processing records (possible Sorter Sweeper subscription/processing failure).

actions.label: Escalate with failure mode
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if OPC COM tag updates are not present or if OPC COM updates exist but there are no corresponding Sorter Sweeper processing records.

title: Remove a Tote via the OptiSweep / WCS API After AGV Removal
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client to remove a tote by submitting POST RemoveTote with the required ToteId. The associated AGV must be removed before the tote-removal request is submitted.
when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API when a tote must be removed from the system and the associated AGV has already been removed.
not_for: Do not use POST RemoveTote while the associated AGV remains in the system.
Do not use this procedure to remove the AGV; the source identifies RemoveAgv separately but does not define the complete AGV-removal procedure or its verification response.

steps.title: Verify the associated AGV removal state in the OptiSweep / WCS API
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, review the AGVs API area and the available AGV status or removal information for the AGV associated with the tote. Proceed only when the associated AGV has been removed from the system.
steps.purpose: Ensure the prerequisite for tote removal is satisfied before changing tote state.
steps.expected_result: The associated AGV is confirmed as removed before any POST RemoveTote request is submitted.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV is no longer present as an associated AGV in the available OptiSweep / WCS API state.
steps.failure_condition: The AGV remains in the system, or the available API state does not provide enough information to confirm that it has been removed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The associated AGV remains in the system.
The AGV cannot be removed first.

title: Inspect Robot Location Attributes in the Robotics Database
summary: A read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic for inspecting Robot Location records in the OptiSweep Robotics database and comparing the record with the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI location cue. Review station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when L2/L3 support needs to interpret a station or location in the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and associate it with a location shown in the RMS / fleet status UI.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify Robotics database records.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for a live database query or RMS location comparison; the packet does not provide a complete SSMS navigation path or SQL query.

steps.title: Open the Robotics database in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the OptiSweep Robotics database. Use read-only inspection and do not edit or execute changes against database records.
steps.purpose: Establish a read-only view of the OptiSweep Robotics database that contains the Robot Location model/table.
steps.expected_result: The OptiSweep Robotics database is selected and available for inspection in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
steps.healthy_condition: The Robotics database is accessible and its database objects can be inspected without making changes.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database is unavailable, inaccessible, or cannot be inspected read-only.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the database cannot be accessed read-only.
Escalate to L3_support if the Robotics database is unavailable or access cannot be established.

actions.label: Select Robotics database
actions.exact_action: Select the OptiSweep Robotics database in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

steps.title: Locate the Robot Location record
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), locate the Robot Location database model/table and inspect the record for the relevant station or location. Use the available station or location identity to select the record; do not infer an unprovided table path or SQL query.
steps.purpose: Find the live location record corresponding to the station or location under investigation.
steps.expected_result: A Robot Location record corresponding to the investigated station or location is present and readable.
steps.healthy_condition: The record has an identifiable station or location identity that can be used for comparison with RMS.
steps.failure_condition: No relevant Robot Location record can be found, or the record lacks enough identifying information to associate it with the investigated location.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the expected Robot Location record is missing.
Escalate if the record cannot be associated with the investigated location.

actions.label: Inspect Robot Location record
actions.exact_action: Locate the Robot Location database model/table and inspect the record for the relevant station or location.

steps.title: Inspect Robot Location attributes
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the Robot Location record fields for station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
steps.purpose: Determine the live configuration and state attributes associated with the investigated location.
steps.expected_result: The live Robot Location record exposes readable values for station or location identity, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking.
steps.healthy_condition: The expected fields are populated and internally usable for identifying the location and interpreting its live occupancy, zone, type, capacity, and dwell-tracking configuration.
steps.failure_condition: One or more identifying or operational fields are blank, inconsistent, or unavailable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if identifying fields are blank or inconsistent.
Do not modify the record to correct a value during this diagnostic.

actions.label: Review location fields
actions.exact_action: Check the station number, occupied state, zone, closeout zone, location type, maximum number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking field.

steps.title: Compare the record with the RMS location cue
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI, locate the corresponding orange location or workstation ID and compare that live location cue with the station or location identity from the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robot Location record. Use the RMS location cue for association; do not assume that color alone proves a field value.
steps.purpose: Corroborate the database location identity against the live RMS / fleet status UI representation.
steps.expected_result: The Robot Location record can be associated with the corresponding RMS / fleet status UI location cue, including an orange location or visible workstation ID when present.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS / fleet status UI location cue and the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) record identify the same station or location.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS / fleet status UI cue cannot be matched to the database record, or the identifying values conflict.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the database record cannot be associated with the RMS location.
Escalate if the RMS cue and database identifying fields are inconsistent.

actions.label: Compare RMS location
actions.exact_action: Compare the live record with the location being investigated in RMS, using orange locations and workstation IDs as visible location cues.

title: Verify Shutdown Staging Mapping for AGVs With Tote vs Without Tote Using the ShutDownStaging Table
summary: Use SSMS/Helix DB (WCS) to validate that the ShutDownStaging table maps shutdown destinations correctly based on whether an AGV has a tote (tote=true) versus no tote (tote=false), including the expected use of ShutdownOffTheEndId and center queue staging for tote-carrying AGVs, and the expected sorter-location/nearest-open-available shutdown queue behavior for non-tote AGVs. Also confirm that the ShutDownStaging Sequence values align with the zone/entrance sequence behavior used to select the correct shutdown queue destination.
when_to_use: When you need to troubleshoot or confirm that AGVs stage correctly during shutdown, specifically validating that tote-carrying AGVs and non-tote AGVs are routed to the correct shutdown staging destinations per the ShutDownStaging table mapping rules (including off-the-end queue vs nearest open available shutdown queue behavior) and that Sequence mapping is consistent.

steps.title: Open SSMS / Helix DB (WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)) and connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database
steps.instruction: Using SSMS / Helix DB (WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)) (surface: wcs_sql), connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the shutdown staging model table.
steps.purpose: Access the WCS database where the ShutDownStaging model/table is stored so you can validate tote vs non-tote shutdown staging mappings.
steps.expected_result: You are connected in SSMS/Helix DB to the OptiSweep/WCS database and can browse/query the database schema/models.
steps.healthy_condition: The database connection is successful and the schema is accessible for locating the ShutDownStaging model/table.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database or cannot access the schema needed to locate the ShutDownStaging model/table.

actions.label: Connect to WCS DB in SSMS/Helix
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS / Helix DB (WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)) and connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the shutdown staging model table.

steps.title: Locate the ShutDownStaging model/table in the WCS database
steps.instruction: In the WCS database schema, locate the shutdown staging database model/table named ShutDownStaging (or the exact table/model name used in the database schema).
steps.purpose: Find the exact ShutDownStaging model/table so you can inspect the tote vs non-tote mapping fields and Sequence behavior.
steps.expected_result: You identify the ShutDownStaging table/model and can view its relevant fields/columns (including WithTote, ShutDownOffTheEndid, ShutDownQueueld, Sequence, and SorterSideDatabaseModelid as shown in the referenced model frame).
steps.healthy_condition: The ShutDownStaging model/table is present and exposes the expected mapping fields used for tote vs non-tote staging.
steps.failure_condition: The ShutDownStaging model/table cannot be found, or the expected mapping fields are not present/visible in the schema.

actions.label: Find ShutDownStaging model/table
actions.exact_action: Locate the shutdown staging database model/table named ShutDownStaging (or the exact table/model name used in the database schema).

steps.title: Validate tote=true rows map to ShutdownOffTheEndid and center queue staging (ShutdownQueueld)
steps.instruction: In ShutDownStaging, review rows where WithTote / tote=true and confirm they map to a shutdown off-the-end queue destination (ShutdownOffTheEndid) and a center queue staging destination (ShutdownQueueld / center queue staging fields as shown in the table).
steps.purpose: Confirm that AGVs carrying a tote (tote=true) are mapped to the expected shutdown off-the-end queue destination and center queue staging destination.
steps.expected_result: For tote=true rows, ShutdownOffTheEndid is populated with an off-the-end queue destination and ShutdownQueueld is populated with the center queue staging destination.
steps.healthy_condition: tote=true rows include mappings for both ShutdownOffTheEndid (off-the-end queue) and ShutdownQueueld (center queue staging).
steps.failure_condition: tote=true rows are missing ShutdownOffTheEndid mappings (off-the-end queue destination not mapped) or missing center queue staging mappings (ShutdownQueueld not mapped).
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the table shows tote=true rows missing ShutdownOffTheEndid mappings.

actions.label: Check tote=true mappings
actions.exact_action: Review rows that correspond to AGVs with tote (tote=true) and confirm they map to a shutdown off-the-end queue destination (ShutdownOffTheEndid) and a center queue staging destination (ShutdownQueueld / center queue staging fields as shown in the table).

steps.title: Validate tote=false rows map to sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior
steps.instruction: In ShutDownStaging, review rows where WithTote / tote=false and confirm they map to sorter locations (i.e., the destination is mapped to sorter locations rather than the shutdown off-the-end queue path).
steps.purpose: Confirm that AGVs without a tote (tote=false) are mapped to sorter locations rather than the off-the-end queue path, matching the expected nearest open available shutdown queue behavior.
steps.expected_result: For tote=false rows, the mapped destination corresponds to sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior rather than the off-the-end queue path used for tote=true.
steps.healthy_condition: tote=false rows are not routed through the off-the-end queue destination path; they map to sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior.
steps.failure_condition: tote=false rows are mapped to the off-the-end queue path instead of sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if tote=false rows are mapped to the off-the-end queue path instead of sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior.

actions.label: Check tote=false mappings
actions.exact_action: Review rows that correspond to AGVs without tote (tote=false) and confirm they map to sorter locations (i.e., the destination is mapped to sorter locations rather than the shutdown off-the-end queue path).

steps.title: Check Sequence behavior aligns with zone/entrance sequence selection of shutdown queue destination
steps.instruction: In ShutDownStaging, check that the table uses a sequence value (Sequence / sequence #) that matches the AGV’s zone/entrance sequence so the system can select the correct shutdown queue destination.
steps.purpose: Ensure the ShutDownStaging Sequence values are consistent so the system can select the correct shutdown queue destination for a given zone/entrance sequence.
steps.expected_result: Sequence values in ShutDownStaging are present and consistent such that a given zone/entrance sequence selects the corresponding shutdown queue destination.
steps.healthy_condition: Sequence values are populated and align with the described 'zone/sequence selects shutdown queue destination' behavior.
steps.failure_condition: Sequence values are missing or inconsistent such that zone/sequence cannot reliably select the correct shutdown queue destination.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if sequence values do not align with the described “zone/sequence selects shutdown queue destination” behavior (e.g., sequence rows are missing or inconsistent).

actions.label: Verify Sequence mapping
actions.exact_action: Check the sequence behavior: confirm that the table uses a sequence value (sequence #) that matches the AGV’s zone/entrance sequence so the system can select the correct shutdown queue destination for that sequence.

steps.title: Stop and escalate on mapping or sequence inconsistencies
steps.instruction: If any of the validation checks fail (tote=true missing ShutdownOffTheEndid, tote=false routed to off-the-end queue path, or Sequence behavior inconsistent), stop further analysis and escalate.
steps.purpose: Ensure incorrect shutdown staging mappings are promptly escalated when they violate the expected tote vs non-tote routing rules or sequence behavior.
steps.expected_result: A clear escalation decision is made based on the specific failing condition(s).
steps.healthy_condition: All checks pass: tote=true rows include ShutdownOffTheEndid and center queue staging; tote=false rows map to sorter locations/nearest open available shutdown queue behavior; Sequence values align with zone/entrance selection behavior.
steps.failure_condition: Any of the specified mapping/sequence failures are present.
stop_or_escalate_if: tote=true rows missing ShutdownOffTheEndid mappings
tote=false rows mapped to off-the-end queue path instead of sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior
Sequence values do not align with zone/sequence selects shutdown queue destination behavior (missing or inconsistent sequence rows)

actions.label: Escalate mapping/sequence issue
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the table shows tote=true rows missing ShutdownOffTheEndid mappings, or if tote=false rows are mapped to the off-the-end queue path instead of sorter locations / nearest open available shutdown queue behavior.

title: Shut Down OptiSweep System Through the WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client to confirm that the system is in the running state, execute POST System Shutdown, and verify that GET System State reports shutdown.
when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API when an authorized L2 or L3 support user needs to shut down the OptiSweep system from its live running state and verify the resulting system state.
not_for: Do not use POST System Shutdown unless GET System State confirms that the system is running.
Do not use this procedure as a physical emergency stop or a substitute for site safety actions.
Do not use this procedure when the API request cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result; escalate instead.

steps.title: Open the System Shutdown request in the WCS API client
steps.instruction: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or an equivalent approved API client and locate POST System Shutdown in the System API list.
steps.purpose: Locate the live shutdown operation before checking or changing system state.
steps.expected_result: The POST System Shutdown request is available in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.healthy_condition: The System API list contains POST System Shutdown and GET System State.
steps.failure_condition: The API client cannot be opened, the System API list is unavailable, or POST System Shutdown cannot be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the API request cannot be executed or POST System Shutdown is not available.

actions.label: Locate System Shutdown
actions.exact_action: Locate POST System Shutdown in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.

steps.title: Verify the current state through the WCS API
steps.instruction: In the OptiSweep / WCS API client, execute GET System State and inspect the returned current system state. Continue only when the returned state is running.
steps.purpose: Ensure the shutdown operation is being applied from the supported running state.
steps.expected_result: GET System State returns the current system state as running.
steps.healthy_condition: The live WCS API response identifies the system state as running.
steps.failure_condition: The returned state is not running, the request fails, or the response is unrecognized.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if GET System State does not report running.
Escalate if GET System State cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result.

actions.label: Get current system state
actions.exact_action: Execute GET System State and confirm that the returned state is running.

steps.title: Execute System Shutdown and query state again
steps.instruction: In the OptiSweep / WCS API client, execute POST System Shutdown. After the request completes, execute GET System State again.
steps.purpose: Issue the supported WCS API shutdown operation and obtain a live post-operation state.
steps.expected_result: The shutdown request completes and a subsequent GET System State response is available for verification.
steps.healthy_condition: POST System Shutdown can be executed while the pre-request state is running, and GET System State returns a recognized state.
steps.failure_condition: The POST request cannot be executed, returns an unrecognized result, or no subsequent system-state response is available.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the API request cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result.

actions.label: Request system shutdown
actions.exact_action: Execute POST System Shutdown.

actions.label: Recheck system state
actions.exact_action: Execute GET System State again after the shutdown request.

steps.title: Confirm the shutdown state
steps.instruction: Inspect the state returned by the post-request GET System State call and compare it with the documented shutdown state.
steps.purpose: Verify that the live system state changed to the documented shutdown state.
steps.expected_result: The post-request GET System State response reports shutdown.
steps.healthy_condition: The live WCS API state is shutdown after POST System Shutdown.
steps.failure_condition: The live WCS API state does not change to shutdown or the returned state is unrecognized.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the system state does not change to shutdown after the shutdown request.
Escalate if the returned state is unrecognized.

actions.label: Verify shutdown state
actions.exact_action: Compare the returned state with the shutdown state.

title: Check SorterSide Entrance, Exit, Tipper Count, and Disabled State in SSMS
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface to perform a read-only inspection of the OptiSweep Robotics SorterSideDatabaseModel. Verify the live sorter-side Name, EntranceId, ExitId, TipperCount, and Disabled fields against the available sorter-side configuration examples.
when_to_use: Use this read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when validating sorter-side queue mappings, the number of associated tippers, or whether a sorter side is disabled.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change TipperCount, EntranceId, ExitId, or Disabled values.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for confirming whether a disabled sorter side is intentionally excluded from the current rollout phase.
Do not use this procedure for live sorter control, tote exchange, or AGV commands.

steps.title: Open the OptiSweep Robotics database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface, open SSMS and select the OptiSweep Robotics database.
steps.purpose: Establish a read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view of the Robotics database that contains the sorter-side model.
steps.expected_result: The OptiSweep Robotics database is selected and available for inspection in SSMS.
steps.healthy_condition: The Robotics database can be opened for read-only inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database is unavailable or the required read-only access cannot be established.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the OptiSweep Robotics database cannot be accessed.

actions.label: Open SSMS
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the OptiSweep Robotics database.

steps.title: Locate SorterSideDatabaseModel in the Robotics database
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface, locate the SorterSideDatabaseModel table or model in the OptiSweep Robotics database.
steps.purpose: Open the sorter-side model that contains the queue mapping, tipper count, and disabled-state fields.
steps.expected_result: The SorterSideDatabaseModel is available for inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: The model or table can be opened and exposes sorter-side records.
steps.failure_condition: The SorterSideDatabaseModel cannot be located or opened.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the model or table is missing from the Robotics database.

actions.label: Locate sorter-side model
actions.exact_action: Locate the SorterSideDatabaseModel table or model.

steps.title: Inspect the relevant sorter-side fields
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface, find the relevant SorterSide record and inspect its Name, EntranceId, ExitId, TipperCount, and Disabled fields.
steps.purpose: Verify that the selected sorter-side record contains readable identifiers and configuration values needed to interpret its mapping.
steps.expected_result: The relevant SorterSide row is present with a readable Name, entrance and exit queue IDs, a numeric TipperCount, and a Disabled value.
steps.healthy_condition: Name, EntranceId, ExitId, TipperCount, and Disabled are populated and readable for the selected sorter-side row.
steps.failure_condition: The row is missing, EntranceId or ExitId is absent, TipperCount is blank or unexpected, or Disabled cannot be read.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the SorterSide row is missing, an entrance or exit ID is absent, TipperCount is blank or unexpected, or the Disabled state cannot be interpreted.

actions.label: Inspect sorter-side row
actions.exact_action: Find the relevant SorterSide record and inspect its Name, EntranceId, ExitId, TipperCount, and Disabled fields.

steps.title: Compare the live row with the sorter-side configuration examples
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface, compare the live SorterSide row with the available examples: SorterSide 1a has EntranceId 46, ExitId 44, TipperCount 4, Disabled 0; SorterSide 1b has EntranceId 246, ExitId 244, TipperCount 4, Disabled 0; SorterSide 2a has EntranceId 446, ExitId 444, TipperCount 4, Disabled 0; and SorterSide 2b has EntranceId 648, ExitId 646, TipperCount 4, Disabled 1.
steps.purpose: Identify mapping or disabled-state discrepancies that may explain sorter-side behavior.
steps.expected_result: The live row can be compared field by field with the named sorter-side examples, and the Disabled value is identified as either 0 or 1 where displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The live row has a coherent Name, EntranceId, ExitId, numeric TipperCount, and Disabled state; any difference from the examples is explainable by the live configuration.
steps.failure_condition: The live row has an unexplained queue-ID or tipper-count mismatch, or its Disabled state conflicts with the observed sorter-side condition or expected rollout configuration.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the live row does not match the expected sorter-side mapping and no approved configuration explanation is available.
Do not change TipperCount, EntranceId, ExitId, or Disabled values during this check.

actions.label: Compare configuration values
actions.exact_action: Compare the live row with the documented row structure for SorterSide 1a, 1b, 2a, and 2b.

title: Verify UPS chat message flow for sorter induction, destination enable/close, and label print triggers
summary: Verify that the live Sorter Sweeper ↔ UPS chat message sequence is occurring for a tote/parcel: tote inducted + destination enabled, scan-derived dimensions/load category collection, sort confirmation, optional hot bin/hop-in closeout triggering exchange, destination close before exchange, and print label message to the printer at the tipper stage.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm that the UPS-facing chat message sequence described for the Sorter Sweeper module is present and progressing for totes/parcels (induction → destination enable → scan data → sort confirmation → hot bin/hop-in exchange → destination close → print label).

steps.title: Open the live OptiSweep/WCS API client surface (Apidog / WCS API)
steps.instruction: Open the live OptiSweep/WCS API client surface (Apidog / WCS API) to begin querying for message evidence tied to the tote/parcel in process.
steps.purpose: Establish the live API view needed to query message evidence for the UPS chat sequence.
steps.expected_result: You are able to run live API queries against the OptiSweep/WCS API from the Apidog client.
steps.healthy_condition: API queries return responses (no timeouts/connection failures) sufficient to locate message evidence for the target tote/parcel.
steps.failure_condition: API queries fail (e.g., no response/timeout) such that message evidence cannot be retrieved.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the API cannot be queried reliably, escalate for deeper API responsiveness investigation (wcs_api_responsiveness).

actions.label: Open API client
actions.exact_action: Open the live OptiSweep/WCS API client surface (Apidog / WCS API).

steps.title: Identify the live API requests/endpoints that correspond to each UPS chat message type in the sequence
steps.instruction: Using the live OptiSweep/WCS API client, identify the API requests/endpoints that provide evidence for: tote inducted message, destination enabled message, scan-derived dimensions/load category, sort confirmation, hot bin/hop-in message (if applicable), destination close message, and print label message to the printer.
steps.purpose: Map the described UPS chat message sequence to concrete live API queries so you can verify ordered presence for the same tote/parcel.
steps.expected_result: You have a set of live API queries that can return evidence records for each message type listed above.
steps.healthy_condition: Each message type can be retrieved as a distinct evidence record set that can be correlated by tote/parcel identifier.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate any live API evidence for one or more required message types (tote inducted, destination enabled, sort confirmation, destination close, print label).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the API evidence mapping cannot be established for required message types, stop and escalate for SME mapping of message types to live API fields/endpoints.

actions.label: Map message types to API evidence
actions.exact_action: Identify the live API endpoints/requests that correspond to the UPS chat message exchanges described in the segment (tote inducted message, destination enabled message, sort confirmation, hot bin message/hop-in message, destination close message, print label message).

steps.title: Verify tote inducted + destination enabled evidence for the same tote/parcel
steps.instruction: For a tote/parcel currently in process, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for both: (1) tote inducted message and (2) destination enabled message. Correlate both evidence records to the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.purpose: Confirm the induction stage of the UPS chat sequence is present and not stuck before destination enable.
steps.expected_result: Both tote inducted and destination enabled evidence records are present for the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.healthy_condition: The two evidence records are present together for the same tote/parcel and do not indicate the process is stuck before destination enable.
steps.failure_condition: Tote inducted exists but destination enabled is missing for the same tote/parcel, or the evidence indicates the sequence is stuck earlier.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if tote inducted is present but destination enabled is missing for the same tote/parcel.

actions.label: Query induction evidence
actions.exact_action: Query the API for evidence that a tote inducted message and a destination enabled message were sent/received for that tote.

steps.title: Verify scan-derived dimensions and load category evidence
steps.instruction: For the same tote/parcel context, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for scan-derived parcel dimensions and load category fields that are described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.
steps.purpose: Confirm the scan tunnel data collection stage is occurring and populating the parcel attributes used downstream.
steps.expected_result: Dimensions and load category fields are populated for the parcel/tote context.
steps.healthy_condition: Dimension and load category values are present (not null/empty) for the same tote/parcel identifier that has induction evidence.
steps.failure_condition: Scan-derived dimensions and/or load category are missing or not populated for the tote/parcel in process.
stop_or_escalate_if: If scan-derived dimensions/load category are missing while induction evidence exists, escalate for deeper module-level investigation (Sorter Sweeper vs XLE COM vs OPC COM).

actions.label: Query scan data evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for scan/parcel data collection evidence (dimensions and load category) that is described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.

steps.title: Verify sort confirmation evidence includes final destination
steps.instruction: For the same tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for sort confirmation records. Confirm that a sort confirmation record exists and includes a final destination for the parcel.
steps.purpose: Confirm the sort stage is completed and that the parcel has a final destination in the confirmation evidence.
steps.expected_result: A sort confirmation evidence record exists for the tote/parcel and includes a final destination.
steps.healthy_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is present and shows a final destination value for the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.failure_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is missing, or it exists without a final destination value.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if sort confirmation evidence is missing for the tote/parcel.

actions.label: Query sort confirmation
actions.exact_action: Query for sort confirmation evidence that sort was sent from XLE onto the chat and that a sort confirmation was sent from the sorter onto the chat.

steps.title: Verify hot bin closeout / hop-in exchange evidence (when expected)
steps.instruction: If the tote(s) are expected to be hop-in/hot-bin, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for hot bin message/hop-in message records for those totes. Confirm that the exchange-related state advances immediately after the hot bin/hop-in evidence.
steps.purpose: Confirm the hot bin/hop-in closeout path triggers an exchange immediately when UPS sends the hot bin message.
steps.expected_result: Hot bin/hop-in evidence exists for the tote(s) and exchange-related state advances immediately after.
steps.healthy_condition: For hop-in/hot-bin totes, hot bin/hop-in evidence is present and exchange advancement is observable in the evidence timeline for the same tote(s).
steps.failure_condition: Hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing when expected, or exchange advancement does not occur immediately after hot bin/hop-in evidence.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing for totes that are expected to be hop-in.

actions.label: Query hot bin/hop-in evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for a hot bin message/hop-in message for totes that are hop in and confirm an exchange is triggered immediately.

steps.title: Verify destination close message exists before exchange advancement
steps.instruction: Before the exchange-related state advances for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a destination close message being sent onto the chat. Correlate it to the destination tied to the tote.
steps.purpose: Confirm the destination close stage is sent before the exchange occurs.
steps.expected_result: A destination close message evidence record exists for the destination tied to the tote before exchange-related state advances.
steps.healthy_condition: Destination close evidence is present and occurs earlier in the evidence timeline than exchange advancement for the same tote/parcel.
steps.failure_condition: Destination close message is missing, or exchange advancement occurs without destination close evidence preceding it.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if destination close message is missing before the exchange-related state advances.

actions.label: Query destination close evidence
actions.exact_action: Before an exchange, query for a destination close message being sent onto the chat.

steps.title: Verify print label message is sent at the tipper stage
steps.instruction: At the tipper stage for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a print label message being sent to the printer. Confirm it is associated with the label provided by XLE (e.g., label payload/identifier present).
steps.purpose: Confirm the final stage: label print trigger message is sent to the printer with the label provided by XLE.
steps.expected_result: A print label message evidence record exists and is associated with the label provided by XLE (label payload/identifier present).
steps.healthy_condition: Print label evidence is present for the tote/parcel at the tipper stage and includes an associated label identifier/payload.
steps.failure_condition: Print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.

actions.label: Query print label evidence
actions.exact_action: At the tipper stage, query for a print label message being sent to the printer.

steps.title: Stop and escalate on missing/out-of-order message evidence
steps.instruction: If any required message evidence is missing or out of order for the same tote/parcel (tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label missing at tipper), stop further checks and escalate for deeper module-level investigation.
steps.purpose: Ensure rapid escalation when the required message sequence is incomplete or out of order for the same tote/parcel.
steps.expected_result: A clear escalation decision is made based on which message evidence is missing/out of order.
steps.healthy_condition: All required message evidence is present in the expected order for the tote/parcel under investigation.
steps.failure_condition: Any required evidence is missing or the order is violated for the same tote/parcel.
stop_or_escalate_if: tote inducted present but destination enabled missing
sort confirmation missing
destination close missing before exchange
print label message missing at tipper
only one side present (e.g., scan data present but sort confirmation missing)

actions.label: Escalate based on evidence gap
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if any required message evidence is missing (e.g., tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label message missing at tipper).

title: Check IgnitionLaneActivityModel for Missing Dimension Data in SSMS
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect the read-only dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel view and determine whether recent lane activity records contain dimension data expected from the dimensioners. Correlate dimension fields with package identifiers, Message, PackageClassification, Missing DimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, and Diverted indicators. This procedure does not modify or reboot dimensioners.
when_to_use: Use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when support needs to verify whether recent lane activity records contain expected dimension data, especially when Missing DimensionData is suspected or affected records show blank or absent dimension values.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to reboot, reconfigure, or otherwise modify dimensioners.
Do not use this procedure as a dimensioner recovery procedure; the source supports database verification only.

steps.title: Open the applicable WCS / Helix database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In SSMS, select the applicable WCS / Helix database containing the dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel view or model. Use the database for inspection only.
steps.purpose: Establish access to the live database that contains the lane activity model.
steps.expected_result: The applicable WCS / Helix database is selected and dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel is available to open.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS can access the applicable WCS / Helix database and expose dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel for read-only inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The applicable database or dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel cannot be accessed or located.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the applicable WCS / Helix database or dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel cannot be accessed.

actions.label: Select WCS / Helix database
actions.exact_action: Select the applicable WCS/Helix database containing the dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel view or model.

steps.title: Open dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel in read-only view
steps.instruction: Open dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel in the read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view. Confirm that the lane activity table displays the record and field set used for this check.
steps.purpose: Display the live lane activity records and the fields needed for the dimension-data check.
steps.expected_result: The live view displays dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel records with lane, package, dimension, and status-related columns.
steps.healthy_condition: The view is readable and includes fields such as Last Update, SorterName, SortName, SortGuid, Zone, LaneName, PackageUid, Tracking Number, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, Message, PackageClassification, Missing DimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, and Diverted.
steps.failure_condition: The view is unavailable, unreadable, or does not expose the records and fields required for the investigation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the model cannot be opened or the required fields are not available.

actions.label: Open lane activity model
actions.exact_action: Open the dbo.IgnitionLaneActivityModel records using the read-only view.

steps.title: Identify recent lane activity records
steps.instruction: Review recent values in Last Update, SorterName, SortName, Zone, LaneName, PackageUid, and Tracking Number in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) lane activity view. Use these fields to identify the records relevant to the reported lane or sorter condition.
steps.purpose: Limit the inspection to the relevant recent records and identify the affected sorter, zone, lane, and package activity.
steps.expected_result: Relevant recent lane activity records are identified with their update time, sorter and lane location, PackageUid, and Tracking Number.
steps.healthy_condition: Recent records are present and can be associated with the investigated sorter, zone, lane, or package.
steps.failure_condition: No recent lane activity records are present, or the records cannot be associated with the affected lane, sorter, or package.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if recent lane activity records are absent for the affected area or investigation period.

actions.label: Review recent identifiers
actions.exact_action: Review recent values in Last Update, SorterName, SortName, Zone, LaneName, PackageUid, and Tracking Number.

steps.title: Inspect dimension and weight fields
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) records identified in the previous step, inspect Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube. Compare whether these fields contain values or are blank or missing for the affected records.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the relevant lane activity records contain dimension and weight data or show missing values.
steps.expected_result: Each relevant record shows the observable state of Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant records contain observable values in the available dimension and weight fields. The source does not define a universal numeric threshold; interpret the result from field presence or absence.
steps.failure_condition: One or more relevant records have blank or absent Length, Width, Height, Weight, or Cube values, indicating that expected dimension data is not present for those records.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if dimension fields remain blank or missing for affected records.

actions.label: Check dimension fields
actions.exact_action: Check whether Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube contain dimension and weight values or are blank/missing for the records being investigated.

steps.title: Review lane activity status indicators
steps.instruction: For the same records in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), review Message, PackageClassification, Missing DimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, and Diverted. Record the observed values without assigning undocumented meanings to binary-like or value-like indicators.
steps.purpose: Correlate the dimension-field state with the message and status indicators for the same records.
steps.expected_result: The affected records show their Message and PackageClassification values together with the observed Missing DimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, and Diverted values.
steps.healthy_condition: The records have a visible Message and PackageClassification, dimension fields are populated where expected, and Missing DimensionData is not indicated for the records under investigation.
steps.failure_condition: Missing DimensionData is indicated, or the records combine blank or absent dimension fields with a relevant status indicator. MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, or Diverted may also be present and should be reported as observed rather than reinterpreted.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if Missing DimensionData is present for affected records.
Escalate to L2/L3 support if the status fields and dimension fields do not provide a clear observable result.

actions.label: Review status columns
actions.exact_action: Review Message, PackageClassification, Missing DimensionData, MissingInduct, Tote Not Found, and Diverted for the same records.

title: Start OptiSweep System Through the WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent approved API client to start the system from a shutdown state, then verify the live system state is no longer shutdown.
when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API when the live system state is shutdown and an authorized L2 or L3 support user needs to start the system through the System Startup operation.
not_for: Do not use when GET System State does not report shutdown.
Do not use as a substitute for investigating an API request that cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result.
Do not use this procedure to perform physical recovery, E-stop, or LOTO actions.

steps.title: Locate System Startup in the WCS API client
steps.instruction: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or an equivalent approved API client and locate POST System Startup in the System API list.
steps.purpose: Identify the approved API operation used to start OptiSweep from a shutdown state.
steps.expected_result: The System API list displays POST System Startup and GET System State.
steps.healthy_condition: Both named operations are available in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.failure_condition: POST System Startup or GET System State is not available, cannot be located, or cannot be executed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The required API operation cannot be located or executed.

actions.label: Open the System API list
actions.exact_action: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API in Apidog or an equivalent approved API client and locate POST System Startup.

steps.title: Confirm the system is shut down
steps.instruction: In the OptiSweep / WCS API client, execute GET System State and inspect the returned current system state. Continue only when the returned state is shutdown.
steps.purpose: Verify that the startup operation is applicable to the current live system state.
steps.expected_result: GET System State returns shutdown as the current system state.
steps.healthy_condition: The live API response reports shutdown, which is the state for which System Startup is defined.
steps.failure_condition: The response reports a state other than shutdown, or the response is unavailable or unrecognized.
stop_or_escalate_if: GET System State does not report shutdown.
GET System State cannot be executed or returns an unrecognized result.

actions.label: Read current system state
actions.exact_action: Execute GET System State and confirm that the returned state is shutdown.

steps.title: Execute System Startup and recheck state
steps.instruction: After confirming shutdown in the OptiSweep / WCS API, execute POST System Startup. Then execute GET System State again and inspect the returned state.
steps.purpose: Issue the supported startup request and obtain a current post-request system state.
steps.expected_result: The startup request completes and the subsequent GET System State response returns the current post-startup state.
steps.healthy_condition: The post-request state is no longer shutdown.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be executed, returns an unrecognized result, or the subsequent state remains shutdown.
stop_or_escalate_if: The System Startup request cannot be executed.
The API returns an unrecognized result.
The subsequent system state remains shutdown.

actions.label: Start the system
actions.exact_action: Execute POST System Startup.

actions.label: Retrieve post-startup state
actions.exact_action: Retrieve GET System State again.

steps.title: Verify the system left shutdown
steps.instruction: Compare the second GET System State result with the initial shutdown result in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the startup operation achieved the supported state transition.
steps.expected_result: The second GET System State result no longer reports shutdown, indicating that the system left the shutdown state.
steps.healthy_condition: The live system state is a running or other non-shutdown state returned by GET System State.
steps.failure_condition: The live system state still reports shutdown or the returned state cannot be interpreted.
stop_or_escalate_if: The system state does not change after the startup request.
The returned state is unrecognized.

actions.label: Compare system states
actions.exact_action: Compare the returned state with the documented running or non-shutdown state.

title: Verify Robotics module AGV state machine generates Geek Plus execution commands from Sorter Sweeper tote tasks
summary: Validate the handoff from Sorter Sweeper tote tasks to the Robotics module’s AGV state machine and confirm that the Robotics module generates Geek Plus execution commands for the documented AGV task set (induct tote, remove tote, initialize AGV, go to, pick up tote, move tote, drop off tote, cancel request, go charge).
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm that tote tasks created by Sorter Sweeper are received by the Robotics module (AGV state machine) and that the Robotics module generates Geek Plus execution commands matching the expected AGV command/task names.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for physical safety actions (e.g., E-stop). This procedure is for validating software command generation/handoff behavior only.

steps.title: Confirm the Robotics module is the AGV state machine that receives tote tasks and generates Geek Plus commands
steps.instruction: On the live OptiSweep/WCS/Robotics command-generation evidence you have access to, confirm that the Robotics module is the component responsible for acting as the AGV state machine that receives tote tasks from Sorter Sweeper and generates commands for Geek Plus to execute.
steps.purpose: Establish the expected software responsibility boundary before validating the tote-task handoff and command generation.
steps.expected_result: You can observe that tote tasks originating from Sorter Sweeper are handled by the Robotics module as the AGV state machine, and that Geek Plus execution commands are produced from those tote tasks.
steps.healthy_condition: The live evidence shows Robotics module command generation activity corresponding to tote-task handling (not just Sorter Sweeper orchestration).
steps.failure_condition: Live evidence indicates tote tasks are received/processed by Sorter Sweeper but Robotics module does not generate Geek Plus execution commands.
stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot find any live evidence that Robotics module generates Geek Plus commands from tote tasks, stop and escalate for deeper Robotics module / Geek Plus command-generation troubleshooting.

actions.label: Verify Robotics module state-machine responsibility
actions.exact_action: Confirm Robotics module acts as the state machine for the AGVs and generates commands for Geek Plus to execute those tasks.

steps.title: Verify the Robotics module receives tote tasks from the Sorter Sweeper module
steps.instruction: Using the live evidence you have access to for Robotics module command generation and/or Robotics-side task/command tracking, verify that tote tasks created by Sorter Sweeper are present/consumed by the Robotics module.
steps.purpose: Confirm the first handoff: Sorter Sweeper tote-task creation/orchestration reaches the Robotics module.
steps.expected_result: For the relevant tote tasks, Robotics module shows corresponding command-generation activity (or command records) that indicate it received/processed those tote tasks.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote-task-driven command generation is observable in Robotics-side evidence (e.g., command records progressing through statuses).
steps.failure_condition: Tote tasks are present at Sorter Sweeper, but there is no corresponding Robotics module command-generation activity for those tasks.
stop_or_escalate_if: If tote tasks are received but Robotics module does not generate Geek Plus commands, stop and escalate for deeper Robotics module / Geek Plus command generation troubleshooting.

actions.label: Check tote-task handoff into Robotics module
actions.exact_action: Verify that the Robotics module receives tote tasks from the Sorter Sweeper module.

steps.title: Check that the Robotics module generates Geek Plus commands for the expected AGV task set
steps.instruction: For the relevant tote tasks, verify that the Robotics module generates Geek Plus execution commands corresponding to the documented AGV task set: induct tote, remove tote, initialize AGV, go to, pick up tote, move tote, drop off tote, cancel request, go charge.
steps.purpose: Validate the second handoff: Robotics module command generation matches the documented AGV task/command names that Geek Plus should execute.
steps.expected_result: Support can confirm that for the relevant tote tasks, the Robotics module produces Geek Plus execution commands corresponding to the documented AGV task set.
steps.healthy_condition: The generated command set includes the expected command/task names (Induct tote, Remove tote, Initialize AGV, Go to, Pickup tote, Move tote, Drop off tote, Cancel Request, Go Charge) for the tote-task sequence being validated.
steps.failure_condition: Geek Plus commands are not generated, or the generated command set does not match the documented task names.
stop_or_escalate_if: If tote tasks are received but Geek Plus commands are not generated (or the generated command set does not match the documented task names), stop and escalate for deeper Robotics module / Geek Plus command generation troubleshooting.

actions.label: Validate expected command/task names are generated
actions.exact_action: Use the documented AGV command/task names as the checklist for what should be generated/handled: induct tote, remove tote, initialize AGV, go to, pick up tote, move tote, drop off tote, cancel request, go charge.

title: View Current Tote Exchange Settings in the OptiSweep / WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog to submit GET GetExchangeSettings and inspect the current tote exchange headings or exchange settings.
when_to_use: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog when support needs to inspect the current tote exchange headings or exchange settings without changing them.
not_for: Do not use this read-only check to modify exchange settings.
Do not use it to infer settings that are not returned by GET GetExchangeSettings.
Do not use it as a substitute for a procedure that updates exchange settings.

steps.title: Open the Totes API area in Apidog
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client, open the OptiSweep / WCS API and navigate to the Totes API area.
steps.purpose: Access the live OptiSweep / WCS API request used to inspect tote exchange settings.
steps.expected_result: The Totes API area is visible and includes the GET GetExchangeSettings request.
steps.healthy_condition: The WCS API client displays the Totes API area and the GetExchangeSettings request.
steps.failure_condition: The Totes API area or GET GetExchangeSettings request is not available.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the Totes API area or GET GetExchangeSettings request is unavailable.

actions.label: Open Totes API
actions.exact_action: Open the Totes API area in Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client.

steps.title: Submit GET GetExchangeSettings
steps.instruction: In the Totes API area of Apidog, open the GET GetExchangeSettings request and submit it using the displayed request controls.
steps.purpose: Retrieve the current tote exchange headings or exchange settings from the live OptiSweep / WCS API.
steps.expected_result: The GET GetExchangeSettings request completes and displays a returned result for the current exchange settings.
steps.healthy_condition: The request can be submitted and produces a returned result.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted or does not return the current exchange settings.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the request cannot be submitted.
Escalate to L3 support if the request does not return the current exchange settings.

actions.label: Submit settings request
actions.exact_action: Open the GET GetExchangeSettings request and submit it.

steps.title: Review the returned exchange headings or settings
steps.instruction: Review the returned result in the OptiSweep / WCS API client and identify the displayed current exchange headings or exchange settings.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the live API returned the current tote exchange information needed for diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: The returned result displays the current exchange headings or current exchange settings.
steps.healthy_condition: Current exchange headings or exchange settings are visible in the returned API result.
steps.failure_condition: No current exchange headings or exchange settings are displayed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the returned result does not display the current exchange headings or exchange settings.
Do not modify exchange settings as part of this read-only check.

actions.label: Review returned settings
actions.exact_action: Review the returned exchange headings or current exchange settings.

title: Verify Robot Location model fields and location types/statuses used by RMS orange locations
summary: Using the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only access surface, verify the Robot Location database model table includes the expected location attributes (station number, occupied, zone, closeout zone, location type, max AGVs, dwell-time tracking) and that the enumerated location types/statuses match the RMS orange location categories (sorter/tipper/hospital/shut down/GLD pre queue).
when_to_use: When you need to confirm that RMS orange location categories are backed by the expected Robot Location model/table definition in the WCS/Robotics database (fields present and location type/status enumerations match the expected categories).

steps.title: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only access surface
steps.instruction: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) access surface to connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the Robotics database model table definitions for the Robot Location model.
steps.purpose: Establish access to the OptiSweep/WCS database where the Robotics database model table definitions are stored.
steps.expected_result: SSMS is connected to the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the Robotics database model table definitions for the Robot Location model.
steps.healthy_condition: You can browse the database objects needed to locate the Robot Location database model table definition.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect to the expected OptiSweep/WCS database or cannot access the Robotics model/table definitions needed to locate the Robot Location model table.

actions.label: Connect to OptiSweep/WCS database in SSMS
actions.exact_action: In SSMS, connect to the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the Robotics database model table definitions for the Robot Location model.

steps.title: Locate Robot Location database model table and verify required location attributes
steps.instruction: In SSMS, locate the Robot Location database model table definition and verify it includes fields/attributes for: station number, occupied (occupied or not), zone, closeout zone, location type, Max number of AGVs allowed at that location, and whether the location should be tracked for dwell time there.
steps.purpose: Confirm the Robot Location model table includes the expected location attributes used by RMS orange locations.
steps.expected_result: The Robot Location database model table definition shows the expected location attributes: station number, occupied, zone, closeout zone, location type, Max number of AGVs allowed, and dwell-time tracking (tracked vs not tracked).
steps.healthy_condition: All required attributes are present in the Robot Location model/table definition with names/meaning consistent with the expected set (station number, occupied, zone, closeout zone, location type, max AGVs, dwell tracking).
steps.failure_condition: One or more required attributes are missing from the Robot Location model/table definition or are named differently than expected such that the mapping cannot be confirmed.
stop_or_escalate_if: If required fields (station number, occupied, zone/closeout zone, location type, max AGVs, dwell-time tracking) are missing or named differently than expected, escalate to deeper model/catalog review.

actions.label: Verify required fields exist in Robot Location model/table
actions.exact_action: Locate the Robot Location database model table and verify it includes fields/attributes for: station number, occupied (occupied or not), zone, closeout zone, location type, Max number of AGVs allowed at that location, and whether the location should be tracked for dwell time there.

steps.title: Verify Robot Location model includes expected location types/statuses for RMS orange categories
steps.instruction: In the same Robot Location model/table definition, verify the listed location types/statuses include the categories: sorter entrance queue, sorter queue, sorter exit queue; tipper, tipper queue, tipper exit queue; hospital drop off, hospital entrance queue, hospital pickup, hospital exit queue; queue shut down, off the end shut down queue; GLD pre queue entrance, GLD pre queue exit.
steps.purpose: Confirm the enumerated location types/statuses in the Robot Location model match the RMS orange location categories.
steps.expected_result: The Robot Location model/table definition includes the named location types/statuses for sorter/tipper/hospital/shut down/GLD pre queue categories.
steps.healthy_condition: All listed categories appear in the Robot Location model/table definition (as location types/statuses) with names consistent with the expected set.
steps.failure_condition: One or more expected location types/statuses are missing from the Robot Location model/table definition.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the named location types/statuses (sorter entrance/queue/exit, tipper/queues, hospital queues, shut down queues, GLD pre queue entrance/exit) are missing from the Robot Location model, escalate because RMS orange location categories may not be backed by the expected model.

actions.label: Check enumerated location types/statuses list
actions.exact_action: In the same Robot Location model/table definition, verify the listed location types/statuses include the categories named in the segment: sorter entrance queue, sorter queue, sorter exit queue; tipper, tipper queue, tipper exit queue; hospital drop off, hospital entrance queue, hospital pickup, hospital exit queue; queue shut down, off the end shut down queue; GLD pre queue entrance, GLD pre queue exit.

steps.title: Cross-check RMS orange location categories map to the same Robot Location types/statuses
steps.instruction: Using the Robot Location model/table definition you verified, confirm that the segment’s RMS orange location categories correspond to the same named location types/statuses you see in the Robot Location model/table definition.
steps.purpose: Ensure the Robot Location model’s location types/statuses correspond to the RMS orange locations categories.
steps.expected_result: The RMS orange location categories map consistently to the location types/statuses present in the Robot Location model/table definition.
steps.healthy_condition: The set of location types/statuses in the Robot Location model/table definition matches the expected RMS orange categories (sorter/tipper/hospital/shut down/GLD pre queue).
steps.failure_condition: The RMS orange categories cannot be mapped consistently because the Robot Location model/table definition lacks or differs from the expected location types/statuses.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the mapping is inconsistent (e.g., missing or mismatched location types/statuses), escalate to deeper model/catalog review.

actions.label: Validate mapping consistency
actions.exact_action: Cross-check that the segment’s statement about RMS orange locations is consistent with the location types/statuses you see in the Robot Location model (i.e., the RMS orange location categories map to the same named location types/statuses).

title: Check SystemDatabaseModel lifecycle/staging status in Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics (SSMS)
summary: Use SSMS against the Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics database to confirm the SystemDatabaseModel snapshot lifecycle/staging status value is currently one of the expected states (StartingUp, StartUpRequested, Running, ShutDownRequested, ZoneConfigRequested, ZoneConfigStaging, CloseOutRequested, CloseOutStaging, CloseOutStaged).
when_to_use: When you need to verify the current system lifecycle/staging state (startup, running, shutdown, zone config, closeout) by checking the SystemDatabaseModel snapshot status values in the Robotics database.

steps.title: Connect to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and select Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics
steps.instruction: Using SSMS (WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)), connect to the environment and select the Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics database.
steps.purpose: Establish the correct SSMS connection and database context for reading SystemDatabaseModel snapshot status.

steps.healthy_condition: The Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics database appears in the SSMS object tree and is selectable/active.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect to SSMS or cannot select/open Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics due to connection or permission errors.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if you cannot connect to SSMS or cannot access the Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics database (permissions/query errors).

actions.label: Open SSMS and connect
