actions.label: Select Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics
actions.exact_action: Select the Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics database

steps.title: Locate dbo.SystemDatabaseModel in the dbo schema
steps.instruction: In SSMS, navigate to the dbo schema and locate the table/model named [dbo].[SystemDatabaseModel].
steps.purpose: Ensure you are querying the correct model/table that contains the system lifecycle/staging snapshot status.
steps.expected_result: dbo.SystemDatabaseModel is found and visible in the SSMS database object tree.
steps.healthy_condition: dbo.SystemDatabaseModel exists under the dbo schema for Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics.
steps.failure_condition: dbo.SystemDatabaseModel is missing/unavailable or cannot be accessed due to permissions.

actions.exact_action: In the dbo schema, locate the table/model named [dbo].[SystemDatabaseModel].

steps.title: Read the SystemDatabaseModel snapshot status using WITH (SNAPSHOT)
steps.instruction: Run a read-only query/view of [dbo].[SystemDatabaseModel] using WITH (SNAPSHOT) to view the current snapshot row(s) and the status field(s) that represent lifecycle/staging state.
steps.purpose: Retrieve the current lifecycle/staging status value(s) from the SystemDatabaseModel snapshot.
steps.expected_result: You can view the current SystemDatabaseModel snapshot row(s) and identify the lifecycle/staging status value present in the status field(s).
steps.healthy_condition: The query returns snapshot row(s) showing a lifecycle/staging status value that is one of the documented set.
steps.failure_condition: The snapshot cannot be read (query/permission errors) or the returned status value(s) are outside the documented set or appear inconsistent.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the snapshot cannot be read (permissions/query errors).
Stop and escalate if the status value(s) are outside the documented lifecycle/staging set or appear inconsistent (e.g., multiple lifecycle states simultaneously).

actions.label: Query snapshot status
actions.exact_action: Run a read-only query to view the current snapshot row(s) for SystemDatabaseModel (the slide indicates it uses WITH (SNAPSHOT) to show state and current sort plan).

steps.title: Confirm the current lifecycle/staging status is within the documented set
steps.instruction: Identify which lifecycle/staging status value is currently present in the SystemDatabaseModel status field(s) and confirm it matches one of: StartingUp, StartUpRequested, Running, ShutDownRequested, ZoneConfigRequested, ZoneConfigStaging, CloseOutRequested, CloseOutStaging, CloseOutStaged.
steps.purpose: Validate that the system lifecycle/staging state is one of the expected values and interpret whether it is consistent.
steps.expected_result: Exactly one current lifecycle/staging status value is present and it matches one of the documented values.
steps.healthy_condition: The status value shown is a single, current lifecycle/staging state from the documented set.
steps.failure_condition: The status value is not in the documented set, or the snapshot shows an unexpected combination (e.g., multiple lifecycle states simultaneously).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the snapshot shows an unexpected combination (e.g., multiple lifecycle states simultaneously).
Escalate if the status value is outside the documented lifecycle/staging set.

actions.label: Match status to documented set
actions.exact_action: Identify which lifecycle/staging status value is currently present in the SystemDatabaseModel status field(s) and confirm it matches one of the documented values.

title: Check Active Dwell Time at Sort Locations Using Location Active Dwell / Location Dwell Activity Tables
summary: Use WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to verify how long an AGV has been sitting at a sort location that is marked for dwell tracking by checking active dwell records in “Location Active Dwell” and, if the AGV has already left, confirming the dwell activity was archived to “Location Dwell activity”.
when_to_use: When you need evidence of dwell timing at a sort location that is configured for dwell tracking (e.g., to confirm how long an AGV has been sitting at that location).

steps.title: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the OptiSweep database containing dwell models
steps.instruction: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics / location dwell models.
steps.purpose: Establish DB connectivity so you can query the dwell tracking models/tables.
steps.expected_result: SSMS is connected to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics/location dwell models so you can browse/query the dwell-related model tables.
steps.healthy_condition: You can access the database objects/models needed to locate “Location Active Dwell” and the archived “Location Dwell activity” records.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the OptiSweep database or cannot locate the dwell-related models/tables needed to perform the check.

actions.label: Connect to OptiSweep DB in SSMS
actions.exact_action: Open WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and connect to the OptiSweep database that contains the Robotics / location dwell models.

steps.title: Locate the “Location Active Dwell” model/table
steps.instruction: In SSMS, locate the model/table named “Location Active Dwell” (Location Active Dwell model table).
steps.purpose: Identify the active dwell dataset that contains current dwell records for dwell-tracked sort locations.
steps.expected_result: You find the “Location Active Dwell” model/table in the OptiSweep database.
steps.healthy_condition: The “Location Active Dwell” model/table is present and accessible for querying/browsing.
steps.failure_condition: The “Location Active Dwell” model/table cannot be found or is not accessible in the connected database.

actions.label: Find Location Active Dwell model/table
actions.exact_action: Locate the model/table named “Location Active Dwell” (Location Active Dwell model table).

steps.title: Find dwell-tracked sort location rows and read the dwell time value
steps.instruction: In “Location Active Dwell”, find the row(s) for the relevant sort location(s) that are marked for dwell tracking and identify the dwell time value (how long the AGV has been sitting at that location).
steps.purpose: Determine how long the AGV has been sitting at the specific dwell-tracked sort location.
steps.expected_result: For the selected dwell-tracked sort location(s), “Location Active Dwell” shows row(s) containing dwell timing information (dwell time / total dwell duration) for the current active dwell.
steps.healthy_condition: Active dwell rows exist for the dwell-tracked location(s), and the dwell time value reflects the current duration the AGV has been sitting at that location.
steps.failure_condition: No active dwell row exists in “Location Active Dwell” for a location that you expect to be dwell-tracked.
stop_or_escalate_if: If no active dwell record exists in “Location Active Dwell” for a location that is expected to be dwell-tracked, escalate for deeper investigation (e.g., whether the location is correctly marked for dwell tracking or whether dwell tracking is not being recorded).

actions.label: Query active dwell rows for the location(s)
actions.exact_action: In “Location Active Dwell”, find the row(s) for the relevant sort location(s) that are marked for dwell tracking and identify the dwell time value (how long the AGV has been sitting at that location).

steps.title: Confirm whether the dwell record is still active
steps.instruction: Confirm whether the dwell record is still active (present in “Location Active Dwell”).
steps.purpose: Verify that the dwell you are measuring is currently active (still present in the active dwell table).
steps.expected_result: The dwell record for the location/AGV is either present in “Location Active Dwell” (active) or absent (indicating the AGV has left and the dwell should have been archived).
steps.healthy_condition: If the AGV is currently at the dwell-tracked location, the corresponding dwell record is present in “Location Active Dwell”.
steps.failure_condition: The dwell record is absent from “Location Active Dwell” when you expect it to be active.

actions.label: Check presence in active dwell table
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether the dwell record is still active (present in Location Active Dwell).

steps.title: If AGV already left, verify archived dwell activity in “Location Dwell activity”
steps.instruction: If the AGV has already left the location, check the archived “Location Dwell activity” records for the same location to confirm the dwell activity was archived after leaving.
steps.purpose: Confirm that dwell tracking completed and the dwell activity was archived after the AGV left the location.
steps.expected_result: When the dwell is no longer active, the corresponding dwell activity is present in “Location Dwell activity” for the same location.
steps.healthy_condition: Active dwell is absent from “Location Active Dwell” and the dwell activity appears in “Location Dwell activity” after the AGV leaves.
steps.failure_condition: Dwell records appear inconsistent between active and archived tables (e.g., missing from both, or present in active when it should have been archived).
stop_or_escalate_if: If dwell records appear inconsistent between active and archived tables, escalate for support to reconcile the timing/archival behavior.

actions.label: Check archived dwell activity
actions.exact_action: If the AGV has already left the location, check the archived “Location Dwell activity” records for the same location to confirm the dwell activity was archived after leaving.

title: Execute an AGV's Active Command Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API ExecutedAgvCommand operation with a confirmed robot ID to execute the active command currently held by an AGV. The source describes this as useful after an unplanned restart when OptiSweep missed callbacks from Geek Plus.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV has an active command but OptiSweep missed callbacks from Geek Plus, including the source-described unplanned-restart scenario.
not_for: Do not use without a confirmed robot ID.
Do not use as a replacement-command or manual-command-entry procedure; the source does not define either.
Do not use when the request cannot be submitted or the AGV does not execute its active command without escalating.

steps.title: Open the ExecutedAgvCommand operation
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API group and locate the operation labeled ExecutedAgvCommand, shown as POST Executed Agv Command.
steps.purpose: Access the OptiSweep / WCS API operation used to execute the active command held by an AGV.
steps.expected_result: The POST Executed Agv Command operation is available for submission in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGVs operation list displays POST Executed Agv Command.
steps.failure_condition: The ExecutedAgvCommand operation is unavailable or the API client cannot be opened.
stop_or_escalate_if: The API client cannot be opened.
The ExecutedAgvCommand operation is not available.

actions.label: Locate API operation
actions.exact_action: Open the AGVs API operation labeled ExecutedAgvCommand / POST Executed Agv Command.

steps.title: Enter the confirmed robot ID
steps.instruction: Provide the confirmed robot ID required by the ExecutedAgvCommand operation in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.purpose: Target the AGV whose active command is to be executed.
steps.expected_result: The request contains the robot ID for the intended AGV.
steps.healthy_condition: A confirmed robot ID is present for the intended AGV.
steps.failure_condition: The robot ID is missing, unconfirmed, or does not identify the intended AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: The robot ID cannot be confirmed.
The intended AGV cannot be identified.

actions.label: Confirm robot ID
actions.exact_action: Provide the robot ID required by ExecutedAgvCommand.

steps.title: Submit the active-command request
steps.instruction: Submit the POST ExecutedAgvCommand request in the OptiSweep / WCS API client with the confirmed robot ID.
steps.purpose: Request execution of the active command already held by the AGV.
steps.expected_result: The POST request is submitted for the selected AGV.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep / WCS API client accepts and submits the POST ExecutedAgvCommand request.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted.
stop_or_escalate_if: The request cannot be submitted.

actions.label: Submit API request
actions.exact_action: Submit the POST ExecutedAgvCommand request.

steps.title: Verify active-command execution
steps.instruction: Use the live AGV status or movement view, including the OptiSweep / WCS API AGV status information when available, to verify that the selected AGV executes its active command.
steps.purpose: Confirm on a live AGV surface that the active command was executed.
steps.expected_result: The selected AGV's live status or movement shows execution or progression of the active command.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV status or movement view shows the selected AGV executing or progressing the active command.
steps.failure_condition: The AGV does not execute or progress the active command after the request.
stop_or_escalate_if: The AGV does not execute its active command.
The live AGV status or movement view does not show execution or progression.

actions.label: Verify AGV state
actions.exact_action: Verify on the live AGV status or movement view that the AGV's active command is executed.

title: Check AGV State, Command Vitals, and Errors in the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog to inspect an AGV's live state, current command fields, vitals, network identity, AGV errors, system errors, and errorAlert indicator.
when_to_use: Use this Apidog / OptiSweep WCS API diagnostic when support needs to verify an AGV's live state, current command information, vitals, network identity, or AGV and system error indications.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to remove, recover, pause, resume, or execute an AGV command.
Do not use this procedure to infer a healthy battery or voltage range; the source provides example values but no complete operating thresholds.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.

steps.title: Open Get Agv Statuses in the Apidog WCS API client
steps.instruction: In the Apidog / WCS API client, open the AGVS area and select the request labeled "Get Agv Statuses".
steps.purpose: Open the live OptiSweep WCS API request that returns AGV status information.
steps.expected_result: The Get Agv Statuses request is open and can return an AGV status response.
steps.healthy_condition: The Apidog / WCS API client displays the Get Agv Statuses request and its response area.
steps.failure_condition: The request is unavailable, cannot be opened, or does not return a response.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the diagnostic and escalate to L2_support if the Get Agv Statuses response cannot be obtained.

actions.label: Open AGV status request
actions.exact_action: Select "Get Agv Statuses" in the AGVS area of the Apidog / WCS API client.

steps.title: Identify the AGV and inspect its state in the Apidog WCS API response
steps.instruction: In the Apidog / WCS API response, locate the affected AGV by its "name" and review its "state". Record the returned value exactly, including values such as "AtSorterEntranceQueue" or "SWaitingInzone".
steps.purpose: Associate the returned status information with the affected AGV and its current operating or location state.
steps.expected_result: The response identifies the AGV and provides its current state value.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected AGV has a returned "name" and a readable "state" value.
steps.failure_condition: The response does not identify the AGV or the "state" field is absent or unreadable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2_support if the response does not identify the AGV or provide its state.

actions.label: Inspect AGV identity and state
actions.exact_action: Review the returned "name" and "state" fields for the affected AGV.

steps.title: Inspect current command fields in the Apidog WCS API response
steps.instruction: In the Apidog / WCS API response for the identified AGV, review "commandGuid", "commandName", and "commandStatus". Record empty command fields as empty.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the response contains current AGV command information without assuming a command when fields are empty.
steps.expected_result: The response shows the available command GUID, command name, and command status values for the AGV.
steps.healthy_condition: The command fields are present and their returned values, including empty values, are recorded accurately.
steps.failure_condition: The command fields are unavailable or the response cannot be associated with the identified AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2_support if the command fields are unavailable or cannot be associated with the affected AGV.

actions.label: Inspect command information
actions.exact_action: Review "commandGuid", "commandName", and "commandStatus" in the Get Agv Statuses response.

steps.title: Inspect AGV vitals and network identity in the Apidog WCS API
steps.instruction: In the Apidog / WCS API response, review "battery", "voltage", "status", and "ip" for the identified AGV. Record the displayed values without applying an unsupported battery or voltage threshold.
steps.purpose: Capture the AGV's returned battery, voltage, status, and IP values for live diagnostic comparison.
steps.expected_result: The response provides the AGV's displayed battery value, voltage value, status, and IP address.
steps.healthy_condition: The vitals and identity fields are present; the source example shows values such as battery 78, voltage 56200, and "status": "NORMAL".
steps.failure_condition: One or more vitals or identity fields are unavailable, or the response cannot identify the AGV's returned values.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2_support if the response does not provide the AGV vitals or network identity needed for the diagnostic.

actions.label: Inspect AGV vitals and IP
actions.exact_action: Review "battery", "voltage", "status", and "ip" in the Get Agv Statuses response.

steps.title: Inspect AGV and system errors in the Apidog WCS API response
steps.instruction: In the Apidog / WCS API response, review "errorCode", "errorDescription", "errorCause", "systemErrorDescription", "systemErrorResolution", and "errorAlert". Treat populated error fields or "errorAlert": true as reported error indications. For active system errors, the related error information can include the error name, area, error code, last-seen time, system error description, and system error resolution.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the AGV or system has a reported error and whether the error alert is active.
steps.expected_result: The response shows the AGV and system error fields and indicates whether errorAlert is true or false.
steps.healthy_condition: The source's no-error example has "status": "NORMAL", empty AGV and system error fields, and "errorAlert": false.
steps.failure_condition: An error field contains a reported value or "errorAlert": true. A system error may identify an area such as AGV or Communication and include a system error description or resolution.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2_support when "errorAlert" is true.
Escalate when AGV or system error fields contain a reported error requiring further investigation.

actions.label: Inspect error indicators
actions.exact_action: Review the AGV error fields, system error fields, and "errorAlert" in the Get Agv Statuses response.

title: Verify Hospital Pickup and Drop-Off Location ID Mapping
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database to verify that hospital station pickup and drop-off identifiers resolve to the intended Location records.
when_to_use: Use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when validating hospital station configuration or investigating whether hospital pickup and drop-off identifiers resolve to Location records.
not_for: Do not use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) procedure to change hospital station IDs, pickup IDs, drop-off IDs, or database relationships.
Do not use this procedure as a general database-model orientation or training walkthrough without a live mapping check.

steps.title: Open the Sorter Sweeper location models
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view, open the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Location and HospitalStation records or models. Identify the available HospitalStationId, PickupId, DropOffId, and Location ID fields.
steps.purpose: Establish the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) records needed for the mapping check.
steps.expected_result: The WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view exposes the hospital station and location records needed for comparison.
steps.healthy_condition: Both the HospitalStation information and the Location records are available, with location-related identifier fields visible.
steps.failure_condition: The required HospitalStation or Location records are unavailable, or the relevant identifier fields cannot be identified.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate to L3_support if the required WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) records or identifier fields are not available.

actions.label: Open location models
actions.exact_action: Locate the Location and HospitalStation records in the Sorter Sweeper Database.

steps.title: Identify the hospital station pickup and drop-off IDs
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) HospitalStation record, identify the hospital station's HospitalStationId, PickupId, and DropOffId. Treat the pickup and drop-off identifiers as the location identifiers described for the hospital station.
steps.purpose: Obtain the identifiers that must resolve to Location records.
steps.expected_result: The WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) HospitalStation record provides the pickup and drop-off identifiers associated with the selected hospital station.
steps.healthy_condition: A HospitalStationId is associated with identifiable PickupId and DropOffId values.
steps.failure_condition: A PickupId or DropOffId is absent, cannot be associated with a HospitalStationId, or is not identifiable in the HospitalStation record.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate to L3_support if the selected hospital station has no identifiable PickupId or DropOffId.

actions.label: Inspect hospital station identifiers
actions.exact_action: Locate the HospitalStationId, PickupId, and DropOffId values in the HospitalStation record.

steps.title: Compare identifiers with Location records
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Location records, compare the HospitalStation PickupId and DropOffId from the selected HospitalStation record with the corresponding Location IDs. Check each identifier separately and determine whether it resolves to one identifiable Location row.
steps.purpose: Verify that each hospital station identifier resolves to an intended Location row.
steps.expected_result: Each hospital station PickupId and DropOffId resolves to an identifiable Location record, with the associated location identifier visible in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
steps.healthy_condition: Both identifiers resolve to Location rows and the relationship is unambiguous for the hospital station being checked.
steps.failure_condition: A PickupId or DropOffId has no matching Location row, maps to an unexpected location, or produces multiple or otherwise ambiguous matches.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate to L2_support or L3_support if a PickupId or DropOffId has no matching Location row.
Stop and escalate if an identifier maps to an unexpected or ambiguous Location relationship.

actions.label: Check pickup location
actions.exact_action: Compare the hospital station PickupId with the Location records.

actions.label: Check drop-off location
actions.exact_action: Compare the hospital station DropOffId with the Location records.

steps.title: Record the matched location records
steps.instruction: From the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) inspection, record the HospitalStationId, PickupId, DropOffId, the matched Location IDs, and the associated HospitalStation or Location records. Record any missing, unexpected, or ambiguous relationship without modifying the database.
steps.purpose: Preserve the observed mapping for the hospital station under investigation.
steps.expected_result: The diagnostic record contains the observed hospital station identifiers and their matched Location records, or clearly identifies an unresolved mapping.
steps.healthy_condition: The recorded PickupId and DropOffId each have one identifiable associated Location record.
steps.failure_condition: The recorded result shows a missing, unexpected, or ambiguous Location relationship.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate the recorded result to L3_support when a pickup or drop-off ID does not resolve or resolves unexpectedly.
Do not modify IDs or database relationships.

actions.label: Record mapping result
actions.exact_action: Record the matched location IDs and the associated hospital station or location records.

title: Check Hospital Tag Variable Types and Stored Values in the WCS Database
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database to inspect HospitalTag records. Verify TagTypeParent, TagTypeChild, TagPath, VariableType, the applicable typed value field, and Disabled state for a hospital or PLC tag.
when_to_use: Use this WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when validating how a hospital-controller or PLC tag is represented in the Sorter Sweeper HospitalTag model, especially when the observed tag value, type, or communication path is in question.
not_for: Do not use this read-only check to change database configuration or tag definitions.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for confirming an active hospital or PLC communication path when the record is Disabled.

steps.title: Open the HospitalTag model in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view, open the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the HospitalTag / Hospital Tags Model records. Inspect the fields TagTypeParent, TagTypeChild, TagPath, VariableType, StringValue, IntValue, UintValue, BoolValue, Date_Time, and Disabled.
steps.purpose: Access the live Sorter Sweeper tag records that define hospital-controller and PLC tag communication.
steps.expected_result: A HospitalTag record or set of records is visible with the named tag-definition and typed-value fields.
steps.healthy_condition: The HospitalTag model is available and the fields required for identifying the tag and its stored value can be inspected.
steps.failure_condition: The HospitalTag model or required fields cannot be located in the Sorter Sweeper Database.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3_support if the HospitalTag record or required fields are missing.

actions.label: Inspect HospitalTag records
actions.exact_action: Locate the HospitalTag / Hospital Tags Model records in the Sorter Sweeper Database and inspect the named fields.

steps.title: Identify the tag type and WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) TagPath
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) HospitalTag record, inspect TagTypeParent and TagTypeChild. Confirm that TagPath identifies the associated hospital controller or PLC tag. TagTypeParent indicates whether the tag is an input or output.
steps.purpose: Confirm which hospital or PLC tag the database record represents and how its parent and child tag types are classified.
steps.expected_result: The record shows identifiable TagTypeParent and TagTypeChild values and a TagPath associated with the expected hospital controller or PLC tag.
steps.healthy_condition: TagPath identifies the expected hospital or PLC tag, and the parent and child type fields are populated or otherwise observable.
steps.failure_condition: TagPath is missing or does not identify the expected hospital or PLC tag, or the tag type fields cannot be interpreted from the record.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if TagPath does not identify the expected hospital or PLC tag.

actions.label: Inspect tag identity
actions.exact_action: Inspect TagTypeParent, TagTypeChild, and TagPath for the selected HospitalTag record.

steps.title: Determine the typed value field in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: Inspect VariableType in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) HospitalTag record. Use the indicated type to determine whether the applicable value is stored in StringValue, IntValue, UintValue, BoolValue, or Date_Time.
steps.purpose: Use VariableType to identify which stored value column contains the tag value.
steps.expected_result: VariableType identifies the value representation and points to the corresponding typed value field.
steps.healthy_condition: VariableType is present and its associated value field can be identified among StringValue, IntValue, UintValue, BoolValue, and Date_Time.
steps.failure_condition: VariableType is missing, cannot be interpreted, or does not identify an applicable typed value field.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if VariableType does not identify or align with an applicable value field.

actions.label: Inspect VariableType
actions.exact_action: Inspect VariableType and determine the corresponding typed value field.

steps.title: Compare the stored value with VariableType in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: Inspect the value field associated with VariableType in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) record. Compare the observed value with VariableType. Treat unrelated value fields that are NULL as unused fields for that record when the selected typed value field contains the tag value.
steps.purpose: Verify that the live tag value is stored in the field selected by VariableType rather than being read from an unrelated value column.
steps.expected_result: The applicable typed value field contains the observed tag value, while unrelated value fields may be NULL.
steps.healthy_condition: The populated value field matches VariableType; for example, the record examples show StringValue values such as `00000336` or `CloseOut`, IntValue values such as `0`, and BoolValue-associated records with the other typed fields NULL.
steps.failure_condition: The value is populated in a field that does not correspond to VariableType, or no applicable value field contains the tag value.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if VariableType and the populated value field do not align.

actions.label: Inspect the applicable value
actions.exact_action: Inspect the value field selected by VariableType and compare the stored value with the record's VariableType.

steps.title: Inspect Disabled state and record the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) observation
steps.instruction: Inspect Disabled in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) HospitalTag record. Record the observed Disabled state together with TagPath, VariableType, and the value in the applicable typed field.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the tag is enabled for the expected communication path and preserve the diagnostic observation.
steps.expected_result: Disabled is observable, and the diagnostic record contains the tag path, variable type, applicable stored value, and disabled state.
steps.healthy_condition: The tag is not Disabled when an active hospital or PLC communication path is required, and its TagPath, VariableType, and applicable value field are identifiable.
steps.failure_condition: The tag is Disabled when an active hospital or PLC communication path is required, or the required identifying and value fields cannot be recorded.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the tag is Disabled when an active hospital or PLC communication path is required.
Do not change database configuration as part of this check.

actions.label: Inspect Disabled state
actions.exact_action: Inspect Disabled and record the observed value, type, tag path, applicable stored value, and tag state.

title: Check Ignition Gateway OPC Connections status for tipper OPC endpoints
summary: Use the Ignition Gateway UI to check the current OPC Connections status for specific tipper endpoints. Confirm whether the expected tipper entries show “Faulted” (example: tipper 7 and 8 powered off show “Faulted”).
when_to_use: When you need to verify whether Ignition Gateway shows expected tipper OPC connections as healthy vs “Faulted” for specific tippers (example tippers: 7 and 8).

steps.title: Open Ignition Gateway and navigate to Config > OPC > OPC Connections
steps.instruction: In the Ignition Gateway UI, navigate to Config > OPC > OPC Connections.
steps.purpose: Reach the live Ignition Gateway page that lists current OPC connections for tipper endpoints.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition Gateway OPC Connections page is open and shows a connections list where tipper entries can be located.
steps.healthy_condition: The page loads and the connections list is visible for the tipper entries you intend to check.
steps.failure_condition: The OPC Connections page does not load or the connections list is not visible.

actions.label: Navigate to OPC Connections
actions.exact_action: Under Config, OPC, OPC Connections you can view the current connections.

steps.title: Locate the relevant tipper entries (example: tipper 7 and tipper 8) in the OPC Connections list
steps.instruction: In the OPC Connections list, locate the entries for the relevant tippers (example shown: tipper 7 and tipper 8).
steps.purpose: Identify the specific OPC connection rows corresponding to the tipper endpoints you are validating.
steps.expected_result: You can see the connections list rows for the selected tipper entries (e.g., tipper 7 and tipper 8).
steps.healthy_condition: The tipper entries appear in the connections list and are readable.
steps.failure_condition: The expected tipper entries are missing from the connections list.

actions.label: Find tipper rows
actions.exact_action: Locate the entries for the relevant tippers (example in source: tipper 7 and tipper 8).

steps.title: Verify the connection status value for each selected tipper entry
steps.instruction: For each located tipper entry, observe the connection status value shown in the list (example status shown: “Faulted” for tipper 7 and tipper 8).
steps.purpose: Determine whether Ignition Gateway reports the tipper OPC connections as healthy vs “Faulted”.
steps.expected_result: The selected tipper entries show the connection status value as displayed in the OPC Connections list (example: “Faulted”).
steps.healthy_condition: If the tipper is powered off (as in the example), its OPC connection status shows “Faulted”.
steps.failure_condition: The status does not match the expected relationship described in the example (e.g., a powered-off tipper is not showing “Faulted”, or a powered-on tipper is showing “Faulted”).
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2_support if the OPC connection status does not match the observed physical state (e.g., a powered-off tipper is not showing “Faulted”, or a powered-on tipper is showing “Faulted”).

actions.label: Read status
actions.exact_action: Observe the connection status value shown in the list (example in source: “Faulted”).

steps.title: Compare Ignition Gateway OPC status to the expected powered-off vs “Faulted” example
steps.instruction: Compare what you observe in the OPC Connections list to the example expectation: if the tipper is powered off, its OPC connection status is shown as “Faulted”.
steps.purpose: Make the pass/fail determination based on the explicit example expectation provided in the source.
steps.expected_result: You determine whether the observed status aligns with the expected powered-off → “Faulted” relationship from the example.

actions.label: Navigate to OPC Connections

steps.title: Review the displayed OPC connection states
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway Config > OPC > OPC Connections list, review the displayed status for the relevant connections and distinguish Connected from Faulted.

title: Check Tipper Active Communications in Ignition Gateway
summary: Use the Ignition gateway web UI to inspect Configuration > Active Communications and verify the displayed power and fault state for Tipper 7 and Tipper 8.
when_to_use: Use this Ignition gateway diagnostic when investigating whether the live communications for Tipper 7 or Tipper 8 are powered on and communicating, or when the gateway communications state needs to be verified.
not_for: Do not use this runbook as a corrective-action or communication-restart procedure; the source does not provide a restart or repair procedure.
Do not use this runbook to establish healthy-state thresholds; the source only provides the displayed power and fault states.

steps.title: Open the Ignition gateway performance page
steps.instruction: In a web browser, open the Ignition gateway at http://localhost:8088/web/status/sys.perf.
steps.purpose: Reach the live Ignition gateway UI used to inspect gateway and tipper communication status.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition gateway system performance page opens and displays the gateway UI, including its performance and configuration areas.
steps.healthy_condition: The Ignition gateway system performance page is reachable and its UI loads.
steps.failure_condition: The Ignition gateway UI or system performance page cannot be opened.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Ignition gateway UI cannot be opened.

actions.label: Open Ignition gateway
actions.exact_action: Open http://localhost:8088/web/status/sys.perf in a web browser.

steps.title: Open Active Communications in the Ignition gateway
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway UI, open Configuration and then select Active Communications.
steps.purpose: Navigate to the live Ignition gateway view that exposes the tipper communication status.
steps.expected_result: The Active Communications view opens and displays communication entries that can be inspected for the tippers.
steps.healthy_condition: The Active Communications view is available and displays the communication entries.
steps.failure_condition: The Active Communications view cannot be opened or the relevant communication entries are not displayed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Active Communications view cannot be opened.

actions.label: Open Active Communications
actions.exact_action: Select Configuration > Active Communications in the Ignition gateway UI.

steps.title: Inspect Tipper 7 and Tipper 8 communication states
steps.instruction: In Ignition gateway Active Communications, locate the entries for Tipper 7 and Tipper 8 and observe each entry's displayed power and fault state.
steps.purpose: Determine whether either tipper communication is displayed as powered off or faulted in the live Ignition gateway.
steps.expected_result: A displayed state is available for both Tipper 7 and Tipper 8. The example state is powered off and faulted for both entries.
steps.healthy_condition: The Tipper 7 and Tipper 8 entries are displayed in the Active Communications view without the powered-off and faulted condition described in the source.
steps.failure_condition: Either Tipper 7 or Tipper 8 is displayed as powered off and faulted.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when Tipper 7 or Tipper 8 is displayed as powered off and faulted.

actions.label: Inspect Tipper 7
actions.exact_action: Locate the Tipper 7 communication entry and observe its displayed power and fault state.

actions.label: Inspect Tipper 8
actions.exact_action: Locate the Tipper 8 communication entry and observe its displayed power and fault state.

steps.title: Record the displayed tipper states
steps.instruction: Record the displayed power and fault state for Tipper 7 and Tipper 8 from the Ignition gateway Active Communications view.
steps.purpose: Preserve the observed live status for further support investigation.
steps.expected_result: The recorded observation identifies the state of each tipper communication, including whether it is powered off and displayed as faulted.
steps.healthy_condition: The recorded state for each tipper does not show the powered-off and faulted condition.
steps.failure_condition: The recorded state for either tipper shows powered off and faulted, or the state cannot be determined from the Ignition gateway view.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when Tipper 7 or Tipper 8 is recorded as powered off and faulted.
Escalate if the state of either tipper cannot be determined.

actions.label: Record communication states
actions.exact_action: Record whether each tipper communication is powered off and displayed as faulted.

title: Inspect Ignition Lane Activity Records in the WCS / Helix DB
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of [dbo].[IgnitionLaneActivityMode] with the SNAPSHOT qualifier to inspect lane activity, package identifiers, measurements, classification, message values, and missing-dimension fields for lane or package troubleshooting.
when_to_use: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) for read-only troubleshooting when a lane or package requires inspection of Ignition lane activity, sorter and lane identity, package measurements, message status, classification, or missing-dimension data.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database records, issue corrective commands, reboot dimensioners, or perform physical equipment actions.
Do not use the displayed NewSort, SortConf, null, dash-valued, or numeric fields as a definitive fault interpretation without an established operational meaning or L3 review.

steps.title: Open the Ignition lane activity view
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the read-only query or view for [dbo].[IgnitionLaneActivityMode] with the SNAPSHOT qualifier. Do not edit the object or its records.
steps.purpose: Establish a read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view of the lane activity records.
steps.expected_result: The WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid opens and identifies the [dbo].[IgnitionLaneActivityMode] object with the SNAPSHOT qualifier.
steps.healthy_condition: The read-only result grid is available and exposes the lane activity fields needed for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The object cannot be opened, the read-only result grid is unavailable, or the expected fields are not exposed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support if the named database object cannot be opened or the expected result fields are unavailable.
Stop if the available access is not read-only.

actions.label: Open read-only lane activity view
actions.exact_action: Open the read-only query or view for [dbo].[IgnitionLaneActivityMode] WITH (SNAPSHOT) in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).

steps.title: Inspect sorter and lane identity fields
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid, inspect the date or timestamp and the SorterName, SortName, SortGuid, Zone, and LaneName fields. Use the available incident time, sorter, zone, or lane information to identify the relevant records.
steps.purpose: Associate the returned records with the relevant time, sorter, zone, and lane.
steps.expected_result: The result grid provides timestamped records with displayed sorter, sort, GUID, zone, and lane-name values that can be compared with the affected lane or sorter context.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant records can be associated with the affected sorter, zone, and lane using the displayed identity fields.
steps.failure_condition: The records lack the required identity fields or cannot be associated with the affected lane or sorter.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the records cannot be associated with the affected lane or package.

actions.label: Review lane identity columns
actions.exact_action: Inspect date, SorterName, SortName, SortGuid, Zone, and LaneName in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid.

steps.title: Correlate package identifiers and measurements
steps.instruction: For the affected lane or package in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid, locate PackageUid and TrackingNumber. Compare the displayed Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube values for the associated record.
steps.purpose: Identify the affected package and inspect its displayed physical-attribute values.
steps.expected_result: The package record can be identified by PackageUid and/or TrackingNumber, and its displayed measurement fields can be compared, including populated, blank, null, or dash-valued entries.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected package is identifiable and the displayed Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube values are available for review.
steps.failure_condition: The package cannot be identified, or the measurement fields are unavailable or cannot be associated with the package record.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the affected package cannot be identified or the records cannot be associated with it.

actions.label: Review package and measurement fields
actions.exact_action: Locate PackageUid and TrackingNumber, then compare Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid.

steps.title: Review message, classification, and missing-dimension fields
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid, inspect Message, PackageClassification, and MissingDimension Data. Note displayed values such as NewSort, SortConf, numeric flags, nulls, blanks, or dash-valued fields. Treat these as observations; do not assign an operational fault meaning unless it is established by L2/L3 support.
steps.purpose: Determine what message and data-quality values are displayed for the affected lane or package.
steps.expected_result: The record shows the displayed message or status-like value, package classification, and missing-dimension data value for the affected record.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant Message, PackageClassification, and MissingDimension Data values are visible and recorded for comparison with the affected lane or package.
steps.failure_condition: The fields are unavailable, the values cannot be associated with the affected record, or their operational meaning is unknown and requires escalation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate for interpretation when NewSort, SortConf, missing-dimension, null, blank, or dash-valued fields do not have an established operational meaning.
Escalate to L3 support if the displayed pattern indicates missing dimension data but the responsible upstream condition is not established.

actions.label: Review status and data-quality fields
actions.exact_action: Inspect Message, PackageClassification, and MissingDimension Data in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) result grid.

title: Pause All AGV Movement Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API PauseAgvs operation in Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client to request that Geek pause movement for all AGVs. PauseAgvs is not an AE stop.
when_to_use: Use when support needs to request a pause of movement for all AGVs through the live OptiSweep / WCS API.
not_for: Do not use or describe PauseAgvs as an AE stop.
Do not use this procedure as a physical E-stop procedure.

steps.title: Open the PauseAgvs operation in the OptiSweep / WCS API client
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API group and locate the operation labeled POST PauseAgvs.
steps.purpose: Identify the live API operation that requests a pause of movement for all AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The AGVs API group displays the POST PauseAgvs operation and it is available for submission.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep / WCS API client is reachable and POST PauseAgvs is present under the AGVs operations.
steps.failure_condition: The API client cannot reach the OptiSweep / WCS API or the PauseAgvs operation is unavailable.
stop_or_escalate_if: The OptiSweep / WCS API client cannot be reached.
POST PauseAgvs is not available.

actions.label: Locate PauseAgvs
actions.exact_action: Open the AGVs API group and locate POST PauseAgvs.

steps.title: Submit POST PauseAgvs
steps.instruction: Submit the POST PauseAgvs request in the OptiSweep / WCS API client. Do not represent or handle this request as an AE stop.
steps.purpose: Send the software request to Geek to pause movement for all AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The POST PauseAgvs request is submitted to request that Geek pause all AGV movement.
steps.healthy_condition: The request is accepted for submission by the OptiSweep / WCS API client and the operation is treated as a pause request rather than an AE stop.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted, or the operation is being interpreted as an AE stop.
stop_or_escalate_if: The POST PauseAgvs request cannot be submitted.
The operation is being treated as an AE stop or another safety-stop function.

actions.label: Submit pause request
actions.exact_action: Submit POST PauseAgvs.

steps.title: Verify the live AGV movement state
steps.instruction: Observe the live AGV fleet status in the RMS / fleet status UI or equivalent live AGV status view after submitting PauseAgvs. Check the current AGV state, current command, vitals, and any AGV or system errors, and confirm that AGV movement is paused.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the pause request produced the intended live fleet behavior.
steps.expected_result: The live fleet observation shows that AGV movement is paused; the status view remains available for reviewing current AGV state, command, vitals, and errors.
steps.healthy_condition: AGVs are no longer moving after the PauseAgvs request, with the live fleet status view available for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: AGV movement continues after the request, or the live status view shows an AGV or system error that prevents confirmation of the paused state.
stop_or_escalate_if: AGV movement continues after the PauseAgvs request.
The live AGV state cannot be observed or the pause cannot be verified.
The status view shows an AGV error or system error associated with the request.

actions.label: Inspect live fleet state
actions.exact_action: Observe the live AGV fleet status and verify that AGV movement is paused.

title: Pause All AGV Movement Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API PauseAgvs operation in Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client to request that Geek pause movement for all AGVs. PauseAgvs is not an AE stop.
when_to_use: Use when support needs to request a pause of movement for all AGVs through the live OptiSweep / WCS API.
not_for: Do not use or describe PauseAgvs as an AE stop.
Do not use this procedure as a physical E-stop procedure.

steps.title: Open the PauseAgvs operation in the OptiSweep / WCS API client
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API group and locate the operation labeled POST PauseAgvs.
steps.purpose: Identify the live API operation that requests a pause of movement for all AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The AGVs API group displays the POST PauseAgvs operation and it is available for submission.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep / WCS API client is reachable and POST PauseAgvs is present under the AGVs operations.
steps.failure_condition: The API client cannot reach the OptiSweep / WCS API or the PauseAgvs operation is unavailable.
stop_or_escalate_if: The OptiSweep / WCS API client cannot be reached.
POST PauseAgvs is not available.

actions.label: Locate PauseAgvs
actions.exact_action: Open the AGVs API group and locate POST PauseAgvs.

steps.title: Submit POST PauseAgvs
steps.instruction: Submit the POST PauseAgvs request in the OptiSweep / WCS API client. Do not represent or handle this request as an AE stop.
steps.purpose: Send the software request to Geek to pause movement for all AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The POST PauseAgvs request is submitted to request that Geek pause all AGV movement.
steps.healthy_condition: The request is accepted for submission by the OptiSweep / WCS API client and the operation is treated as a pause request rather than an AE stop.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted, or the operation is being interpreted as an AE stop.
stop_or_escalate_if: The POST PauseAgvs request cannot be submitted.

actions.label: Submit pause request
actions.exact_action: Submit POST PauseAgvs.

steps.title: Verify the live AGV movement state
steps.instruction: Observe the live AGV fleet status in the RMS / fleet status UI or equivalent live AGV status view after submitting PauseAgvs. Check the current AGV state, current command, vitals, and any AGV or system errors, and confirm that AGV movement is paused.

steps.expected_result: The live fleet observation shows that AGV movement is paused; the status view remains available for reviewing current AGV state, command, vitals, and errors.
steps.healthy_condition: AGVs are no longer moving after the PauseAgvs request, with the live fleet status view available for inspection.
steps.failure_condition: AGV movement continues after the request, or the live status view shows an AGV or system error that prevents confirmation of the paused state.

actions.exact_action: Observe the live AGV fleet status and verify that AGV movement is paused.

title: Recover a Specified AGV Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client to submit the POST RecoverAgv operation with a confirmed robot ID. RecoverAgv requests Geek to add the specified AGV back into the system. Verify the result with the Get Agv Statuses request.
when_to_use: Use when a specified AGV must be added back into the OptiSweep system through the Geek Plus recovery path and a confirmed robot ID is available.
not_for: Do not use without a confirmed robot ID.
Do not use as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.
Do not use to infer success from request submission alone; verify the AGV in Get Agv Statuses.

steps.title: Open the RecoverAgv operation in Apidog
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API group and locate the POST RecoverAgv operation.
steps.purpose: Select the live OptiSweep / WCS API operation used to request that Geek add the specified AGV back into the system.
steps.expected_result: The AGVs API list displays the POST RecoverAgv operation and it is available for submission.
steps.healthy_condition: The POST RecoverAgv operation is visible in the AGVs API group.
steps.failure_condition: The AGVs API group or POST RecoverAgv operation is unavailable, or the request cannot be opened for submission.
stop_or_escalate_if: The POST RecoverAgv operation is not available.
The API client cannot open or submit the operation.

actions.label: Locate RecoverAgv
actions.exact_action: Locate the AGVs API operation labeled POST RecoverAgv.

steps.title: Enter the confirmed robot ID
steps.instruction: In the POST RecoverAgv request in the Apidog / WCS API client, provide the confirmed robot ID for the specified AGV.
steps.purpose: Identify the specific AGV that the RecoverAgv request will add back into the system.
steps.expected_result: The RecoverAgv request contains the robot ID for the intended AGV and is ready for submission.
steps.healthy_condition: The robot ID is present and has been confirmed as belonging to the intended AGV.
steps.failure_condition: The robot ID is missing, unconfirmed, or does not identify the intended AGV.
stop_or_escalate_if: The robot ID cannot be confirmed.
The request does not provide a way to specify the robot ID.

actions.label: Confirm robot ID
actions.exact_action: Provide the robot ID required by RecoverAgv.

steps.title: Submit the POST RecoverAgv request
steps.instruction: Submit the POST RecoverAgv request in the Apidog / WCS API client after confirming that the intended robot ID is present.
steps.purpose: Send the recovery request through the OptiSweep / WCS API to request that Geek add the specified AGV to the system.
steps.expected_result: The POST RecoverAgv request is submitted for the specified robot ID.
steps.healthy_condition: The WCS API client accepts the request for submission without a client-side submission failure.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted or the API client reports a submission failure.
stop_or_escalate_if: The request cannot be submitted.
The robot ID is not confirmed before submission.

actions.label: Submit recovery request
actions.exact_action: Submit the POST RecoverAgv request.

steps.title: Verify the AGV in Get Agv Statuses
steps.instruction: Use the GET Get Agv Statuses operation in the Apidog / WCS API client and inspect the returned AGV entries for the specified robot ID. Review the returned name, state, command status, battery, status, errorCode, errorDescription, errorCause, systemErrorDescription, systemErrorResolution, and errorAlert fields when present.
steps.purpose: Confirm in live WCS API state that the specified AGV is represented again after the recovery request.
steps.expected_result: The returned AGV status data contains an entry for the specified robot ID, representing the AGV again in the system state.
steps.healthy_condition: The specified robot ID is present in Get Agv Statuses and the returned status does not indicate an active error for that AGV, such as errorAlert true or populated error fields.
steps.failure_condition: The specified robot ID is absent from Get Agv Statuses, or the returned AGV data indicates an error state that prevents confirmation of recovery.
stop_or_escalate_if: The specified AGV does not reappear in the returned system state.
The returned status shows an AGV error or system error that is not resolved by the recovery request.

actions.label: Request AGV statuses
actions.exact_action: Use GET Get Agv Statuses to show the current state of AGVs.

actions.label: Check specified robot
actions.exact_action: Inspect the returned AGV status data for the specified robot ID.

title: Remove a Specified AGV Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API RemoveAgv operation in Apidog or an equivalent API client to request removal of one specified AGV from the system through Geek. The request requires the AGV's robot ID and must be verified using the AGV status response.
when_to_use: Use when an identified AGV must be removed from the OptiSweep system through the live OptiSweep / WCS API and the robot ID is confirmed.

steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVS operation group and locate the POST RemoveAgv operation.
steps.purpose: Identify the live OptiSweep / WCS API operation used to request removal of one AGV.
steps.expected_result: The AGVS operation list displays POST RemoveAgv and the request can be opened for input.
steps.healthy_condition: POST RemoveAgv is visible under AGVS and the API client is ready to accept the request input.
steps.failure_condition: The AGVS operation group or POST RemoveAgv is unavailable, or the API client cannot be opened.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the OptiSweep / WCS API client cannot be accessed.

steps.healthy_condition: The entered robot ID identifies the specified AGV and is ready for submission.

steps.purpose: Send the removal request for the specified AGV through the live OptiSweep / WCS API.

steps.purpose: Confirm from live AGV system state that the specified robot is no longer represented as an active AGV.
steps.expected_result: The specified robot is no longer represented as an active AGV in the returned system state, or its returned state/status indicates removal.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the specified AGV remains present after the request.

title: Resend an AGV Command to Geek+ Using the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog to resubmit a Geek+ AGV request when the command GUID is available, then review GET command status for the associated main GUID. This is useful after an unplanned restart when Geek+ may have missed the request.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV command request may have been missed by Geek+ after an unplanned restart and a command GUID is available from the command database model or command status data.
not_for: Do not use when the required command GUID is unavailable.
Do not use as a physical AGV recovery or E-stop procedure.
Do not treat execution of the resend request as confirmation that Geek+ completed the command; the packet does not provide completion confirmation.

steps.title: Open the Resend Geek Command request in Apidog
steps.instruction: On the primary server, open Apidog / WCS API client and select the AGV request labeled "Resend Geek Command". Confirm that the related GET Get Agv Statuses request is available for status review.
steps.purpose: Access the live OptiSweep / WCS API request used to resubmit an AGV command to Geek+.
steps.expected_result: The Apidog AGV request list displays POST Resend Geek Command and GET Get Agv Statuses.
steps.healthy_condition: The Resend Geek Command request is available in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.failure_condition: The required API request is unavailable or the OptiSweep / WCS API client cannot be accessed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if Apidog or the OptiSweep / WCS API cannot be accessed.
Escalate if the Resend Geek Command request is not available.

actions.label: Open AGV API requests
actions.exact_action: Select the AGV request labeled "Resend Geek Command" in Apidog.

steps.title: Obtain and verify the command GUID
steps.instruction: Review the command database model or AGV command status data in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) or the OptiSweep / WCS API. Locate the command GUID associated with the command. Confirm that the command GUID is present before continuing.
steps.purpose: Ensure the resend request has the identifier required to resubmit the AGV command.
steps.expected_result: A command GUID is present for the AGV command selected for resend.
steps.healthy_condition: The command data exposes a non-missing command GUID that can be supplied to Resend Geek Command.
steps.failure_condition: The command GUID is missing or cannot be associated with the command being recovered.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the required command GUID is unavailable.
Escalate if the command data cannot identify the command GUID.

actions.label: Inspect command data

steps.title: Submit Resend Geek Command

steps.purpose: Resubmit the identified AGV command request to Geek+.
steps.expected_result: The Resend Geek Command request executes with the required command GUID and resends the request to Geek+.
steps.healthy_condition: The API client shows that the Resend Geek Command request was executed using the verified command GUID.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be executed, or the required command GUID is not accepted or available.
stop_or_escalate_if: Do not proceed if the command GUID is missing.
Escalate if the resend request cannot be executed.

actions.label: Resend the Geek+ command
actions.exact_action: Provide the command GUID to the "Resend Geek Command" request and execute the request.

steps.expected_result: GET command status exposes the associated main GUID for the command.
steps.healthy_condition: The command status response contains the expected main GUID field or value associated with the resent command.
steps.failure_condition: GET command status does not expose the expected main GUID, or the command status cannot be retrieved.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if GET command status does not expose the expected main GUID.
Escalate if command status cannot be retrieved after the resend request.

actions.label: Review command status
actions.exact_action: Open or review GET command status information and check for the associated main GUID.

title: Restart the OptiSweep Windows Service in Windows Services After Flatlined Tipper Heartbeats in the Ignition Gateway
summary: Use the Ignition gateway to verify that a tipper heartbeat is flat-lined, then use Windows Services to locate and restart the OptiSweep service. Confirm that the service returns to Running and that the Ignition gateway heartbeat is no longer flat-lined.
when_to_use: Use this Ignition gateway and Windows Services procedure when a live tipper heartbeat is flat-lined or missing, including after an unplanned restart where Ignition may have started later than WCS and the OptiSweep service did not reestablish OPC-related heartbeat communication.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a general database, API, or broader system restart procedure.
Do not use it when a flat-lined or missing tipper heartbeat has not been verified in the Ignition gateway.

steps.title: Check the tipper heartbeat in the Ignition gateway
steps.instruction: In the Ignition gateway, inspect the live heartbeat indication for the affected tipper and determine whether heartbeat communication is being received or is flat-lined.
steps.purpose: Verify that the recovery trigger is present before restarting the OptiSweep service.
steps.expected_result: The affected tipper's live heartbeat indication is identified as either active or flat-lined, providing the basis for the service-restart decision.
steps.healthy_condition: The tipper heartbeat indication is not flat-lined and heartbeat communication is being received.
steps.failure_condition: The tipper heartbeat indication is flat-lined or heartbeat communication is not being received.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the heartbeat is not flat-lined, do not perform this service-restart procedure.
If the affected tipper or heartbeat indication cannot be identified in the Ignition gateway, escalate for L2 support.

actions.label: Inspect tipper heartbeat
actions.exact_action: Check to make sure that tippers are getting heartbeats.

steps.title: Locate OptiSweep in Windows Services
steps.instruction: Open Windows Services MMC, locate the service named "OptiSweep," and review its Status.
steps.purpose: Confirm the Windows service entry and inspect its current status before restarting it.
steps.expected_result: The Windows Services console displays the OptiSweep service entry and its current Status.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep entry is present and its Status is Running.
steps.failure_condition: The OptiSweep entry is absent, or its Status is not Running.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the OptiSweep service cannot be located, escalate to L2 support.
If Windows Services cannot be opened or the service status cannot be read, escalate to L2 support.

actions.label: Inspect OptiSweep service
actions.exact_action: Locate the service named "OptiSweep" and review its Status.

steps.title: Restart the OptiSweep service in Windows Services
steps.instruction: In Windows Services, use the OptiSweep service's "Restart the service" control.
steps.purpose: Reestablish the OptiSweep service path associated with the flat-lined tipper heartbeat.
steps.expected_result: Windows Services accepts the restart request for the OptiSweep service.
steps.healthy_condition: The restart action completes without an error and the service can be observed returning to an operational state.
steps.failure_condition: The restart control is unavailable, the restart request fails, or the service does not return to an operational state.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the OptiSweep service cannot be restarted.
Escalate if the restart request reports an error.

actions.label: Restart OptiSweep
actions.exact_action: Use the Windows Services "Restart the service" control for the OptiSweep service.

steps.title: Confirm service state and tipper heartbeat recovery
steps.instruction: In Windows Services, verify that the OptiSweep service returns to a Running state. Then return to the Ignition gateway and recheck the affected tipper's live heartbeat indication.
steps.purpose: Verify recovery on both the Windows Services and Ignition gateway surfaces.
steps.expected_result: The OptiSweep service shows Running and the affected tipper heartbeat is no longer flat-lined.
steps.healthy_condition: Windows Services shows OptiSweep as Running, and the Ignition gateway shows heartbeat communication for the affected tipper.
steps.failure_condition: OptiSweep does not return to Running, or the tipper heartbeat remains flat-lined after the restart.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the OptiSweep service does not return to Running.
Escalate if the tipper heartbeat remains flat-lined after the service restart.

actions.label: Verify service state
actions.exact_action: Verify that the OptiSweep service returns to a Running state.

actions.label: Recheck tipper heartbeat
actions.exact_action: Recheck the tipper heartbeat in the Ignition gateway for a non-flat-lined indication.

title: Resume All AGV Movement Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client to submit the POST ResumeAgvs operation, which requests Geek to resume movement for all paused AGVs. Verify the resulting fleet state through the WCS API AGV status view.
when_to_use: Use when all AGV movement was paused through the OptiSweep / WCS API and movement needs to be resumed through the live WCS API surface.
not_for: Do not use ResumeAgvs as a physical E-stop reset.
Do not use this procedure for physical AGV recovery or physical safety-stop reset.

steps.title: Locate ResumeAgvs in the OptiSweep / WCS API
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API operations and locate the operation labeled POST ResumeAgvs.
steps.purpose: Identify the live API operation that requests Geek to resume movement for all paused AGVs.
steps.expected_result: The AGVs API list displays POST ResumeAgvs and identifies it as the operation that requests Geek to resume all AGV movement.
steps.healthy_condition: The intended operation is clearly identified as POST ResumeAgvs under the AGVs API operations.
steps.failure_condition: POST ResumeAgvs is unavailable, cannot be located, or the WCS API client cannot display the AGVs operations.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the WCS API client cannot display or locate POST ResumeAgvs.

actions.label: Open AGVs API operations
actions.exact_action: Open the AGVs API operations in Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client.

actions.label: Locate ResumeAgvs
actions.exact_action: Locate the operation labeled POST ResumeAgvs.

steps.title: Submit the POST ResumeAgvs request
steps.instruction: Submit the POST ResumeAgvs request in Apidog or the equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.purpose: Send the live WCS API request to Geek to resume movement for the paused AGV fleet.
steps.expected_result: The POST ResumeAgvs request is submitted to request that Geek resume all AGV movement.
steps.healthy_condition: The WCS API client accepts and submits the POST ResumeAgvs request without a submission failure.
steps.failure_condition: The request cannot be submitted or the WCS API client reports a submission failure.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the POST ResumeAgvs request cannot be submitted.

actions.label: Submit ResumeAgvs
actions.exact_action: Submit the POST ResumeAgvs request.

steps.title: Verify the live AGV fleet state
steps.instruction: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API AGV status view, including Get Agv Statuses, and observe the current AGV state, command, commandStatus, status, errorCode, errorDescription, errorCause, systemErrorDescription, systemErrorResolution, and errorAlert. Confirm through the available live fleet observation that AGV movement has resumed.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the resume request produced the intended live fleet behavior.
steps.expected_result: The live AGV status view reflects resumed movement for the previously paused fleet and provides current AGV state and error information for verification.
steps.healthy_condition: AGV status data is available, AGVs are no longer remaining paused, and the live status view does not show an active AGV or system error preventing movement. The status view can include fields such as state, commandName, commandStatus, status, errorCode, errorDescription, and errorAlert.
steps.failure_condition: AGV movement remains paused, the status view shows an active AGV or system error, or current AGV status cannot be retrieved.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if AGV movement remains paused after the ResumeAgvs request.
Stop and escalate if current AGV status cannot be retrieved.
Stop and escalate if the live status view shows an active AGV or system error preventing movement.

actions.label: Retrieve AGV statuses
actions.exact_action: Use GET Get Agv Statuses in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.

actions.label: Observe fleet movement
actions.exact_action: Observe the live AGV fleet state and verify that AGV movement resumes.

steps.title: Open the RMS / fleet status UI
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui).
steps.purpose: Start the health check by accessing the RMS fleet status page.

steps.failure_condition: The RMS page is blank, fails to load, or appears unreachable.

title: Check RMS Map Monitor for System Emergency-Stop Status
summary: Use the RMS / fleet status UI Map Monitor to inspect the live system emergency-stop message, fleet Total and Exception counts, and the Robot Info fields associated with a selected robot.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic on the RMS / fleet status UI when verifying whether the live fleet is reporting a system emergency-stop state and when identifying the robot status information associated with that display.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to clear, reset, or otherwise change an emergency-stop state.
Do not use this procedure as a physical emergency-stop response or as a recovery procedure.

steps.title: Open the RMS Map Monitor
steps.instruction: Open the RMS / fleet status UI and navigate to the Map Monitor page. Confirm that the robot map, Message Panel, and robot status area are displayed.
steps.purpose: Open the live RMS / fleet status UI page that exposes the fleet map, messages, and robot status information.
steps.expected_result: The RMS Map Monitor page is available and displays the robot map with the fleet monitoring and robot information areas.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS Map Monitor loads and the map, Message Panel, and robot status area can be inspected.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS Map Monitor is unavailable or the robot and fleet information cannot be confirmed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The RMS Map Monitor is unavailable.
The displayed robot or fleet information cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Open Map Monitor
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI and navigate to the Map Monitor page.

steps.title: Inspect fleet Total and Exception counts
steps.instruction: On the RMS Map Monitor, inspect the fleet summary and note the displayed Total and Exception counts. The captured RMS screen shows Total 34 and Exception 0; use the values currently displayed in the live RMS session rather than assuming those captured values remain current.
steps.purpose: Determine the current fleet size and whether the RMS fleet summary reports exceptions.
steps.expected_result: The current RMS fleet Total and Exception values are visible and can be used to characterize the displayed fleet state.
steps.healthy_condition: The Total and Exception fields are visible and the current Exception count does not indicate a robot exception.
steps.failure_condition: The Exception count indicates one or more exceptions, or the Total or Exception fields are unavailable or cannot be confirmed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The Exception count indicates a robot exception.
The Total or Exception values cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Inspect fleet summary
actions.exact_action: Check the fleet summary for the displayed Total and Exception counts.

steps.title: Check the system emergency-stop message
steps.instruction: Inspect the RMS Map Monitor Message Panel and message area for the exact status text "Currently in system emergency stop state."
steps.purpose: Determine whether the live RMS Map Monitor is reporting a system emergency-stop state.
steps.expected_result: The operator can determine whether the RMS Message Panel currently displays the system emergency-stop status.
steps.healthy_condition: The exact system emergency-stop message is not displayed in the current RMS Message Panel.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS Map Monitor displays "Currently in system emergency stop state."
stop_or_escalate_if: The RMS Map Monitor displays "Currently in system emergency stop state."
The Message Panel or displayed status cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Inspect emergency-stop message
actions.exact_action: Check whether the Map Monitor displays the message "Currently in system emergency stop state."

steps.title: Review the selected robot status fields
steps.instruction: When an affected robot entry is present in the RMS Map Monitor, select it and review the Robot Info panel. Inspect Robot ID, Type, Node Code, Path Mode, Location, Exception status, and Robot Task information. The captured screen includes Robot ID 1555125, Type P40-V2, Node Code 11001075, Path Mode IDLE, Location, Exception status, and Robot Task details; use the values currently displayed for the selected robot.
steps.purpose: Associate the displayed system or exception state with the affected robot's live RMS status details.
steps.expected_result: The selected robot's identifying, location, exception, path, and task fields are visible and can be associated with the RMS emergency-stop or exception display.
steps.healthy_condition: The selected robot's Robot ID, Type, Node Code, Path Mode, Location, Exception status, and Robot Task fields are available for inspection, with no unaccounted exception shown.
steps.failure_condition: The selected robot shows an exception or emergency-stop-related status, or the required Robot Info fields are unavailable or cannot be confirmed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The selected robot has an exception or emergency-stop-related status.
The Robot Info fields or associated task information cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Select affected robot
actions.exact_action: Select the affected robot entry, when present, and review the displayed Robot ID, Type, Node Code, Path Mode, Location, Exception status, and task information.
