title: Diagnose AGV Robot Command State in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) in read-only mode to trace an AGV command through the Robotics Database RobotCommandDatabaseModel active-command table and Robot Command Activity history. Review command identity, status, robot, container, station, location, parameters, and lifecycle timing fields to determine whether the command was sent, started, completed, errored, or cancelled.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic on the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) when support needs to verify the lifecycle of an AGV command requested by the Robotics module, including whether an active command is Sent or InProgress, whether it has been archived, or whether it has an errored or cancelled status.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database records, resubmit commands, remove or recover an AGV, restart services, or issue other command changes.
Do not use this procedure as a replacement for physical AGV recovery or safety actions.

steps.title: Open the active command table in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open the OptiSweep Robotics database and locate the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table. Review the active command rows and the command/status columns.
steps.purpose: Establish whether the command is currently active and identify the lifecycle fields available for inspection.
steps.expected_result: The live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) view shows active robot commands requested by the Robotics module, with fields including CommandGuid, CommandName, Status, RobotCode, Parameters, Sent Time, InProgress Time, and Executed Time.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant command is present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel with identifiable command and robot information and lifecycle fields available for review.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database or RobotCommandDatabaseModel table cannot be accessed, or the active command table does not contain the expected command record.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3_support if the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) or Robotics database cannot be accessed.
Escalate if the relevant command cannot be located in the active table after checking the available command identifiers.

actions.label: Open active command records
actions.exact_action: Open the OptiSweep WCS / Helix Robotics database and locate the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table.

steps.title: Identify the command in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) RobotCommandDatabaseModel table, find the relevant row using the command name, RobotCode, CommandGuid, container or station parameters. For a Move Tote command, compare the ContainerId and StationId values in Parameters with the reported movement.
steps.purpose: Match the reported AGV activity to the correct active command record.
steps.expected_result: One active RobotCommandDatabaseModel row is matched to the reported AGV command using command identity and parameter values.
steps.healthy_condition: The matched row has a consistent CommandName, RobotCode, and relevant container or station parameter values.
steps.failure_condition: Multiple records cannot be distinguished, the identifiers do not match the reported command, or no active record matches the command details.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the command cannot be uniquely matched using the available command name, RobotCode, CommandGuid, container, station, or parameter values.

actions.label: Match command identifiers
actions.exact_action: Find the relevant command using the command name, RobotCode, container or station parameters.

steps.title: Interpret command status and lifecycle timing in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the matched WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) row, review Status, Sent Time, InProgress Time, and Executed Time. A Sent command may have InProgress Time and Executed Time as NULL. An InProgress command has an InProgress Time while Executed Time remains NULL until the command is finalized.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the command was sent, progressed to execution, or remains active without expected progression.
steps.expected_result: The live row provides an observable lifecycle state through Status and the presence or absence of Sent Time, InProgress Time, and Executed Time.
steps.healthy_condition: A command in Sent state has a Sent Time and may have NULL InProgress Time and Executed Time; a command in InProgress state has an InProgress Time and may still have NULL Executed Time.
steps.failure_condition: The command has an errored or cancelled Status, or remains active with only Sent Time and no expected InProgress Time evidence for the operational situation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the database diagnostic and escalate to L2/L3 support if Status is errored or cancelled.
Escalate if the command remains active without the expected InProgress or Executed Time evidence.

actions.label: Review lifecycle fields
actions.exact_action: Check the Status value and timing fields.

steps.title: Check AGV location fields in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robotics data, review the matched command's related robot location information, including CurrentLocationId and DestinationLocationId when available. Compare the location state with the command's station or destination parameters.
steps.purpose: Correlate command progression with the AGV's current and destination location state when location or queue capacity is relevant.
steps.expected_result: The live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) data shows the AGV's current location and destination location in relation to the command being diagnosed.
steps.healthy_condition: CurrentLocationId and DestinationLocationId are present and consistent with the command's station or destination; the observed location state does not contradict the command lifecycle.
steps.failure_condition: Location fields are missing, inconsistent with the command's station or destination, or indicate that the command remains associated with a queue or location without expected progression.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if current or destination location data conflicts with the command parameters or indicates a stuck command.

actions.label: Review robot locations
actions.exact_action: Check the command's current and destination location information in the robot database model when location state is relevant.

steps.title: Review finalized command history in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
steps.instruction: If the command is no longer active in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) RobotCommandDatabaseModel table, locate the corresponding record in Robot Command Activity. Review the command name, status, robot name, container, station, parameters, Sent Time, InProgress Time, Executed Time, station circuit, and total time.
steps.purpose: Determine the final outcome and execution timing when the command is no longer present in the active table.
steps.expected_result: The live Robot Command Activity record provides the historical status and execution/timing information for the finalized command.
steps.healthy_condition: A completed command is absent from the active RobotCommandDatabaseModel table and is present in Robot Command Activity with a completed status and applicable execution and timing fields.
steps.failure_condition: The command is absent from both the active RobotCommandDatabaseModel table and Robot Command Activity, or its historical record has an errored or cancelled status.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the command cannot be located in either the active RobotCommandDatabaseModel table or Robot Command Activity history.
Escalate if the historical status is errored or cancelled.

actions.label: Review command history
actions.exact_action: If the command is no longer active, locate the corresponding record in Robot Command Activity and review the command name, status, robot name, container, station, parameters, Sent Time, InProgress Time, Executed Time, station circuit, and total time fields.

title: Check Robot Command Database Model Table for Active Robot Command Status (Sent → In Progress → Archived)
summary: Use WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to verify whether a robot command is still active in RobotCommandDatabaseModel, whether it progressed from sent to in-progress, and whether completed commands have been archived to robot command activity (historical record).
when_to_use: When you need to confirm the lifecycle evidence of a specific robot command for an AGV (sent vs in-progress vs completed/archived) using the active transactional table and the archived historical record.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the primary method to resolve physical safety issues (use on-site physical safety procedures instead).
Do not use this procedure when you only need to view AGV faults/errors without checking command lifecycle evidence (use the appropriate active error/fault procedure instead).

steps.title: Connect to WCS / Helix DB in SSMS (read-only)
steps.instruction: Open SSMS and connect to the WCS / Helix DB read-only environment.
steps.purpose: Access the WCS / Helix DB environment where RobotCommandDatabaseModel and the archived robot command activity record are stored.
steps.expected_result: SSMS is connected to the WCS / Helix DB environment and ready to browse databases/tables.
steps.healthy_condition: You can view the database list and expand the relevant WCS/OptiSweep database(s) in Object Explorer.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot connect to the WCS / Helix DB environment or cannot view the database list.

actions.label: Connect to SSMS WCS/Helix DB
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and connect to the WCS / Helix DB read-only environment.

steps.title: Open the WCS/OptiSweep database containing RobotCommandDatabaseModel
steps.instruction: In the database list, open the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table.
steps.purpose: Ensure you are querying the correct database that contains the active transactional table for robot command lifecycle evidence.
steps.expected_result: The database containing RobotCommandDatabaseModel is opened/expanded in SSMS.
steps.healthy_condition: RobotCommandDatabaseModel is discoverable under the database’s table list.
steps.failure_condition: RobotCommandDatabaseModel is not found in the selected database.

actions.label: Select correct WCS/OptiSweep database
actions.exact_action: In the database list, open the OptiSweep/WCS database that contains the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table (robot command transactional tables).

steps.title: Locate RobotCommandDatabaseModel and identify lifecycle evidence fields
steps.instruction: Locate the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table and identify the columns/fields shown in the table UI for command lifecycle evidence, including sent time and in-progress time, plus command identifiers such as command name and robot/container/station parameters.
steps.purpose: Confirm the table columns/fields needed to determine sent → in-progress → archived lifecycle progression.
steps.expected_result: RobotCommandDatabaseModel is open and the lifecycle evidence fields (sent time and in-progress time) and identifiers (command name and robot/container/station parameters) are visible.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see sent time and in-progress time fields in the table view, along with command name/status and robot/container/station parameters.
steps.failure_condition: The table view does not show sent time and in-progress time fields, or required identifiers are not visible.

actions.label: Open RobotCommandDatabaseModel
actions.exact_action: Locate the RobotCommandDatabaseModel table and identify the columns/fields shown in the table UI for command lifecycle evidence, including sent time and in-progress time, plus command identifiers such as command name and robot/container/station parameters.

steps.title: Find the specific command instance by CommandName and robot/container/station identifiers
steps.instruction: Find the specific command instance by using the command name (e.g., MoveTote, PickupTote, DropOffTote, RemoveAgv, GoCharge) and the relevant robot/container/station identifiers that match the incident context.
steps.purpose: Target the correct row(s) representing the command instance tied to the incident context.
steps.expected_result: A matching row (or set of rows) for the targeted CommandName and robot/container/station identifiers is located in RobotCommandDatabaseModel.
steps.healthy_condition: The located row(s) correspond to the incident’s robot/container/station identifiers and show a sent time value.
steps.failure_condition: No matching command row can be found for the provided CommandName and robot/container/station identifiers.

actions.label: Locate command row(s)
actions.exact_action: Find the specific command instance by using the command name and the relevant robot/container/station identifiers that match the incident context.

steps.title: Verify lifecycle progression: sent time and in-progress time
steps.instruction: Observe the lifecycle timestamps/fields for the targeted row: confirm whether the row shows a sent time and whether it has transitioned to an in-progress state (in-progress time populated).
steps.purpose: Determine whether the command is still active and whether it has progressed from sent to in-progress.
steps.expected_result: For the targeted command row, sent time is populated; in-progress time is populated if the command has progressed to in-progress.
steps.healthy_condition: Sent time is populated; in-progress time is populated when the AGV is marked as in-progress for that command.
steps.failure_condition: Sent time is populated but in-progress time is not populated (command remains stuck in sent without in-progress transition).
stop_or_escalate_if: If the command remains in RobotCommandDatabaseModel without an in-progress transition (sent time populated but in-progress time not populated), escalate for deeper command/task state troubleshooting rather than assuming completion.

actions.label: Check sent vs in-progress timestamps
actions.exact_action: Observe the lifecycle timestamps/fields: confirm whether the row shows a sent time and whether it has transitioned to an in-progress state (in-progress time populated).

steps.title: Check destination/queue-capacity interaction evidence for in-progress commands
steps.instruction: If the command is in-progress, confirm queue/capacity interaction evidence by checking that the destination queue/location is reflected as freed/occupied based on in-progress status (e.g., in-progress indicates the AGV is occupying the queue/location capacity).
steps.purpose: Corroborate that in-progress status corresponds to active queue/location occupancy behavior.
steps.expected_result: The destination/current location fields associated with the in-progress command reflect active occupancy behavior consistent with queue capacity handling.
steps.healthy_condition: In-progress status aligns with queue/location occupancy freeing/occupying behavior described by the robot location model (max AGVs per queue/location).
steps.failure_condition: In-progress status does not align with expected occupancy/capacity evidence for the destination queue/location.

actions.label: Corroborate queue/location occupancy evidence
actions.exact_action: Confirm queue/capacity interaction evidence by checking that the destination queue/location is reflected as freed/occupied based on in-progress status.

steps.title: Verify completion: command archived out of RobotCommandDatabaseModel into robot command activity
steps.instruction: If the command is completed, verify it is no longer present as an active command in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and instead exists in the archived robot command activity (historical record).
steps.purpose: Confirm that completed commands are no longer present in the active transactional table and are available in the historical archive with a resolved status.
steps.expected_result: For the targeted command instance, RobotCommandDatabaseModel no longer contains the active row; the command appears in robot command activity archive with a status such as errored or cancelled.
steps.healthy_condition: Active table does not show the completed command; archived activity contains the command record with a resolved status (e.g., errored or cancelled).
steps.failure_condition: The command appears completed but is still present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel, or the command cannot be found in either active or archived records.
stop_or_escalate_if: If the command appears completed but is still present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel, escalate to investigate archiving behavior and transactional table consistency.
If you cannot locate the command by CommandName + robot/container/station identifiers, confirm the correct robot/container/station context and command naming used by the Robotics module.

actions.label: Check active vs archived presence
actions.exact_action: Verify it is no longer present as an active command in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and instead exists in the archived robot command activity (historical record).

title: Check Active Errors in the Robotics SystemActiveError Model
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Robotics Database SystemActiveErrorModel to determine whether system errors are currently active and capture the available identifying fields, including Name, Area, Error or area code, SystemErrorDescription, and Last Seen.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when troubleshooting a reported system or AGV-related condition and a read-only confirmation of currently active system errors is needed in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a recovery or resolution procedure.
Do not use the presence of an active row as evidence that the documented resolution has been completed.
Do not use this procedure to interpret historical errors as currently active; resolved system errors are archived to the SystemErrorActivityModel.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the Robotics Database. Use the database and table list to locate the Robotics database and its dbo.SystemActiveErrorModel table.
steps.purpose: Reach the Robotics database that contains the SystemActiveErrorModel.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics database is available in SSMS and dbo.SystemActiveErrorModel can be located in its table list.
steps.healthy_condition: The Robotics database and SystemActiveErrorModel are visible and accessible for read-only inspection.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics database or SystemActiveErrorModel cannot be located or accessed.
stop_or_escalate_if: The Robotics database is unavailable.
The SystemActiveErrorModel cannot be located or accessed.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

actions.label: Locate active-error model
actions.exact_action: Locate the SystemActiveErrorModel in the Robotics database table list.

steps.title: Inspect current SystemActiveErrorModel rows
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), open dbo.SystemActiveErrorModel and inspect the current rows. Review the Name, Area, Error or area code, Last Seen, and SystemErrorDescription fields.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the reported condition is represented by a currently active system-error row.
steps.expected_result: The model displays zero or more current active-error rows with observable identifying fields and displayed Last Seen information.
steps.healthy_condition: The model can be inspected and each relevant row has sufficient identifying information to compare with the reported condition.
steps.failure_condition: The active state cannot be confirmed, a relevant row is missing identifying fields, or the model cannot be inspected.
stop_or_escalate_if: The SystemActiveErrorModel cannot be opened.
The displayed active state cannot be confirmed.
A relevant row lacks Name, Area, Error or area code, SystemErrorDescription, or Last Seen information.

actions.label: Open active-error model
actions.exact_action: Open the SystemActiveErrorModel and inspect the current rows.

actions.label: Review identifying fields
actions.exact_action: Inspect Name, Area, Error or area code, SystemErrorDescription, and Last Seen.

steps.title: Capture details for relevant active rows
steps.instruction: For each relevant row in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), capture the Name, Area, Error or area code, SystemErrorDescription, and Last Seen value. Compare examples such as AGV has not moved in 30 seconds or Communication Error with the reported condition.
steps.purpose: Create an identifiable record of the active error or confirm that no current active row is present.
steps.expected_result: Each relevant active row has a captured name, area, error or area code, description, and Last Seen value, or the model shows no current active row.
steps.healthy_condition: The captured row details clearly identify the error and its current displayed Last Seen information.
steps.failure_condition: No active row corresponds to the reported condition, the row fields are incomplete, or the displayed information is insufficient to confirm active state.
stop_or_escalate_if: The reported fault is not represented in the active-error model.
No current active row is present when one is expected.
The displayed fields are incomplete.
The active state cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Capture active-error fields
actions.exact_action: Record the Name, Area, error or area code, SystemErrorDescription, and Last Seen value for each relevant row.

actions.label: Compare reported condition
actions.exact_action: Compare the observed error row with the reported condition.

steps.title: Stop when the active-error check is inconclusive
steps.instruction: Stop the diagnostic and escalate to L3_support when no matching active row is present, a relevant row lacks identifying fields, or the active state cannot be confirmed. Do not treat an active row as evidence that the documented resolution has been completed.
steps.purpose: Prevent an incomplete or missing database row from being treated as confirmation of the reported condition or its resolution.
steps.expected_result: The result is classified as either a confirmed observable active-error match, no current active row, or an inconclusive check requiring escalation.
steps.healthy_condition: The diagnostic outcome explicitly distinguishes current active-error evidence from the absence of a row or an inconclusive result.
steps.failure_condition: An incomplete, missing, or active row is incorrectly treated as proof of fault resolution or as a complete diagnosis.
stop_or_escalate_if: No active row is present for an expected fault.
The reported fault is not represented in the active-error model.
A row lacks the identifying fields needed for comparison.
The active state cannot be confirmed.

actions.label: Classify diagnostic result
actions.exact_action: Stop if no active row is present or the displayed fields are incomplete.

actions.label: Escalate inconclusive result
actions.exact_action: Escalate when the reported fault is not represented in the active-error model or the active state cannot be confirmed.

title: Verify Resolved Errors in the Robotics SystemErrorActivityModel
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the Robotics Database to verify that a resolved active error appears as archived activity in the SystemErrorActivityModel. Inspect the SystemErrorDescription, SystemErrorResolution, Start Time, Finish Time, and duration fields.
when_to_use: Use this read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when an active error is reported as resolved and support must verify that the error was archived in the Robotics Database SystemErrorActivityModel with recorded timing and resolution details.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to infer resolution success solely from the presence of a SystemErrorResolution value.
Do not use this procedure as a recovery or error-clearing procedure; it only verifies archived error activity.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the Robotics Database and open the database view used to inspect the SystemErrorActivityModel.
steps.purpose: Access the Robotics Database where the SystemErrorActivityModel archived-error records are stored.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics Database is selected and the SystemErrorActivityModel is available for inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS is connected to the Robotics Database and the SystemErrorActivityModel can be opened.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics Database or SystemErrorActivityModel is unavailable for inspection.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Robotics Database or SystemErrorActivityModel cannot be accessed.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

steps.title: Locate the archived error record
steps.instruction: In the Robotics Database SystemErrorActivityModel on WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), locate the record using the error name or SystemErrorDescription.
steps.purpose: Find the archived activity record corresponding to the error reported as resolved.
steps.expected_result: A SystemErrorActivityModel row corresponding to the reported error is located.
steps.healthy_condition: The matching archived row is identifiable by its error name or SystemErrorDescription.
steps.failure_condition: No corresponding archived SystemErrorActivityModel row can be located.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if an error reported as resolved has no corresponding archived SystemErrorActivityModel record.

actions.label: Locate archived error
actions.exact_action: Open the SystemErrorActivityModel and locate the error record by its error name or SystemErrorDescription.

steps.title: Inspect the archived error fields
steps.instruction: On the matching SystemErrorActivityModel row in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect SystemErrorDescription, SystemErrorResolution, Start Time, Finish Time, and duration.
steps.purpose: Verify that the archived record contains the error description, recorded resolution, and timing information needed for diagnostic confirmation.
steps.expected_result: The matching row displays values for SystemErrorDescription, SystemErrorResolution, Start Time, Finish Time, and duration.
steps.healthy_condition: The archived row contains the expected description and resolution details, with populated Start Time, Finish Time, and duration fields.
steps.failure_condition: One or more expected fields are empty, especially Finish Time or duration.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if Finish Time or duration is empty.
Do not treat a populated SystemErrorResolution alone as proof that the error was resolved.

actions.label: Inspect archived fields
actions.exact_action: Check the SystemErrorDescription, SystemErrorResolution, Start Time, Finish Time, and duration values for the record.

steps.title: Confirm completed archived timing
steps.instruction: In the SystemErrorActivityModel on WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), verify that the matching resolved error has both a Finish Time and a recorded duration in addition to its Start Time.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the resolved error is represented as completed archived activity rather than only as an active-state record.
steps.expected_result: The resolved error has a populated Finish Time and duration in the SystemErrorActivityModel.
steps.healthy_condition: The archived record contains Start Time, Finish Time, and duration, along with the SystemErrorDescription and SystemErrorResolution.
steps.failure_condition: The record is absent, remains represented only as active-state information, or has an empty Finish Time or duration.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when an error reported as resolved has no archived SystemErrorActivityModel record.
Escalate when the archived record lacks Finish Time or duration evidence.

actions.label: Confirm archived completion
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the resolved error has a Finish Time and duration rather than only an active-state record.

title: Look Up System Error Definitions in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS against the WCS / Helix Robotics Database to match a reported system error to its Error, Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution values.
when_to_use: Use this read-only SSMS diagnostic when a named system error must be interpreted using the Robotics Database SystemErrorDefinition table. Use the returned Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution values to support troubleshooting and escalation.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to execute the SystemErrorResolution value.
Do not use this procedure to perform mutating database actions or equipment actions.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for checking current active errors in the SystemActiveError model.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface, open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.
steps.purpose: Establish a read-only connection to the database that contains the system error definitions.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics Database is selected in SSMS and the SystemErrorDefinition table is available for inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS displays the Robotics Database and exposes the SystemErrorDefinition table.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics Database or SystemErrorDefinition table cannot be accessed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Robotics Database or the SystemErrorDefinition table is unavailable.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

steps.title: Open the SystemErrorDefinition table
steps.instruction: In SSMS, open the SystemErrorDefinition table and inspect the displayed Error, Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution columns.
steps.purpose: Locate the table and fields needed to interpret the reported system error.
steps.expected_result: The SystemErrorDefinition table displays the reported error entry or confirms that no matching entry is present.
steps.healthy_condition: The table is readable and the Error, Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution fields are available for the lookup.
steps.failure_condition: The table cannot be opened, the reported Error entry is absent, or the required definition columns are unavailable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the lookup if the reported error is not present.
Escalate if the SystemErrorDefinition table cannot be read.

actions.label: Open definition table
actions.exact_action: Open the SystemErrorDefinition table and locate the relevant Error entry.

steps.title: Inspect the error definition values
steps.instruction: In the SSMS SystemErrorDefinition row, inspect and preserve the Error, Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution values. Examples shown in the table include AgvHasNotMoved30Seconds / AGV / AGV has not moved in 30 seconds / Reboot AGV and AgvOutOfSequence / AGV / AGV is out of sequence / Remove AGV.
steps.purpose: Capture the documented classification, description, and resolution information associated with the reported system error.
steps.expected_result: The matching row provides a non-empty Error name with corresponding Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution values.
steps.healthy_condition: The row contains a consistent Error, Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution value that can be reported for troubleshooting.
steps.failure_condition: One or more required definition fields are empty, unreadable, or inconsistent with the reported Error.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop the lookup if any required definition field is empty.
Escalate if the definition values are inconsistent.

actions.label: Read definition fields
actions.exact_action: Check the corresponding Area, SystemErrorDescription, and SystemErrorResolution values.

steps.title: Preserve unmatched or incomplete lookup results
steps.instruction: If the reported Error is not present or any required definition field is empty or inconsistent in SSMS, stop the lookup and preserve the observed error name together with the missing or inconsistent field information for escalation.
steps.purpose: Provide an accurate escalation record when the Robotics Database does not contain a usable definition.
steps.expected_result: The escalation record identifies the observed error name and states whether the row was absent or which definition field was missing or inconsistent.
steps.healthy_condition: A complete, consistent definition row is available and no escalation is required for the lookup itself.
steps.failure_condition: No matching SystemErrorDefinition row exists, or the row lacks a usable Area, SystemErrorDescription, or SystemErrorResolution value.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when the reported error has no matching SystemErrorDefinition row.
Escalate when definition fields are missing or inconsistent.
Do not perform a database or equipment action based only on the SystemErrorResolution value.

actions.label: Preserve lookup gap
actions.exact_action: Preserve the observed error name for escalation.

title: Check Sorter-Side Charger Assignment in SSMS / Helix DB
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) to inspect sorter-side and charger-assignment records. Confirm that the charger has a sorter-side model ID, that the charger is associated with the expected charging area or sorter side, and that its availability or disabled status is consistent with the investigation.
when_to_use: Use this read-only diagnostic when investigating whether a charger is assigned to the expected sorter side, whether the assignment is present, or whether charger availability or disabled status may explain charging behavior. Perform the inspection in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change sorter-side assignments, charging-area mappings, charger availability, or disabled status.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for confirming an exact live table or column name; the supplied source does not provide the complete SSMS navigation path or schema.

steps.title: Open the WCS / Helix DB records in SSMS
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), locate the sorter-side database model and the charging database model or charging-location records for the charger under investigation. Use the live model or record names available in the environment; the supplied source does not specify an exact database name, table name, or navigation path.
steps.purpose: Locate the live database records needed to inspect the charger and its sorter-side association.
steps.expected_result: The relevant sorter-side and charger-related records are available for read-only inspection in SSMS.
steps.healthy_condition: The records can be opened and provide an identifiable charger or charging location together with sorter-side or charging-area association data.
steps.failure_condition: The required records cannot be located, the charger cannot be identified, or the available schema does not expose the association needed for the check.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3 support or engineering if the live schema cannot be identified or the required charger-assignment records are unavailable.

actions.label: Locate live database models
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and locate the sorter-side database model or charger-assignment records.

steps.title: Inspect the charger and sorter-side model ID
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), find the investigated charger or charging location. Inspect the sorter-side identifier or model ID associated with it, along with the charging area, charger location or station, tote stand association, and any available or disabled status shown in the live records.
steps.purpose: Determine which sorter-side identifier is associated with the charger and inspect related charging configuration.
steps.expected_result: The charger record shows a sorter-side identifier or model ID and identifies its related charging-area or charger configuration.
steps.healthy_condition: A sorter-side identifier is present, the charger is associated with a charging area or location, and the record exposes an interpretable availability or disabled status.
steps.failure_condition: The sorter-side identifier is missing, the charger has no charging-area association, or the charger status is unavailable or disabled when the investigation expects it to be usable.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the sorter-side identifier or model ID is missing.
Escalate if the charger has no identifiable charging-area or location association.
Do not edit the record when the charger is disabled or unavailable.

actions.label: Inspect charger assignment
actions.exact_action: Find the charger or charging location being investigated and inspect its sorter-side ID or model ID.

actions.label: Inspect charger status
actions.exact_action: Inspect the associated charging area, charger location, tote stand, and whether the charger or charging area is disabled.

steps.title: Compare the assignment with the expected charging relationship
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the recorded sorter-side model ID and charger status with the expected sorter side for the charger. Confirm whether the charger is assigned to the expected side for normal charging. If the records describe cross-side use, identify whether another side's charger is available for emergency charging without changing the configuration.
steps.purpose: Decide whether the configured charger assignment supports the expected normal or emergency charging relationship.
steps.expected_result: The recorded assignment either maps the charger to the expected sorter side for normal charging or clearly identifies a configured cross-side available charger relationship for emergency use.
steps.healthy_condition: The sorter-side identifier matches the expected side, the charger is not marked disabled for the intended use, and any emergency cross-side relationship is distinguishable from the normal assignment.
steps.failure_condition: The identifier maps to the wrong sorter side, the assignment is absent, the charger is disabled or unavailable contrary to the expected use, or the records conflict about the normal versus emergency relationship.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/engineering if the sorter-side identifier is missing or maps to the wrong side.
Escalate if the assignment conflicts with the charger's charging-area or disabled status.

steps.purpose: Relate the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) observations to the reported AI1, default-dimension, or tote-overflow condition.

actions.exact_action: Compare the recent SortConf records with the reported AI1 data loss, default dimensions, or tote overflow.

steps.purpose: Determine whether the tag activity is represented consistently with the associated departure and recorded fault information.
steps.expected_result: The tag path and value can be associated with the relevant departure record, or the record shows that the event cannot be correlated.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant departure record and Tag Read/Tag Write entries are present and their Task Name, ToteId, TagPath, Value, and available fault information can be correlated.
steps.failure_condition: The TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the departure event, the departure record is missing, or the record contains fault information requiring escalation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the TagPath and Value cannot be correlated with the tipper event.
Do not infer a fault-code meaning or corrective action when the database record only provides the recorded value.

actions.label: Compare departure and tag entries
actions.exact_action: Compare the recorded tag path and value with the associated departure and fault-code information to determine whether the event is represented in the logs.

title: Check Tipper Model Station, Printer, and Tipper Status Fields
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only surface to inspect the Sorter Sweeper Database Tipper model for the relevant operator station. Verify the Tipper ID and station association, Printer Name and printer IP when configured, Location ID, and Tipper Status.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to verify the live tipper configuration used by the system, including the station-to-tipper association, printer configuration, location association, or current Tipper Status in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
not_for: Changing printer, location, station, or tipper-status configuration.
Operating or recovering a tipper through the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU.
Replacing a live equipment fault investigation with configuration inspection alone.

steps.title: Open the Tipper model in the Sorter Sweeper Database
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), use the read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper model records for the relevant operator station.
steps.purpose: Access the live configuration record for the operator station being investigated.
steps.expected_result: The relevant Tipper model record or records are available for inspection in the Sorter Sweeper Database.
steps.healthy_condition: A Tipper model record is present for the identified station.
steps.failure_condition: The relevant Tipper model record cannot be located or is missing.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the relevant Tipper model record is missing.

actions.label: Locate Tipper model records
actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper model records for the relevant operator station.

steps.title: Verify Tipper ID and station association
steps.instruction: In the live Tipper model record in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the Tipper ID and station association. Confirm the documented left/right representation used for the station.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the Tipper model identifies the expected tipper and its operator-station relationship.
steps.expected_result: The record identifies a Tipper ID associated with the relevant operator station and shows the applicable left/right representation.
steps.healthy_condition: The Tipper ID and station association are present and consistent with the identified operator station.
steps.failure_condition: The Tipper ID is absent, the station association is inconsistent, or the left/right representation cannot be reconciled with the station.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the station or Tipper ID association is inconsistent.

actions.label: Check station-to-tipper mapping
actions.exact_action: Check the Tipper ID and station association, including the documented left/right representation used for the station.

steps.title: Check printer name and printer IP
steps.instruction: In the live Tipper model record in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect Printer Name and the associated printer IP. Perform this check when a printer is configured for the tipper.
steps.purpose: Verify the printer information associated with the tipper when label printing is configured.
steps.expected_result: The Tipper model shows the configured Printer Name and associated printer IP when printer configuration is applicable.
steps.healthy_condition: Printer Name and printer IP are present when the tipper is expected to use a configured printer.
steps.failure_condition: Printer information is absent when a printer is required, or the displayed printer information does not match the expected tipper configuration.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if printer information is absent when required.

actions.label: Check printer configuration
actions.exact_action: Check the Printer Name and associated printer IP used for label directives, when a printer is configured for the tipper.

steps.title: Verify the Location ID
steps.instruction: In the live Tipper model record in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the Location ID and compare it with the expected location for the relevant operator station.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the tipper is associated with the expected station location.
steps.expected_result: The Tipper model contains a Location ID that can be compared with the expected station location.
steps.healthy_condition: The Location ID is present and matches the expected station location.
steps.failure_condition: The Location ID is absent or does not match the expected station location.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the location association is inconsistent.

actions.label: Check tipper location
actions.exact_action: Check the Location ID associated with the tipper and compare it with the expected station location.

steps.title: Inspect Tipper Status
steps.instruction: In the live Tipper model record in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect Tipper Status and record whether the value is Ready, Not Ready, or Disabled.
steps.purpose: Determine the current observable status of the tipper configuration record.
steps.expected_result: The Tipper Status field displays one of the documented values: Ready, Not Ready, or Disabled.
steps.healthy_condition: Tipper Status is Ready.
steps.failure_condition: Tipper Status is Not Ready or Disabled, or the field does not contain an observable documented status value.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if Tipper Status is Not Ready or Disabled.

actions.label: Check Tipper Status
actions.exact_action: Inspect Tipper Status and record whether the value is Ready, Not Ready, or Disabled.

title: Validate Sorter Location Records and Lane Status in SSMS
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) in read-only mode to inspect the SorterSweeper Location Model, verify station and location mappings, and interpret LaneStatus for a selected sorter, tipper, hospital, or induction location.
when_to_use: Use this read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when support must validate a SorterSweeper location record, station or cell-code mapping, location category, lane status, or related KeepClose and TipperSelect configuration.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database rows or configuration values.
Do not use this procedure as a physical sorter, AGV, hospital, or tipper recovery procedure.
Do not treat a nullable LoadCategory or AGV-related field as a fault solely because its value is NULL.
Do not use this procedure to infer an undocumented LaneStatus value or an unverified station mapping.

steps.title: Open the SorterSweeper database in SSMS
steps.instruction: In WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the WCS / Helix SorterSweeper database and open the Location Model or its corresponding location records using read-only access.
steps.purpose: Access the live WCS / Helix DB surface that stores the SorterSweeper location records.
steps.expected_result: The SorterSweeper location records are available for inspection in SSMS.
steps.healthy_condition: The expected SorterSweeper database and location records are accessible without making changes.
steps.failure_condition: The database or location records are unavailable, access is not read-only, or the expected Location Model cannot be identified.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the expected SorterSweeper database or Location Model is missing.
Stop if the available access does not provide a read-only inspection path.

actions.label: Select SorterSweeper database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the WCS / Helix SorterSweeper database.

actions.label: Open location records
actions.exact_action: Open the Location Model or its corresponding location records.

steps.title: Inspect the location record fields
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Location Model records, inspect Location, Station, SorterName, LocationCellCode, Zone, Sequence, Lane, LoadCategory, LaneDelay, LaneStatus, LocationType, KeepClose, and TipperSelect.
steps.purpose: Confirm that the selected location record contains the fields needed to validate its station, lane, and control mapping.
steps.expected_result: The selected location row is present and its available fields can be read, including its station, cell code, lane, location type, and lane status.
steps.healthy_condition: The row contains the expected location identity and the relevant fields are populated or explicitly NULL where the source indicates a nullable value.
steps.failure_condition: The expected row is missing, required mapping fields do not identify the location, or a value is present that cannot be interpreted from the documented fields.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the expected location row is missing.
Do not change a value because it appears NULL; verify whether the field is documented as nullable.

actions.label: Review location attributes
actions.exact_action: Inspect Location, Station, SorterName, LocationCellCode, Zone, Sequence, Lane, LoadCategory, LaneDelay, LaneStatus, LocationType, KeepClose, and TipperSelect.

steps.title: Validate the location type
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) location record, inspect LocationType and compare it with the documented categories: Sorter, Tipper, Hospital, or Induction.
steps.purpose: Determine which documented station category the selected location represents.
steps.expected_result: LocationType identifies the selected location as Sorter, Tipper, Hospital, or Induction.
steps.healthy_condition: The LocationType value matches the intended station category; an Induction location represents the specified tote induction location at the hospital, and a Hospital location represents the specified tote drop-off location.
steps.failure_condition: LocationType is missing, contains an undocumented value, or does not match the intended station category.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LocationType is undocumented or does not match the station mapping.

actions.label: Check LocationType
actions.exact_action: Confirm that LocationType identifies Sorter, Tipper, Hospital, or Induction.

steps.title: Compare LocationCellCode with the station mapping
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the selected location's LocationCellCode and Station with the associated station mapping. For an Induction or Hospital location, verify whether the AGV-reported cell code is the same cell code as the location used for the hospital-controller presence notification.
steps.purpose: Verify that the location's cell-code identity corresponds to the intended station and supports the documented presence-notification behavior.
steps.expected_result: The selected LocationCellCode corresponds to the intended Station; for an Induction or Hospital location, the mapping identifies the cell code used for the documented hospital-controller notification behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: LocationCellCode and Station agree with the associated mapping and the location category.
steps.failure_condition: LocationCellCode does not match the station mapping, the mapping is missing, or the location category is inconsistent with the expected notification relationship.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LocationCellCode does not match the station mapping.
Escalate if an Induction or Hospital location cannot be associated with the expected cell-code relationship.

actions.label: Compare cell code and station
actions.exact_action: Compare LocationCellCode with the associated station mapping.

steps.title: Interpret LaneStatus
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) location record, inspect LaneStatus and record whether it is Active, Bypassed, or Not tracking.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the selected lane or location is open, closed, or excluded from use according to the live database state.
steps.expected_result: LaneStatus displays one of the documented values and support records the corresponding operational interpretation.
steps.healthy_condition: Active indicates the lane is open for use; Bypassed indicates the lane is closed; Not tracking indicates the location is excluded from use until it becomes Active or Bypassed.
steps.failure_condition: LaneStatus contains an undocumented value, or the location remains Not tracking when it is expected to participate in sorter operation.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if LaneStatus contains an undocumented value.
Escalate if the location remains Not tracking when it is expected to participate in sorter operation.
Do not change LaneStatus or other database values as part of this diagnostic.

actions.label: Read lane status
actions.exact_action: Inspect LaneStatus and record whether the location is Active, Bypassed, or Not tracking.

steps.title: Review KeepClose and TipperSelect when applicable
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) location record, inspect KeepClose and TipperSelect when those configuration values are relevant to the location. Preserve source-supported NULL values for nullable fields, including applicable load-category or AGV-related values, rather than treating every NULL as an error.
steps.purpose: Check location-specific closeout and tipper-selection configuration without misclassifying supported NULL values.
steps.expected_result: KeepClose and TipperSelect are recorded when applicable, and nullable fields are distinguished from mapping or status faults.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed KeepClose and TipperSelect values are consistent with the location's documented use, while supported NULL values remain unchanged and are not automatically classified as faults.
steps.failure_condition: A relevant KeepClose or TipperSelect value conflicts with the expected location use, or a value is treated as an error solely because it is NULL.
stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if a relevant KeepClose or TipperSelect value conflicts with the expected location mapping.
Do not modify configuration values.
Do not escalate a nullable field solely because its value is NULL.

actions.label: Check location configuration
actions.exact_action: Check KeepClose and TipperSelect for the location when those configuration values are relevant.

title: Use OptiSweep/WCS API actions to reopen all chutes and cancel closeout exchanges
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) to (1) reopen any previously closed shoots/chutes and (2) cancel closeout exchanges that are not currently in progress. This is intended for recovery after a customer manual bag-out/closeout where the sort was not cycled.
when_to_use: When a customer did a manual bag out/closeout and the system needs to start up again without cycling the sort.

steps.title: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API)
steps.instruction: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) and navigate to the System actions list.
steps.purpose: Access the System actions needed to reopen chutes and cancel closeout exchanges.
steps.expected_result: The API client shows the available System actions, including the action named "Open All Chutes".
steps.healthy_condition: The System actions list is visible and "Open All Chutes" is selectable.
steps.failure_condition: The System actions list is not accessible or "Open All Chutes" is not available to select.

actions.label: Open API client and view System actions
actions.exact_action: Open the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API).

steps.title: Execute "Open All Chutes"
steps.instruction: Select the System action named "Open All Chutes" and execute it.
steps.purpose: Reopen any previously closed shoots/chutes so the system can resume after manual bag-out/closeout.
steps.expected_result: The "Open All Chutes" call completes successfully and returns a successful API response/status (no error).
steps.healthy_condition: API response/status indicates success for the "Open All Chutes" request.
steps.failure_condition: API response/status indicates an error or the call does not complete successfully.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the "Open All Chutes" API call returns an error or does not complete successfully.

actions.label: Run Open All Chutes
actions.exact_action: Select the System action named "Open All Chutes" and execute it.

steps.title: Verify "Open All Chutes" success via API response/status
steps.instruction: Check the API response/status returned by the "Open All Chutes" call and confirm it indicates success (no error).
steps.purpose: Confirm the system-level chute reopening request succeeded before making any further changes.
steps.expected_result: "Open All Chutes" shows a successful API response/status.
steps.healthy_condition: The response/status panel for the executed call indicates success.
steps.failure_condition: The response/status indicates failure (error) or the call did not succeed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the "Open All Chutes" response/status indicates an error or unsuccessful completion.

actions.label: Inspect API response/status
actions.exact_action: Verify the action completed successfully by checking the API response/status returned by the call (e.g., request succeeded / no error).

steps.title: Execute "Cancel Close Out" (only if closeout exchanges are not in progress)
steps.instruction: If there are closeout exchanges that are not in progress, select the System action named "Cancel Close Out" and execute it.
steps.purpose: Cancel closeout exchanges that are not currently in progress so the system can resume without cycling the sort.
steps.expected_result: The "Cancel Close Out" call completes successfully and returns a successful API response/status (no error).
steps.healthy_condition: API response/status indicates success for the "Cancel Close Out" request.
steps.failure_condition: API response/status indicates an error or the call does not complete successfully.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the "Cancel Close Out" API call returns an error or does not complete successfully.

actions.label: Run Cancel Close Out
actions.exact_action: Select the System action named "Cancel Close Out" and execute it.

steps.title: Verify "Cancel Close Out" success via API response/status
steps.instruction: Check the API response/status returned by the "Cancel Close Out" call and confirm it indicates success (no error).
steps.purpose: Confirm closeout cancellation succeeded before ending the procedure.
steps.expected_result: "Cancel Close Out" shows a successful API response/status.
steps.healthy_condition: The response/status panel for the executed call indicates success.
steps.failure_condition: The response/status indicates failure (error) or the call did not succeed.
stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the "Cancel Close Out" response/status indicates an error or unsuccessful completion.

actions.label: Inspect API response/status
actions.exact_action: Verify the "Cancel Close Out" call completed successfully via the API response/status.

steps.title: Stop after both API calls succeed; do not perform additional system state changes
steps.instruction: Once both API calls have returned successful responses, stop the procedure and do not attempt additional system state changes in this procedure.
steps.purpose: Limit changes to only the two documented system actions for this recovery scenario.
steps.expected_result: Procedure ends after successful completion of the executed actions.
steps.healthy_condition: No further system actions are executed beyond "Open All Chutes" and (if applicable) "Cancel Close Out".
steps.failure_condition: Additional system state changes are attempted after successful responses.

actions.label: Confirm completion and stop
actions.exact_action: Stop the procedure once both API calls have returned successful responses; do not attempt additional system state changes in this procedure.

title: Verify OptiSweep/WCS Windows service health when RMS/logs appear silent
summary: When the system appears to have a crash/restart period and logs may be silent, verify whether the relevant OptiSweep/WCS Windows service(s) are actually Running vs Stopped in the Windows Services MMC. Use the service state as the primary observable when log activity is missing.
when_to_use: Use when RMS and/or other log-based signals appear silent during a suspected OptiSweep/WCS crash/restart window, and you need host-level evidence that the service is Running vs Stopped.

steps.title: Open Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host
steps.instruction: On the OptiSweep/WCS host, open the Windows Services MMC / Windows Services view (the Services list).
steps.purpose: Establish the host-level view needed to determine whether the OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Running vs Stopped when logs may be silent.
steps.expected_result: The Services list is visible with a Status column that can show Running vs Stopped for services.
steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly see the Services list and the Status values (Running/Stopped) for services.
steps.failure_condition: The Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, or you cannot access the Services MMC on the host.
stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot access the Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host

actions.label: Open Services MMC
actions.exact_action: Open the Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host.

steps.title: Locate OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check Running vs Stopped
steps.instruction: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) (the segment notes there are about 10 services) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.
steps.purpose: Determine whether the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Running or Stopped during the suspected silent/crash window.
steps.expected_result: You identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and observe their Status as Running or Stopped.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running during normal operation.
steps.failure_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped, or you observe restart behavior consistent with the suspected crash/restart period.
stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list
The Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status

actions.label: Find relevant services and read Status
actions.exact_action: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.

steps.title: Interpret Stopped/restarting service state as evidence consistent with the silent crash window
steps.instruction: If the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Stopped (or show restart behavior), treat that as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period during the suspected crash window.
steps.purpose: Use the service state as the observable indicator when logs are silent, matching the segment’s described behavior during crash periods.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion matches the observed Status: Stopped/restarting supports the suspected crash/restart period; Running supports normal operation.
steps.healthy_condition: During normal operation, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Running.
steps.failure_condition: During the suspected crash window, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Stopped or restarting.
stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component

actions.label: Confirm evidence from service state
actions.exact_action: If the service is Stopped (or repeatedly restarting), treat this as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period.

steps.title: Stop and escalate when service identification/status is unclear
steps.instruction: If you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list, or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, stop and escalate.
steps.purpose: Ensure you do not proceed with an unsupported conclusion when the relevant service(s) cannot be identified or the status evidence is not clear.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated with the evidence that the relevant service(s) could not be identified or status was unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service(s) are identifiable and show clear Running/Stopped status.
steps.failure_condition: Service identification is ambiguous or the Services view does not provide clear Running/Stopped status.
stop_or_escalate_if: Cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) among the ~10 services
Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.
